sec07-card-sec07-F05.front: What are pavement markings made of, and what traffic flows do yellow centerlines divide?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.expected_back: Pavement markings are lines, words or figures placed on the pavement with paint, reflectors or other markers, and yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.front: What kind of road carries a single broken yellow centerline, where do you drive, and when may you cross?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.expected_back: A single broken yellow centerline marks a road with only two lanes of traffic, you drive to its right, and you may cross it to pass another vehicle when it is safe.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.front: What passing rule do double solid yellow lines set, and for what lone maneuver may you cross them?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.expected_back: Double solid yellow lines mark the center of a road where passing is prohibited in both directions, and you may cross them only to turn left into or out of an alley, private road or driveway.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.front: What does a single solid yellow no-passing line on a two-lane road forbid, and when may you cross it?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.expected_back: A no passing line is a single solid yellow line on a two-lane road marking a zone where passing is prohibited, and like the double yellow line it may be crossed only to turn left into or out of an alley, private road or driveway.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.front: How does crossing a broken yellow centerline differ from crossing a solid yellow no-passing stripe?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.expected_back: A broken yellow centerline may be crossed to pass when safe, while a solid yellow no passing line may be crossed only for a left turn into or out of an alley, private road or driveway.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.front: What directional clue separates yellow lane lines from white lane lines?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.expected_back: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions, while white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.front: What traffic do white lane lines divide, and how must you position your car relative to them?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.expected_back: White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction, and you are required to drive between them.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.front: When are you allowed to move across a single dashed white lane line?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.expected_back: A single dashed white lane line may be crossed whenever you can do so safely.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.front: What does a single solid white line warn—especially when painted wider—and when may you cross it?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.expected_back: A single solid white line warns that changing lanes there is hazardous, a wider line signals a greater hazard, and such a line may be crossed only in unusual circumstances and only with great care.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.front: What rule does a double solid white lane line set for changing lanes?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.expected_back: A double solid white line means that moving from lane to lane is prohibited, and you must not cross it.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.front: How does crossing a single solid white line compare with a double solid white line?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.expected_back: A single solid white line may be crossed only in unusual circumstances with great care, while a double solid white line may never be crossed.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.front: What are solid yellow or white obstruction markings painted in traffic lanes designed to do?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.expected_back: Obstruction markings are solid lines in the traffic lanes, yellow or white, that steer you around an obstruction in the road such as a bridge support.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.front: On which side may you pass white obstruction markings versus yellow obstruction markings?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.expected_back: White obstruction markings may be passed on either side, but yellow obstruction markings must be kept on your left, so you pass them on the right only.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.front: What rule applies when white directional arrows or words appear in your lane, including multi-direction arrows?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.expected_back: Directional markings are white arrows or words painted in the lane to show the direction you must take, you must move only as the arrow indicates, and where arrows show more than one direction you may choose any of them.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.front: How does color change which side you take around painted obstruction lines?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.expected_back: White obstruction markings may be passed on either side, while yellow obstruction markings must be passed on the right only.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.front: How does a lane painted with one directional arrow differ from a lane painted with a multi-direction arrow?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.expected_back: A single directional arrow commands one movement only, while a lane with arrows for more than one direction lets you choose any of those directions.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.front: How is a two-way left-turn center lane striped, who may enter it, and what maneuver is banned inside it?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.expected_back: Two-way left turn channelization markings combine solid and dashed yellow lines to mark a center lane that vehicles traveling in either direction may use only for left turns, and the lane must never be used for passing.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.front: What does a solid white line painted across traffic lanes at an intersection or crosswalk indicate?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.expected_back: A stop line is a solid white line running across the lanes at an intersection or pedestrian crosswalk, and it shows exactly where to stop.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.front: What dual message do crosswalk lines send to walkers and drivers, and what must drivers do?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.expected_back: Crosswalk lines show pedestrians where to cross safely and warn drivers that pedestrians may be crossing at that spot, and you must stop for pedestrians in crosswalks.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.front: How does a striped two-way center left-turn lane differ from plain double solid yellow centerlines?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.expected_back: The two-way left turn lane is open to vehicles from both directions for left turns only, while double solid yellow lines without such a lane allow crossing only for a left turn into a driveway or alley.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.front: How does the role of a transverse white stop line differ from adjacent crosswalk lines?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.expected_back: A stop line marks the exact stopping place at an intersection or crosswalk, while crosswalk lines mark where pedestrians cross and oblige drivers to stop for them.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.front: Which three painted elements make up standard railroad crossing pavement markings?
sec07-card-sec07-F21.expected_back: Railroad crossing markings are white markings in the traffic lane before a crossing, consisting of a large X with two R letters, a solid yellow centerline running the whole distance to prevent passing, and a white stop line across the lane.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.front: How can traffic islands be built, and what job do they perform on the roadway?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.expected_back: Traffic islands come in many designs, from painted markings alone to combinations of curbing, paving or landscaping, and they are used to direct you into separate traffic lanes.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.front: When is a traffic island called a safety island, and what driving rule applies to every traffic island?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.expected_back: A traffic island is called a safety island when it protects pedestrians who may have to stand in the roadway, and you should never drive into or across a traffic island.

sec07-card-sec07-R11.front: What distinguishes a general traffic island from a safety island, and what rule covers both?
sec07-card-sec07-R11.expected_back: A traffic island directs vehicles into separate lanes, while a safety island is a traffic island that shelters pedestrians, and neither may be driven into or across.

sec07-card-sec07-R09.front: How do white railroad-approach pavement markings contrast with red pavement markings?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.expected_back: Railroad crossing pavement markings are white with a yellow no-passing centerline, while red pavement markings mean a roadway must not be entered at all.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.front: Which four physical installations control traffic flow, and into what three functional categories do they fall?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.expected_back: Traffic flow is controlled by pavement markings, traffic islands, signals and signs, and these devices fall into three categories, regulatory devices, warning devices, and guide and information signs.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.front: What kinds of actions do regulatory devices demand, and what follows if you disobey one?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.expected_back: Regulatory devices tell you to stop, to go a certain direction or to limit your speed, every regulatory device demands an action from you, and failing to comply is subject to penalty.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.front: What do warning devices alert you to, and what risk comes from shrugging one off?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.expected_back: Warning devices advise you of hazardous conditions or the possibility of them, and ignoring a warning device can lead to a crash caused by your own negligence.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.front: How do guide and information signs help you during a drive?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.expected_back: Guide and information signs help you find your way safely or give information that makes the trip more comfortable.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.front: What message do red pavement paint or red roadway reflectors deliver?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.expected_back: Red pavement markings or red reflectors mark a roadway that must not be entered or used.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.front: Where do solid white edge lines run compared with solid yellow edge lines?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.expected_back: Edge lines are solid white or yellow lines along the edge of the roadway used as a safety guide, with white along the right edge and yellow allowed along the left edge of divided streets and highways.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.front: On a divided highway at night or in rain, how do white and yellow edge stripes orient your lane?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.expected_back: White edge lines run along the right edge of the roadway, while yellow edge lines may run along the left edge of a divided highway.

sec07-card-sec07-R10.front: How does disobeying a regulatory device differ in consequence from ignoring a warning device?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.expected_back: A regulatory device requires an action and carries a penalty for non-compliance, while a warning device advises of a hazard and ignoring it risks a crash through negligence.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.front: Which seating positions require seat-belt use under Hawaii law?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.expected_back: Safety belts keep you from being injured and can save your life, and Hawaii law requires every front and back seat occupant to use a seat belt.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.front: What age rule requires a child restraint, and when must a child under eight use a booster seat?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.expected_back: A child under age four must ride in a child restraint, and a child under age eight must be belted in a booster seat if the child is shorter than four feet and weighs less than forty pounds.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.front: Why can occupants never rely on air bags alone during a multi-impact crash, and what happens after deployment?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.expected_back: Air bags are supplemental protection for a first impact only, because they deflate immediately and occupants must rely on belts in any later impact, and deployed air bags should be replaced to keep full protection.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.front: Contrast Hawaii's unconditional child-restraint age rule with its conditional booster-seat rule?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.expected_back: A child under four needs a child restraint, while a child under eight needs a booster seat only when the child is under four feet tall and under forty pounds.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.front: Compare how long an air bag protects you during a collision with how long a safety belt protects you?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.expected_back: Air bags protect only in the first impact and then deflate, while safety belts protect through every impact of a crash.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.front: How often is Hawaii's Periodic Motor Vehicle Inspection required for standard cars, ambulances, and brand-new vehicles?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.expected_back: Vehicles on public highways need a PMVI at least annually; ambulances require a check every six months, and a new vehicle's next inspection is due two years after its initial inspection when first sold.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.front: How do the safety-inspection intervals for ambulances and newly sold vehicles depart from the annual norm?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.expected_back: Ambulances must be safety inspected once every six months, while a new vehicle needs no further inspection until two years after its initial inspection on the date it was first sold.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.front: What insurance proof must you bring to pass Hawaii safety inspection, and what issued paper stays inside the car?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.expected_back: A Hawaii automobile insurance identification card must be presented to pass the safety inspection, and once the vehicle is approved a sticker is affixed and an inspection certificate is issued that must stay in the vehicle.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.front: Where do safety inspection stations transmit your inspection results?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.expected_back: The results of a safety inspection are sent electronically to the motor vehicle registration file.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.front: Who is authorized to conduct Hawaii safety inspections and issue certificates and stickers?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.expected_back: Many service stations and garages are authorized to perform safety inspections, issue inspection certificates and affix inspection stickers under the state inspection rules.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.front: Line up the three Hawaii safety-inspection intervals for ordinary vehicles, ambulances, and newly sold vehicles?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.expected_back: Ordinary vehicles are inspected once a year, while ambulances are inspected every six months and a newly sold vehicle is exempt until two years after its initial inspection.

sec03-card-sec03-R09.front: Distinguish the role of your insurance identification card at inspection from the role of the inspection certificate afterward?
sec03-card-sec03-R09.expected_back: The insurance identification card is needed to pass the inspection, while the inspection certificate is the document that must then remain in the vehicle.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.front: Which two exterior light colors and positions are banned on non-emergency vehicles in Hawaii?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.expected_back: A red light showing to the front, or a blue light visible from outside the vehicle, is prohibited on any vehicle other than an authorized emergency vehicle.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.front: Which three audible warning devices are illegal on any vehicle except an authorized emergency vehicle?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.expected_back: A bell, exhaust whistle or siren is prohibited equipment except on an authorized emergency vehicle.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.front: Which two muffler modifications or replacements violate Hawaii equipment law?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.expected_back: A muffler cut-out or by-pass is illegal, and so is any muffler that makes more noise than the original equipment manufacturer's muffler.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.front: Group together the two light setups and three sound devices reserved strictly for authorized emergency vehicles?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.expected_back: A red light to the front and a blue light visible outside are both reserved for authorized emergency vehicles, just as bells, exhaust whistles and sirens are.

sec03-card-sec03-F23.front: What is the maximum allowable steering-wheel free play with power steering (engine running) versus without power steering?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.expected_back: The steering wheel should turn smoothly from full right to full left and back, with no more than two inches of free play with power steering, checked with the engine running, or three inches without power steering.

sec03-card-sec03-F24.front: What three handling traits confirm your steering and front wheels are operating properly?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.expected_back: A healthy vehicle responds quickly to small steering movements, does not pull to either side, and its wheels do not shimmy.

sec03-card-sec03-F27.front: Below what fraction of an inch must a tire be replaced, and how does an upside-down Lincoln penny test it?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.expected_back: Replace any tire with less than one sixteenth of an inch of tread, and an easy check is a Lincoln penny placed upside down in the tread, because if the top of Lincoln's head is visible the tire must be replaced.

sec03-card-sec03-F26.front: How often should you check tire inflation, and where do you find the vehicle maker's recommended pressure and size?
sec03-card-sec03-F26.expected_back: Check your tires at least once a month, using the door jamb label for the manufacturer's recommended pressure and tire size, because proper pressure extends tire life and improves handling.

sec03-card-sec03-F28.front: Which four physical flaws should you inspect on all tires including the spare, and what driving clues warn of tire trouble?
sec03-card-sec03-F28.expected_back: Also check tires, including the spare, for cuts, bulges, tread separation and uneven wear, and treat a slight steering wheel vibration or an unusual noise as a possible tire problem.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.front: Compare the steering free-play ceiling on a power-steering vehicle with that on a manual-steering vehicle?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.expected_back: Two inches of steering free play is the limit with power steering, while three inches is the limit without it.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.front: Pair the monthly reference spot for tire pressure with the minimum tread measurement verified by a penny?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.expected_back: Tire pressure is checked at least monthly against the door jamb label, while tread is replaced below one sixteenth of an inch as shown by the penny test.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.front: At what speed and where do you run a common service-brake check, and how should the car behave?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.expected_back: A common brake test is to apply the brakes rather hard at four to eight miles per hour in a place where others are not forced to brake too, and the vehicle should not pull to either side.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.front: Where should you practice with antilock brakes, above what speed do they usually engage, and what pedal error is forbidden?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.expected_back: If your vehicle has antilock brakes, try them in an open area such as a deserted parking lot so you know what to expect, remembering that they usually activate only above ten miles per hour, activate more easily on a wet slippery surface, and must not be pumped.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.front: Why should you verify frequently that your rear brake lamps illuminate when pressing the pedal?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.expected_back: Brake lamps warn other drivers that you are slowing or stopping, so check often that they light when the brakes are applied.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.front: How does the speed for a standard brake-pull check compare with the usual minimum speed for antilock activation?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.expected_back: The ordinary brake test is done at four to eight miles per hour, while antilock brakes usually need more than ten miles per hour to activate.

sec03-card-sec03-F14.front: What dashboard clue warns of turn-signal trouble, and how must you signal turns until it is fixed?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.expected_back: Directional signals let you communicate with other drivers, a change in the dash light indication means they are not working properly, and if they fail you must use hand signals until they are repaired.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.front: Besides quieting engine noise, what lethal cabin hazard requires fixing exhaust leaks right away?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.expected_back: The exhaust system carries gases to an exit point that limits fumes entering the passenger compartment and keeps noise acceptable, so keep it free of leaks to prevent carbon monoxide poisoning and replace defective parts immediately.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.front: During which four low-light or weather situations are headlamps critical, and what two standards must they meet?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.expected_back: Head lamps are critical for night driving, rain, fog and tunnels, and they must work properly and be correctly adjusted at all times.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.front: Why must both the primary latch and secondary catch on a front-opening hood work properly?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.expected_back: A front-opening hood has a primary latch and a secondary catch, and both must work so the hood cannot fly open and block your vision while driving.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.front: What standards apply to a vehicle's horn and to its rear-view mirrors?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.expected_back: Every vehicle must have a horn in good working condition to give an audible warning, and rear-view mirrors must be clean, firmly attached and adjusted for the widest view of the rear horizon.

sec03-card-sec03-F25.front: What safety role do tail lamps and side marker lamps perform, and how should you maintain them?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.expected_back: Tail lamps and side marker lamps warn other drivers of your presence, so check them periodically for proper operation.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.front: How must you communicate turns and stops if your electric directional indicators quit working?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.expected_back: When turn indicators stop working, communicate turns with hand signals until repairs are made.

sec03-card-sec03-R10.front: State Hawaii's noise standard for replacement mufflers alongside its rule on cutouts and bypasses?
sec03-card-sec03-R10.expected_back: A replacement muffler may not be louder than the original equipment muffler, while a muffler cut-out or by-pass is prohibited outright.

sec03-card-sec03-F01.front: Name the core mechanical, body, and gauge components that must meet standards on every Hawaii highway vehicle?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.expected_back: Every motor vehicle driven on Hawaii highways must carry equipment that meets established standards, including brakes, steering, a horn, door handles, tires, an exhaust system, lights, glass, windshield wipers, an odometer, a speedometer, bumpers, wheels and lug nuts, fenders, floor pans, a hood with catches and a gas tank.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.front: If you borrow a friend's or family member's car, who answers legally for its safe mechanical condition?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.expected_back: Even if someone else owns the vehicle, the driver is responsible for its condition, and routine care should be carried out regularly by the driver or by an experienced mechanic.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.front: Why should you verify that every vehicle door latches and locks properly?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.expected_back: Door latches and locks provide safety and security, so make sure every door latches and locks properly.

sec03-card-sec03-F29.front: What three standards keep your windshield, wiper blades, and washer system road-ready?
sec03-card-sec03-F29.expected_back: The windshield must be free of cracks and breaks that interfere with vision, the wipers should clean it evenly without streaks, and the washer reservoir should be kept filled and checked often.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.front: How frequently do drivers younger than twenty crash compared with their share of all licensed drivers?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.expected_back: Crash data show that the youngest drivers, those under age twenty, crash about twice as often as their share of all drivers would predict.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.front: Until which age bracket do crash rates keep dropping, giving drivers the fewest crashes of any group?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.expected_back: As driver age increases crashes keep falling until about age fifty to fifty-four, and drivers in that range have the fewest crashes of any age group.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.front: At what age do crash rates begin climbing again, and how do drivers past seventy-five compare with youth under twenty-five?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.expected_back: Beginning at age fifty-five crashes occur more often as age increases, and drivers over seventy-five have more crashes than middle-aged drivers but still fewer than drivers under twenty-five.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.front: How do under-twenty crash rates contrast with the fifty-to-fifty-four age bracket?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.expected_back: Drivers under twenty have about twice the expected crashes, while drivers around fifty to fifty-four have the fewest of any age group.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.front: Once crashes start rising again at fifty-five, who still crashes less often—drivers over seventy-five or drivers under twenty-five?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.expected_back: Crashes rise again from age fifty-five, but drivers over seventy-five still crash less often than drivers under twenty-five.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.front: What effect do worry, home quarrels, money stress, family illness, fear, or overconfidence have on your driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.expected_back: If you are worried, distracted or preoccupied you cannot count on being alert enough to drive safely, and troubles at home, quarrels, financial worries, serious family illness, personal fears or overconfidence can make you temporarily crash-prone.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.front: What should someone who is angry, grieving, or fresh off a heated argument do before taking the wheel?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.expected_back: A person who has just had a violent argument, or who is angry or grieving, needs some cooling-off time before driving, because taking out frustration or anger on the road is very poor judgment and an expensive way to vent emotion.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.front: What is the safest choice when you feel worried, sick, nervous, frightened, angry, or depressed?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.expected_back: Worry and safe driving do not mix, so if you are worried, ill, nervous, frightened, angry or depressed you should let someone else drive.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.front: How does the handbook pair anger or grief versus worry, illness, or fright before a trip?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.expected_back: Emotional upsets such as anger or grief call for a cooling-off period before driving, while worry, illness or fright call for letting someone else drive.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.front: What three basic elements make up every driving scene, and which one alone can gather facts and act?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.expected_back: Every driving situation involves three basic elements, the environment of highway and traffic, the vehicle, and the driver, and only the driver can gather information, apply skill, knowledge, experience and judgment, and take the action needed to complete the trip safely.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.front: How do good and poor judgment interact with driving skill, and what mainly shapes your judgment?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.expected_back: Good judgment can help make up for lower levels of skill, knowledge or experience, but poor judgment can cancel out any degree of expertise, and your judgment is shaped mainly by your attitude when you drive.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.front: How must a well-adjusted driver treat other people sharing the roadway?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.expected_back: A well-adjusted person is more likely to be a good driver, and you must act with consideration and courtesy toward other road users rather than only from your own point of view.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.front: Because the driver holds full vehicle control, what does your behind-the-wheel attitude reveal about you?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.expected_back: Because full control of the vehicle rests with the driver, your attitude behind the wheel and how you use that power reveal whether you are a bully, a thoughtless lawbreaker or a self-centered lane stealer, or a reliable, courteous and emotionally mature person ready to share the road.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.front: How does good judgment affect limited experience, and what can poor judgment do to expert skill?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.expected_back: Good judgment can compensate for weaker skill or experience, while poor judgment can wipe out even expert skill.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.front: In the trio of surroundings, vehicle, and driver, what separates the driver from the other two?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.expected_back: Driving involves the surroundings, the vehicle and the driver. Only the driver gathers information, applies skill, knowledge, experience and judgment, and acts to complete the task safely.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.front: Even though years build skill at first, what five physical or mental shifts does aging eventually bring?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.expected_back: Driving experience usually increases skill and drivers become safer with the years up to a point, but aging eventually brings reduced hearing and eyesight, less physical dexterity and longer reaction time, longer decision time, and a shorter attention span.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.front: Why do older drivers often grow hazardous to themselves and everyone around them?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.expected_back: Older drivers very often fail to recognize the gradual decline in their ability to cope with driving situations and so become increasingly dangerous to themselves and others.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.front: What five health and medical habits should every driver—including experienced seniors—maintain?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.expected_back: Every driver, including the older experienced driver, should keep physically fit, have an annual physical examination, know how medications affect driving, recognize and drive within personal limitations, and seek and follow a physician's advice about driving capability.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.front: Which four physical or substance conditions does the handbook list as crash causes or contributors?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.expected_back: Your physical condition has an important bearing on safe driving, and alcohol, drugs, illness or disability may cause or contribute to a traffic crash.

sec05-card-sec05-R09.front: Which health habits belong to every driver, and which blind spot trips up older drivers most often?
sec05-card-sec05-R09.expected_back: Annual physical examinations and knowledge of medication effects are habits for every driver, while recognizing a gradual decline is the step older drivers most often miss.

sec05-card-sec05-R10.front: How does the handbook group alcohol, drugs, illness, and disability compared with worry, anger, and overconfidence?
sec05-card-sec05-R10.expected_back: Alcohol, drugs, illness and disability are medical factors that contribute to crashes, while worry, anger and overconfidence are emotional factors that do the same.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.front: With advancing age, which two driving times lengthen and which four capacities shrink?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.expected_back: Aging increases reaction time and decision time, while it decreases hearing, eyesight, dexterity and attention span.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.front: How does craving acceptance and recognition push some young adults into severe crashes?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.expected_back: Young adults want acceptance and recognition of their capabilities, and as drivers they sometimes demonstrate those capabilities beyond the limits of the vehicle, the road and even the most skillful drivers, which often ends in disaster.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.front: How does a young driver escape the show-off trap and prove genuine maturity behind the wheel?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.expected_back: A young driver avoids that trap by resisting the desire to exhibit and compete, which only shows inexperience and immaturity, and by declining every challenge to prove personal or vehicle capability, which is adequate proof of maturity and responsibility.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.front: How does the classic young-driver hazard differ from the classic older-driver hazard?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.expected_back: The younger driver's problem is the urge to exhibit and accept challenges, while the older driver's problem is failing to notice declining ability.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.front: What does turning down a driving dare prove, and what does accepting one prove?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.expected_back: Declining a challenge proves maturity, while accepting one proves only inexperience and immaturity.

sec04-card-sec04-F01.front: Where must a Hawaii highway vehicle be registered, and how often must that county license it?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.expected_back: Hawaii law requires the vehicle you drive on public highways to be registered in the county where you operate it, and to be licensed every year by that same county.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.front: What safety certificate must precede registration, and how does required insurance proof differ for cars versus motorcycles?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.expected_back: A vehicle must have a current, valid safety inspection certificate before it can be registered, with proof of motor vehicle insurance required for cars, buses and trucks at inspection and proof of liability coverage required for motorcycles.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.front: Who keeps the registration certificate, where does it belong, and when does each staggered registration expire?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.expected_back: The registration certificate is issued to the purchaser, who must keep it in the vehicle, and registrations are staggered so that each one expires annually at the end of its twelfth month.

sec04-card-sec04-R07.front: Contrast the insurance proof required at inspection for cars, buses, and trucks with that for motorcycles?
sec04-card-sec04-R07.expected_back: Cars, buses and trucks show proof of motor vehicle insurance at inspection, while motorcycles show proof of liability coverage.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.front: How and within how many days must a registered owner report an address change, and what vehicle details go inside?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.expected_back: When a registered owner's address changes from the one on the registration application, the owner must notify the county agency in writing within thirty days, giving the old and new addresses, the vehicle license number, the make and the vehicle identification number.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.front: What deadline, visit type, and three documents are required when a registered owner's name changes?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.expected_back: When a registered owner's name changes from the one on the certificate of ownership, the owner must appear in person at the county agency within thirty days with proof of the name change, the properly endorsed certificate of ownership and the current year's registration certificate.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.front: Compare how a registered vehicle owner reports an address change versus a legal name change?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.expected_back: A registration address change is a written notice within thirty days, while a registration name change requires appearing in person within thirty days with the endorsed title.

sec04-card-sec04-F24.front: Which vehicles display only a single rear license plate in Hawaii, and where must all other vehicles mount plates?
sec04-card-sec04-F24.expected_back: Motorcycles, trailers and semi-trailers display one license plate on the rear, while every other vehicle must display a plate on both the front and the rear.

sec04-card-sec04-F25.front: What three legal steps apply to mopeds, and where do the moped's plate and inspection sticker go?
sec04-card-sec04-F25.expected_back: Mopeds must be inspected, registered and licensed, and the moped's license plate and inspection sticker must be displayed on its rear.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.front: Group together every Hawaii vehicle that displays a rear-only plate versus vehicles needing both front and rear plates?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.expected_back: Cars carry plates front and rear, while motorcycles, trailers, semi-trailers and mopeds carry a plate on the rear only.

sec04-card-sec04-F21.front: How long can a temporary Hawaii permit last for a vehicle still registered in another state?
sec04-card-sec04-F21.expected_back: A vehicle still registered in another state may receive a Hawaii permit, a temporary registration, that allows driving on Hawaii roads until the home registration expires, but never for longer than a twelve-month period.

sec04-card-sec04-F22.front: Which three documents must you bring to obtain an out-of-state temporary vehicle permit?
sec04-card-sec04-F22.expected_back: To get the temporary permit you must present the vehicle's certificate of registration, its shipping receipt and a current Hawaii safety inspection certificate.

sec04-card-sec04-F23.front: What must you do once an out-of-state temporary permit expires, and who is exempt?
sec04-card-sec04-F23.expected_back: When the temporary permit expires you must register the vehicle with the county agency where you reside, unless you are a member of the United States armed forces.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.front: Contrast the expiration rule for an out-of-state temporary permit with a regular Hawaii registration?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.expected_back: A temporary permit runs until the out-of-state registration expires but never beyond twelve months, while a Hawaii registration expires at the end of its own twelfth month every year.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.front: What official record does registration establish, and what two checks happen the first time a vehicle registers in Hawaii?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.expected_back: Registration creates the official record of a vehicle's ownership, and when a vehicle is first registered in Hawaii it is inspected and weighed so that its identification number and its weight are properly recorded.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.front: Who issues Hawaii registrations and titles, and who holds the certificate of ownership while a loan is active?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.expected_back: Registrations and titles are issued by the appropriate agency in each county, and the Hawaii certificate of ownership, the title, is held by the legal owner or by the lien holder until the loan on the vehicle is paid off.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.front: Where does the county mail registration renewal forms, and what should you do if a detail is wrong?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.expected_back: Registration renewal applications are mailed to your last recorded address, and any error you find on the application should be reported promptly to the county agency.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.front: What stub rule, payment method, and ten-day mailing deadline govern renewing your registration by mail?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.expected_back: To renew by mail you send both parts of the renewal application, without detaching the stub, with a check or money order for the exact total fee shown, mailed to your county agency within ten working days before the end of the expiration month.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.front: How do you renew a currently registered Hawaii vehicle online?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.expected_back: A vehicle currently registered in Hawaii may have its registration renewed online through the state motor vehicle renewal site by selecting the county of registration.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.front: Compare who holds the Hawaii title with who receives and stores the registration certificate?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.expected_back: The title is held by the legal owner or lien holder, while the registration certificate is issued to the purchaser and must be kept in the vehicle.

sec04-card-sec04-R09.front: How does the mail-in registration deadline compare with the actual expiration date of your tags?
sec04-card-sec04-R09.expected_back: Mail renewal must reach the county within ten working days before the end of the expiration month, while the registration itself expires at the end of that month.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.front: What signed paperwork is required when you buy a brand-new vehicle from a dealer in Hawaii?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.expected_back: When you buy a new vehicle in Hawaii you must obtain an application form countersigned by the licensed new car dealer certifying the sale.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.front: Which two alternative ownership documents does Hawaii accept for a brand-new vehicle bought in another state?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.expected_back: For a new vehicle bought in another state, where ownership documents vary, Hawaii accepts either the manufacturer's certificate of origin or a notarized bill of sale.

sec04-card-sec04-F17.front: What three items are required to register a brand-new vehicle bought in a foreign country?
sec04-card-sec04-F17.expected_back: A new vehicle bought in a foreign country needs a bill of sale from the foreign dealer issued in your name, a manufacturer's certification label showing compliance with United States standards, and a seventeen-character vehicle identification number.

sec04-card-sec04-F18.front: Which two ownership documents must accompany a used vehicle purchased in a foreign country?
sec04-card-sec04-F18.expected_back: A used vehicle bought in a foreign country must come with a certificate of registration and a bill of sale as proof of ownership.

sec04-card-sec04-F19.front: Which three items must the named seller give you for an out-of-state used car from a title state?
sec04-card-sec04-F19.expected_back: When you buy a used vehicle in another state, the seller named on that state's title must give you the title itself, the registration certificate and a notarized bill of sale.

sec04-card-sec04-F20.front: What registration proof and how many notarized bills of sale are required for a used car from a non-title state?
sec04-card-sec04-F20.expected_back: A used vehicle from a non-title state comes with that state's current registration certificate or certification of registration plus two notarized bills of sale, the first covering the previous owner's sale to the seller and the second covering the seller's sale to you.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.front: Contrast the ownership documents required for a new out-of-state purchase versus a used title-state purchase?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.expected_back: A new vehicle from another state needs a manufacturer's certificate of origin or a notarized bill of sale, while a used vehicle from another state needs the title, the registration and a notarized bill of sale from the named seller.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.front: When does an out-of-state used vehicle require one notarized bill of sale versus two?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.expected_back: A used vehicle from a title state needs one notarized bill of sale, while one from a non-title state needs two, covering both the current and the previous sale.

sec04-card-sec04-R10.front: Compare the paperwork needed for a new foreign-bought vehicle with that for a used foreign-bought vehicle?
sec04-card-sec04-R10.expected_back: A new foreign-bought vehicle needs a dealer bill of sale, a compliance label and a seventeen-character identification number, while a used foreign-bought vehicle needs a registration certificate and a bill of sale.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.front: What plate option and four Hawaii tax-or-fee exemptions apply to non-resident armed forces members stationed in Hawaii?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.expected_back: A member of the United States armed forces on duty at a military installation in Hawaii who is a legal resident of another state may keep the vehicle registered in that state and is exempt from the Hawaii excise tax on vehicles brought in, the county and state weight taxes, the state registration fee and the highway beautification fee.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.front: Which veterans qualify for an exemption from Hawaii vehicle registration fees?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.expected_back: A veteran who is one hundred percent medically disabled and presents the accompanying paperwork is exempt from paying registration fees.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.front: What six items must a stationed service member bring to switch a mainland-titled vehicle onto Hawaii registration?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.memory_hook: Application, title, registration, safety, shipping, VIN
sec04-card-sec04-F13.expected_back: A service member whose vehicle was last registered and titled in another state and is now subject to Hawaii registration must give the county agency where stationed an application, the out-of-state title and registration, a current Hawaii safety inspection certificate, a shipping receipt and a verification of the vehicle identification number.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.front: When registering a vehicle arriving from a non-title state, what items accompany the application?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.expected_back: For a vehicle from a non-title state, the application is accompanied by the registration certificate, one or more notarized bills of sale establishing the chain of ownership, a current Hawaii safety inspection and a verification of the vehicle serial number.

sec04-card-sec04-R08.front: How does the scope of a stationed non-resident service member's exemption compare with a fully disabled veteran's exemption?
sec04-card-sec04-R08.expected_back: A stationed service member resident elsewhere may keep an out-of-state registration and skip the Hawaii taxes and fees, while a fully disabled veteran is exempt only from registration fees.

sec13-card-sec13-F18.front: Why should you match surrounding traffic speed, and where do you move if you cannot keep up?
sec13-card-sec13-F18.expected_back: Keep pace with traffic, because vehicles moving the same direction at the same speed never collide while moving faster than traffic creates constant conflicts, and if you cannot keep up, move as far right as possible.

sec13-card-sec13-F19.front: How do you count out Hawaii's minimum following interval using a fixed roadside object?
sec13-card-sec13-F19.expected_back: Striking the vehicle ahead is one of the most common crashes and usually comes from following too closely, so check your interval by noting when the vehicle ahead passes a tree, pole or other marker and counting one thousand one, one thousand two, and if you reach the word two before you reach the marker you have at least the two-second interval you should never go below.

sec13-card-sec13-F20.front: What three problems come from tailgating and surging between bursts of speed and hard braking?
sec13-card-sec13-F20.expected_back: Following too closely cuts your view of road and traffic conditions ahead, constantly changing speed confuses other drivers and bursts of speed with heavy braking are wasteful and dangerous, so maintain a steady speed.

sec13-card-sec13-F21.front: How should poor road or weather conditions versus emotions govern your driving speed?
sec13-card-sec13-F21.expected_back: Reduce speed in poor road or weather conditions for better control and more time to react, and never let emotions set your speed, because being in a hurry may mean never arriving at all.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.front: Which exact phrase do you count before reaching a marker to verify a two-second gap?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.expected_back: To check for a safe following gap of at least two seconds, watch the vehicle ahead pass a roadside marker and count one thousand one, one thousand two before reaching that spot.

sec13-card-sec13-F27.front: When is overtaking justified on a two- or three-lane road, and who passes first in a queue?
sec13-card-sec13-F27.expected_back: Passing is hazardous on two or three lane roads because the opposing lane must be used and improper procedure can cause a head-on collision, so pass only when the vehicle ahead is moving below the safe speed, never merely because it is there or to gain a few car lengths in moderate or heavy traffic, and in a line of vehicles let those ahead pass the leader first.

sec13-card-sec13-F28.front: Which side do you normally pass on, when may you pass right, and is the shoulder allowed?
sec13-card-sec13-F28.expected_back: Pass on the left except when the vehicle being overtaken is making or about to make a left turn, in which case pass carefully on the right but never by driving onto the shoulder, and obey every sign and marking that restricts passing.

sec13-card-sec13-F29.front: What sequence of checks, signals, horn use, and acceleration sets up a proper pass?
sec13-card-sec13-F29.expected_back: To pass, keep enough following distance to see opposing traffic, check ahead for conflicting traffic, signal left, physically check behind for anyone passing you, sound the horn so the driver ahead knows, accelerate to passing speed in your own lane, then move left and pass.

sec13-card-sec13-F30.front: What should you do if a conflict appears mid-pass, and when may you return to your lane?
sec13-card-sec13-F30.expected_back: If a conflict appears before the pass is complete, brake sharply and drop back behind the overtaken vehicle instead of speeding up, because speed can be cut more quickly with the brakes than it can be gained with power, and return to your lane only when the overtaken vehicle is visible in your interior rear-view mirror.

sec13-card-sec13-F31.front: On multi-lane roads your way, which lanes are off-limits and where is passing always banned?
sec13-card-sec13-F31.expected_back: Where two or more lanes run in your direction, never use an opposing lane to pass; pass on either side with proper lane change procedure, being extra careful on the right because you approach in the other driver's blind spot, and in every passing situation never pass while approaching or moving through an intersection or crosswalk.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.front: When danger appears mid-pass, which response is required and which move does the manual forbid?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.expected_back: When a conflict appears mid-pass you brake and fall back, while speeding up to finish the pass is the move the manual forbids.

sec13-card-sec13-R06.front: When overtaking a left-turning car on the right, what separates a legal move from an illegal one?
sec13-card-sec13-R06.expected_back: A vehicle turning left may be passed carefully on the right, while passing on the shoulder is prohibited in that same situation.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.front: How do you choose lanes on a two-lane road in open traffic versus heavy congestion?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.expected_back: With one lane in your direction you must use it, taking great care in congested areas, and with two lanes in open free-flowing traffic you use the right lane and the left lane only for passing or when vehicles are entering from the right, while in heavy traffic you may use either lane but keep up with traffic at a steady speed without lane hopping.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.front: Where should through drivers vs. slower drivers travel when three or more lanes run your direction?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.expected_back: With three or more lanes in your direction, choose the center lanes where there are fewer conflicts, leave the right and left lanes for vehicles entering and leaving, keep a steady speed with the flow with few lane changes, and use the right lane if you are slower than other traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-F12.front: What visual checks and minimum signaling distance are required before beginning any lane change?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.expected_back: Lane changes should be kept to a minimum, and before one you check conditions ahead, to the sides and behind using the mirrors and a physical head-turn check of the blind spots, then signal well in advance, the law requiring a signal for at least one hundred feet before the change begins.

sec13-card-sec13-F13.front: How should you steer into a neighboring lane, and is it better to merge ahead or behind?
sec13-card-sec13-F13.expected_back: With ample clearance, move gradually and steadily into the other lane, because abrupt movements can cause overcontrol or loss of control, and it is better to slow slightly and move in behind a vehicle, keeping it in sight, than to speed up and cut in ahead.

sec13-card-sec13-F14.front: Why should you never muscle into a gap at or below safe following distance?
sec13-card-sec13-F14.expected_back: Never force your way into a gap at or below the minimum safe following distance, because that discourteous move makes other drivers close ranks against you, whereas allowing time and signaling properly leads courteous drivers to make room.

sec13-card-sec13-F15.front: Who yields during a lane change, how do you join a backed-up queue, and where are shifts banned?
sec13-card-sec13-F15.expected_back: Always yield to vehicles in the other lane when changing lanes, join a congested lane at the end of the line rather than crowding in ahead, stay in your lane until the change can be made safely even if inconvenient, and never change lanes while approaching or moving through an intersection or crosswalk.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.front: How does normal lane-change yielding contrast with changing lanes inside an intersection or crosswalk?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.expected_back: Changing lanes requires yielding to the vehicles already in the other lane, while changing lanes at or through an intersection or crosswalk is never allowed at all.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.front: How does your primary travel lane shift when moving from two same-way lanes to three or more?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.expected_back: With two lanes in open traffic the right lane is the travel lane and the left is for passing, while with three or more lanes the center lanes are the travel lanes and the outer lanes serve entering and leaving traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-F22.front: How do turns differ from curves, which lanes do you use, and what if you miss your turn lane?
sec13-card-sec13-F22.expected_back: Turns are changes of direction from a lane at intersections or driveways while curves are changes in the direction of the road itself, and for a turn you get into the proper lane well in advance, turn from the lane nearest the turn direction into the nearest available lane, and if you are in the wrong lane continue on and turn elsewhere rather than forcing a last-minute lane change.

sec13-card-sec13-F23.front: When should you slow for a turn or curve, and why hold steady speed through it?
sec13-card-sec13-F23.expected_back: Make precise turns without swinging wide or cutting short, slow to a proper speed before a curve or turn and hold a steady speed through it, because braking or an abrupt speed change in a turn or curve can cause loss of control.

sec13-card-sec13-F24.front: Why does the Hawaii manual advise avoiding left turns and U-turns whenever practical?
sec13-card-sec13-F24.expected_back: Avoid left turns and U-turns whenever possible because they conflict more with traffic, are much more hazardous than right turns and impede other vehicles.

sec13-card-sec13-F25.front: How should you position your car and front wheels after a red light turns green for your left turn?
sec13-card-sec13-F25.expected_back: When waiting to turn left at a red light and the light turns green, move slowly into the intersection with the wheels pointed straight ahead and turn only when the intersection is clear and it is safe.

sec13-card-sec13-F26.front: Who must you scan for on turns, and what rules govern red-light rights and bike lanes?
sec13-card-sec13-F26.expected_back: Watch with great care for pedestrians, bicyclists and motorcyclists when turning, since vehicles, darkness or weather may hide them, always come to a complete stop before a right turn on a red signal, use extra caution on curves and turns in poor weather or on gravel, sand or mud, and do not drive in a bike lane when turning right at an intersection.

sec13-card-sec13-R08.front: Contrast your entry move when waiting to turn left on green versus turning right on red?
sec13-card-sec13-R08.expected_back: While waiting to turn left on green you keep the wheels straight and creep into the intersection, while a right turn on red always begins with a complete stop.

sec13-card-sec13-F36.front: What happens to vehicle control when hard braking locks your wheels, especially the front pair?
sec13-card-sec13-F36.expected_back: A hard brake application can make wheels slide, and sliding wheels, especially the front ones, leave you without control of the vehicle.

sec13-card-sec13-F37.front: Without antilock brakes, how should you brake and steer when an obstacle looms right ahead?
sec13-card-sec13-F37.expected_back: When in danger of hitting a vehicle, person or object, do not jam on the brakes and slide the wheels, because you will almost certainly hit it; instead apply and release the brakes rapidly and steer toward a clear area, even off the road, while avoiding people, trees, utility poles and solid structures, and consult the owner's manual for antilock brakes.

sec13-card-sec13-F38.front: How should you handle braking for turns, slick surfaces, and right after driving through water?
sec13-card-sec13-F38.expected_back: Avoid braking while turning by slowing beforehand, brake very cautiously on water, ice, snow, frost, sand or gravel, and after driving through water test the brakes and, if they are weakened, apply them lightly several times until normal action returns.

sec13-card-sec13-F39.front: What two harms come from resting your foot on the brake, and what does a lit warning lamp mean?
sec13-card-sec13-F39.expected_back: Resting your foot on the brake pedal lights the stop lamps and misleads following drivers and also partly applies the brakes in many vehicles, causing excessive wear, and a brake warning lamp that lights when you brake means a partial failure needing immediate repair.

sec13-card-sec13-F40.front: How far behind the car ahead should you stop in traffic, and why?
sec13-card-sec13-F40.expected_back: Begin slowing as soon as braking ahead becomes apparent, brake smoothly and steadily, and when stopping in traffic stay far enough back to see where the rear tires of the vehicle ahead meet the road, which leaves room to go around if it cannot move.

sec13-card-sec13-F41.front: What happens during prolonged downhill braking, and how do you prevent it?
sec13-card-sec13-F41.expected_back: Prolonged braking heats the brakes and makes them much less effective, which can usually be avoided by shifting to a lower gear so the engine helps hold the speed down.

sec13-card-sec13-F35.front: How do brakes physically stop a car, and why do speed bursts plus hard stops cost money?
sec13-card-sec13-F35.expected_back: Brakes stop a vehicle by turning its energy of motion into wasted heat, so every braking wastes fuel money and wears brakes and tires, and careful braking without bursts of speed followed by hard stops saves energy and money.

sec13-card-sec13-R07.front: Without antilock brakes, how does pumping the pedal compare with jamming it in an emergency?
sec13-card-sec13-R07.expected_back: In an emergency without antilock brakes you pump the brakes and steer clear, while jamming the brakes slides the wheels and removes steering control.

sec13-card-sec13-F01.front: Under Hawaii law, what age threshold and time limit forbid leaving a child unattended in a vehicle?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.expected_back: Hawaii law forbids a driver or any adult passenger from leaving a child under nine years old unattended in a motor vehicle for five minutes or longer, because of dangers such as extreme heat, theft of the car, or accidental use of the emergency brake, power windows or trunk release.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.front: How must you check behind your vehicle before and during backing instead of trusting mirrors?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.expected_back: Backing is dangerous because visibility is restricted, so check the area behind the vehicle before getting in, turn around and look to the rear instead of relying on mirrors whose view is too small, and have someone outside guide you if you cannot see.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.front: What brake check, speed, front-end watch, and parking habit make backing safer?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.expected_back: When backing, apply the brakes gently as the movement starts to confirm they work, always back slowly, watch the front of the vehicle for clearance when backing and turning at once, and avoid backing into or across a roadway, parking so that you can enter traffic forward.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.front: Which lane may you back into when clear, and who bears chief responsibility when leaving a space?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.expected_back: When traffic is clear, back only into the lane nearest the edge of the roadway, and the chief responsibility for avoiding a collision rests with the driver leaving a parking space, who should look, signal and yield.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.front: Why does backing in residential neighborhoods demand extraordinary caution?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.expected_back: Use extraordinary caution when backing in residential areas, because children often play behind and between parked vehicles.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.front: Where must you stop legally when exiting a driveway, and how do you enter the street?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.expected_back: Entering from a driveway you must always stop before crossing the sidewalk area, since failing to stop is unlawful, then move forward slowly watching for pedestrians and vehicles, make sure the lane is clear, enter the nearest lane with a right turn when possible, and accelerate to traffic speed.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.front: How does pulling out of a parallel space compare in direction and risk with leaving a diagonal stall?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.expected_back: From a parallel parking space you move forward into the nearest lane when there is enough gap in traffic, while leaving a diagonal space requires backing into the lane first, a much more dangerous and difficult maneuver that takes more time.

sec13-card-sec13-R09.front: Pair the mandatory stop rule for driveways with the liability rule for backing out of stalls?
sec13-card-sec13-R09.expected_back: Leaving a driveway requires a stop before the sidewalk, while backing out of a parking space places the chief collision responsibility on the driver leaving the space.

sec13-card-sec13-R10.front: Which parking stall lets you pull straight forward into the nearest lane, and which forces backing?
sec13-card-sec13-R10.expected_back: Leaving a parallel space is a forward move into the nearest lane, while leaving a diagonal space means backing into the lane, which is slower and more dangerous.

sec13-card-sec13-R12.front: Connect Hawaii's unattended-vehicle child rule with the residential backing warning?
sec13-card-sec13-R12.expected_back: A child under nine may not be left alone in a vehicle for five minutes or more, while children playing behind parked cars are the reason for extra caution when backing in residential areas.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.front: What is a roundabout, who uses it, and who holds right-of-way at every entry?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.expected_back: A roundabout is a one-way circular intersection serving drivers, pedestrians, pedestrians with disabilities and bicyclists, in which entering traffic must yield to circulating traffic, and each approach carries a yield sign and may have yield line markings.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.front: Which direction do you circulate, which signal exits a roundabout, and what if you miss your exit?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.expected_back: Driving a roundabout, slow on approach, yield to pedestrians and bicyclists when entering and exiting, look left and yield to traffic already circulating including bicyclists, drive to the right of the central island counterclockwise at low speed, signal right to exit, and if you miss your exit go around again.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.front: Compare where you look and yield entering a roundabout with how you signal leaving it?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.expected_back: In a roundabout you look left and yield to circulating traffic, while to leave it you signal with the right turn signal.

sec13-card-sec13-F32.front: Which five visual clues warn that a curb-parked car may pull out or swing open a door?
sec13-card-sec13-F32.expected_back: Parked cars block your view of vehicles, bicycles and pedestrians and may pull out or open a door into your path, so watch for movement in or near the vehicle, lit stop, back-up or signal lamps, exhaust smoke or vapor, and turning front wheels, and assume a driver who has just parked will open the door.

sec13-card-sec13-F33.front: Where must you pull over to load passengers or talk instead of stopping inside a travel lane?
sec13-card-sec13-F33.expected_back: Stopping unnecessarily in a traffic lane is dangerous, discourteous, inconsiderate and illegal, so stops to load or unload or to talk with others must be made in a parking space, loading zone or other place out of the lane.

sec13-card-sec13-F34.front: What space must be open before you ever drive into an intersection or crosswalk?
sec13-card-sec13-F34.expected_back: Do not stop within an intersection or crosswalk, and never drive into an intersection or crosswalk unless there is room for your entire vehicle on the far side.

sec13-card-sec13-F42.front: What is downshifting, which transmissions allow it, and what two driving purposes does it serve?
sec13-card-sec13-F42.expected_back: Downshifting means selecting a lower gear range while moving, works with manual and automatic transmissions, and serves two purposes, greater engine braking when slowing or holding speed on a downgrade and better performance when accelerating.

sec13-card-sec13-F43.front: When do you downshift for a steep hill, and how is it done on a synchronized manual?
sec13-card-sec13-F43.expected_back: Downshift for engine braking before starting down a steep grade because shifting is harder at higher speeds, and on a synchronized manual transmission the procedure is to depress the clutch, move the lever to the next lower gear and release the clutch slowly, while double clutching on a non-synchronized transmission should not be tried without practice.

sec13-card-sec13-F16.front: What is the most frequently listed cause of crashes, and who directly controls its underlying triggers?
sec13-card-sec13-F16.expected_back: Excessive speed for conditions is the most often listed cause of crashes, its underlying cause, whether intoxication, inattention or competition, is controlled directly by the driver, and most vehicles can reach speeds far beyond what the driver, the road and the vehicle can handle.

sec13-card-sec13-F17.front: What two conditions define a safe vehicle speed at any moment?
sec13-card-sec13-F17.expected_back: A safe vehicle speed is adjusted to traffic, weather and road conditions and always stays within the posted limits.

sec13-card-sec13-R11.front: Contrast downshifting before a steep downgrade with riding the brakes all the way down?
sec13-card-sec13-R11.expected_back: Downshifting before a steep grade lets the engine hold speed, while prolonged braking on the grade overheats the brakes and weakens them.

sec13-card-sec13-R13.front: What should you expect from a driver who just parked versus a car showing exhaust or turned wheels?
sec13-card-sec13-R13.expected_back: A driver who has just parked should be assumed about to open the door, while a parked car showing lamps, exhaust vapor or turning wheels should be assumed about to pull out.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.front: In what three-step order do you pick your stopping point on a steady red light, and how long must you wait?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.expected_back: On a red light you must stop at the stop line, or before entering the crosswalk if there is no stop line, or before entering the intersection if there is neither, and you must remain stopped until the signal turns green.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.front: Under what conditions may you turn right on a steady red light, and to whom must you yield?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.expected_back: After stopping on red you may turn right unless a sign prohibits it, and you must yield to all pedestrians and all vehicles while making that turn.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.front: In what specific street-to-street layout is turning left after stopping on red legal?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.expected_back: After stopping on red you may also turn left from a one-way street onto another one-way street whose traffic moves to the left, unless a sign prohibits that turn.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.front: After a full stop with no prohibition posted, how does a legal right on red differ from a legal left on red?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.expected_back: After coming to a stop at a red light, you may turn right unless a sign prohibits it, while you may turn left on red from a one-way street into a one-way street where traffic moves to the left unless a sign prohibits that turn.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.front: Where must you stop on red when no stop bar exists, and where if no crosswalk is marked either?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.expected_back: With no stop line you stop before the crosswalk, while with neither stop line nor crosswalk you stop before entering the intersection.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.front: What does a steady yellow traffic light warn, and what rule governs entering once red appears?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.expected_back: A yellow light warns that red is about to appear, so you should avoid entering the intersection on yellow, and you must never enter the intersection after the red light is shown.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.front: What movements does a steady green ball allow, and who still holds priority over you?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.expected_back: A green light means go straight or turn unless signs prohibit the turn, and you must yield to all pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.front: How does Hawaii's rule for approaching a yellow light differ in strictness from a red light?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.expected_back: A yellow light warns that red is coming and you should avoid entering, while entering after the red light appears is flatly prohibited.

sec08-card-sec08-R09.front: How does your yielding duty on a green light differ from your yielding duty on a right turn on red?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.expected_back: A green light requires yielding to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection, while a right turn on red requires yielding to all pedestrians and all vehicles.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.front: How does allowed movement on a standard green light differ from a lighted green directional pointer?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.expected_back: A green light allows going straight or turning unless signs prohibit, while a green arrow allows movement only in the arrow's direction.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.front: What does a flashing red beacon require—alongside what posted octagon—and what does flashing yellow mean?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.expected_back: Flashing signals are sometimes used to warn of danger, a flashing red signal has the same meaning as a stop sign and a stop sign is also posted there, and a flashing yellow signal means proceed only with caution.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.front: When a normal intersection light switches into flashing red and flashing yellow mode, what rules apply?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.expected_back: When a regular traffic signal shows flashing lights, the flashing red and flashing yellow carry the same meanings as the separate flashing signals.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.front: What is the key action difference between meeting a flashing red beacon and a flashing yellow beacon?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.expected_back: A flashing red signal requires a full stop like a stop sign, while a flashing yellow signal allows you to proceed with caution.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.front: Where are lane control lights hung, and what kind of changing traffic lane do they manage?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.expected_back: Lane control signals are mounted over the lane they govern and set the direction of travel in a lane that carries one direction at some times and the opposite direction at others.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.front: Why must you never drive beneath an overhead red X lane control light?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.expected_back: A red X over a lane means you must not use that lane because traffic in the opposite direction is using it.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.front: What do an overhead downward green pointer and a steady yellow X tell drivers in a reversible lane?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.expected_back: A green arrow lane control signal means you may use that lane, and a steady yellow X means you must move out of the lane because it is about to carry traffic in the opposite direction.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.front: For what single maneuver may you enter a lane beneath a flashing yellow X?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.expected_back: When the yellow X lane control signal is flashing, you may use that lane only while preparing to turn left.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.front: How does a steady yellow X overhead differ from a flashing yellow X overhead?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.expected_back: A steady yellow X orders you out of the lane, while a flashing yellow X permits the lane only for preparing a left turn.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.front: How does an overhead red X lane light differ in meaning from an intersection red turn pointer?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.expected_back: A red X lane control signal means the lane belongs to opposing traffic, while a red arrow means stop for that lane just as a red light would.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.front: What do lighted red and yellow turn lenses mean for the specific lane they control?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.expected_back: Lighted arrows are sometimes used to control turns from a specific lane, and a red arrow or a yellow arrow carries the same meaning as a red or yellow light for that lane.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.front: What movement rule applies when your lane receives a lighted green directional pointer?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.expected_back: A green arrow has the same meaning as a green light for its lane, but you must turn or proceed only in the direction the arrow points.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.front: How do combination signal heads work across multiple lanes, and what rule governs a lit green pointer?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.expected_back: Combination signals pair arrows with standard lights to control every lane, the colors and arrows keep their usual meanings, and when a green arrow is lighted you must move only in the direction it indicates.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.front: Whom do pedestrian lights govern, and which words and icons do they display?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.expected_back: Pedestrian signals control only pedestrian movements and use the lighted words WALK and DON'T WALK together with the symbols of a walking person and an upraised palm.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.front: How does a steady DON'T WALK or raised palm differ from a flashing one for pedestrians?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.expected_back: A steady DON'T WALK or upraised palm means pedestrians must not enter the roadway toward the signal, while a flashing one means no one may start crossing but anyone already crossing may continue to the nearest sidewalk, traffic island or safety zone.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.front: What does a steady WALK or walking-person icon mean compared with a flashing WALK?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.expected_back: A steady WALK or walking person means pedestrians may cross toward the signal, and a flashing WALK or walking person is sometimes used to warn of a possible conflict between pedestrians and vehicles.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.front: For someone already halfway across the street, how does flashing DON'T WALK differ from steady DON'T WALK?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.expected_back: A flashing DON'T WALK lets pedestrians already crossing finish, while a steady DON'T WALK forbids entering the roadway toward the signal.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.front: What extra alert does a flashing WALK add beyond a steady WALK?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.expected_back: A flashing WALK warns of a possible pedestrian-vehicle conflict, while a steady WALK simply permits crossing toward the signal.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.front: What is the main purpose of traffic lights, and at what kinds of spots are they installed?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.expected_back: Traffic signals exist mainly to direct and regulate traffic, and they are installed at intersections and other places where the flow of traffic must be interrupted.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.front: Where do engineers place standard red-yellow-green three-color traffic lights?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.expected_back: Standard three-color signals are used mainly to stop and release traffic at locations with considerable conflict between vehicle movements.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.front: What three main jobs do traffic signs perform, and which visual features carry their meaning?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.expected_back: Traffic signs tell you what actions you must take, warn you of possible hazards, and identify routes and locations, and their meaning is carried by color and shape as well as by words, letters, numbers and silhouettes.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.front: What does the color red communicate on a traffic sign, and is red limited to one sign shape?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.expected_back: The color red on a sign means an action is prohibited, and red appears on signs of various shapes.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.front: What hazards and shapes belong to yellow traffic signs compared with orange traffic signs?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.expected_back: Yellow on a sign warns of hazardous or dangerous conditions and almost always appears on a diamond-shaped sign, while orange warns of road work and appears on rectangular or diamond-shaped signs.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.front: What shape and meaning belong to black-and-white signs, and which three colors mark guide signs?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.expected_back: Black and white signs indicate a required action and are always rectangular, while green, blue and brown are used on guide and information signs, mostly rectangular as well.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.front: How does a yellow sign differ from an orange sign in both meaning and shape?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.expected_back: Yellow warns of hazardous or dangerous conditions and almost always appears on a diamond-shaped sign, while orange warns of road work on rectangular or diamond-shaped signs.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.front: How do black-and-white signs contrast with red signs in both action and outline shape?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.expected_back: Black and white signs command an action and are always rectangular, while red signs prohibit an action and come in various shapes.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.front: How many sides and what colors identify a stop sign, and what must you always do there?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.expected_back: A stop sign is an eight-sided white-on-red sign meaning other traffic has the right of way, so you must always come to a complete stop and yield to approaching traffic before proceeding.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.front: Where do you make your first stop at a stop sign, and what if cross-traffic is hidden from view?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.expected_back: At a stop sign you stop at the stop line, or before the marked or unmarked crosswalk if there is no stop line, and if you cannot see traffic from that first stop you move ahead slowly and stop again where you can see approaching traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.front: What shape and colors mark a yield sign, and when must you come to a full stop?
