sec09-card-sec09-F07.expected_back: A yield sign is a triangular red and white sign meaning other traffic has the right of way, so be ready to stop, but you need to stop only when other traffic actually holds the right of way.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.front: What is the exact stopping difference between a stop sign and a yield sign?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.expected_back: A stop sign always demands a complete stop, while a yield sign demands a stop only when other traffic holds the right of way.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.front: At a stop sign with no painted stop line and a blocked view, where do you stop first and second?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.expected_back: At a stop sign without a stop line you stop before the crosswalk, and when the view is blocked you creep forward and stop a second time where you can see traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.front: What shape is a Do Not Pass sign, and what road locations does it mark?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.expected_back: Do not pass signs are rectangular signs marking places on two- or three-lane roads where you must not pass another vehicle.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.front: What shape, colors, and roadside placement distinguish a No Passing Zone sign?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.expected_back: A no passing zone sign is a pennant-shaped yellow and black sign that supplements the do not pass sign, and it stands on the left side of the road pointing to the start of the no-passing zone.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.front: What does a rectangular black-and-white Pass With Care sign announce?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.expected_back: A pass with care sign is a rectangular black and white sign marking the end of a no-passing zone.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.front: How does the role of a rectangular Do Not Pass sign differ from the left-side pennant?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.expected_back: A do not pass sign is a rectangle marking the no-passing stretch itself, while the no passing zone pennant on the left merely points to where that stretch begins.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.front: How do Do Not Pass and No Passing Zone signs differ in shape, color, placement, and job?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.expected_back: A rectangular Do Not Pass sign marks locations on two-lane or three-lane roads where passing is forbidden, while a yellow and black pennant-shaped No Passing Zone sign on the left side of the road points to the start of a no-passing zone.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.front: What limits can rectangular black-and-white speed signs set, and how must you drive within them?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.expected_back: Speed limit signs are rectangular black and white signs that show the established maximum and minimum limits, which may apply only at certain times, under certain conditions or to certain kinds of vehicles, and you must drive neither faster than the maximum nor slower than the minimum.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.front: What should you do at a Reduced Speed Ahead sign, and where does the lower limit take legal effect?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.expected_back: A reduced speed ahead sign has the same color and shape as a speed limit sign and gives advance notice to begin slowing, and the new lower limit takes effect at the next speed limit sign.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.front: What do black-and-white lane use control signs show, and what rule applies to your lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.expected_back: Lane use control signs are rectangular black and white signs showing that turns are required or unusual turns are permitted from specific lanes at an intersection, and you must move only in the direction shown for your lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.front: What is the purpose of black-and-white alignment signs along a roadway?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.expected_back: Other alignment signs are rectangular black and white signs showing where you must drive so traffic moves safely and smoothly.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.front: What visual symbols identify exclusion signs, and what do they restrict?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.expected_back: Exclusion signs are rectangular and show either a red circle on white or a red circle with a red diagonal slash on black and white, and they restrict or prohibit vehicles, vehicle movements or other activities.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.front: What colors and shape mark worded regulatory signs that govern parking, weights, and vehicle types?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.expected_back: The many other regulatory signs are all rectangular with black or red lettering on a white background, and they restrict people, vehicles, weights, vehicle types, parking and similar matters.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.front: How does a Reduced Speed Ahead sign differ legally from the speed limit sign that follows it?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.expected_back: A reduced speed ahead sign only tells you to start slowing, while the speed limit sign after it is where the lower limit actually takes effect.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.front: How do exclusion signs communicate restrictions differently from other worded regulatory signs?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.expected_back: An exclusion sign uses a red circle, with or without a diagonal slash, to prohibit a movement or activity, while other regulatory signs use black or red lettering on white to state restrictions in words.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.front: What do roadway warning signs alert you to, and how should you respond?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.expected_back: Warning signs alert you to dangers that exist or may exist on or near the road, so be prepared to take safe and proper action when you see one.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.front: What do most warning signs look like, and which common road hazards do Hawaii's examples include?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.expected_back: Most warning signs are yellow diamonds carrying a black border and black symbols or words, and the examples pictured include divided highway, divided highway ends, hill, slippery when wet, pedestrian crossing, and lane ends or road narrows.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.front: Which two meanings can the five-sided school warning carry, and what upcoming intersection control has its own warning?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.expected_back: One warning sign can mean either school crossing or school zone, and another warns of a traffic signal ahead.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.front: What two groups do construction traffic-control devices protect, and what is their basic color?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.expected_back: Construction and maintenance work areas use traffic control devices to guide drivers and pedestrians safely through the work zone and to protect highway workers, and orange is the basic color of these devices.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.front: Which seven traffic-control devices and personnel are most commonly used in work zones?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.expected_back: The most common work zone devices are signs, barricades, drums, cones, tubes, flashing arrow panels and flagpersons.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.front: What do construction and maintenance signs warn about, and which shapes do they use?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.expected_back: Construction and maintenance signs notify drivers of unusual or potentially dangerous conditions in or near work areas, most are diamond-shaped and a few are rectangular.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.front: Which five channelizing devices guide traffic through work zones, and what is added to them at night?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.expected_back: Barricades, vertical panels, drums, cones and tubes are the channelizing devices most often used to alert drivers to work zone hazards and guide them through, and at night they often carry flashing or steady burning lights.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.front: How do diagonal stripes on a barricade or vertical panel tell you which side to pass on?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.expected_back: The diagonal stripes on a barricade or vertical panel point the way traffic should pass, with stripes sloping down to the right meaning bear right and stripes sloping down to the left meaning bear left.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.front: What two messages do large flashing or sequencing arrow panels give drivers day and night?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.expected_back: Large flashing or sequencing arrow panels are used in work zones day and night to guide drivers into certain lanes and to show that part of the road ahead is closed.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.front: What clothing do work-zone flagpersons wear, and what tools do they use to direct traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.expected_back: Flagpersons stop, slow or guide traffic through work zones, wear orange vests, shirts or jackets, and direct traffic with red flags or stop and slow paddles.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.front: What is the exact directional difference between barricade stripes sloping down right versus down left?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.expected_back: Barricade stripes sloping downward to the right mean bear right, while stripes sloping downward to the left mean bear left.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.front: How does a flashing arrow panel's job differ from a flagperson's job in a work zone?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.expected_back: A flashing arrow panel steers drivers into a lane or announces a closure, while a flagperson with a flag or paddle stops, slows or guides traffic in person.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.front: Which four kinds of travel information are covered by guide and information signs?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.expected_back: Guide and information signs cover everything about your location and the location of places and services, including route markers, location and distance signs, park and recreation signs, and service information signs.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.front: How do green, blue, and brown guide signs differ in purpose from yellow warning signs?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.expected_back: Guide and information signs in green, blue or brown locate places and services, while warning signs in yellow describe hazards.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.front: What happens to your license, what temporary permit is issued, and what right do you have if you test at point zero eight or higher or refuse testing?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.expected_back: Under administrative license revocation your license is taken away and you receive a thirty-day temporary driving permit if a test shows a blood alcohol content of point zero eight or more or if you refuse the test, and anyone whose license is revoked may request a hearing.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.front: What blood alcohol limit applies to drivers under age twenty-one under Hawaii's zero tolerance rule?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.expected_back: Under the zero tolerance rule a driver under twenty-one may not operate a motor vehicle with a blood alcohol content of point zero two or more.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.front: At what blood alcohol percentages is a Hawaii driver considered impaired versus under the influence?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.expected_back: When a test shows alcohol in the blood, a driver is considered impaired at a blood alcohol content above point zero five percent but below point zero eight percent, and under the influence at point zero eight percent or more.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.front: How does Hawaii distinguish between being impaired and being under the influence by blood alcohol level?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.expected_back: A blood alcohol content above point zero five but below point zero eight makes a driver impaired, while point zero eight or more makes the driver under the influence.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.front: How does the adult administrative revocation level compare with the underage zero tolerance level?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.expected_back: The adult threshold for administrative revocation is point zero eight, while the zero tolerance threshold for drivers under twenty-one is point zero two.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.front: What revocation rule do a failed test and a refused test share, and what extra penalty hits a refusal?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.expected_back: A failed test and a refused test both trigger administrative revocation with a thirty-day temporary permit, while refusal adds a one, two or four year revocation based on prior alcohol enforcement contacts.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.front: What core prohibition does Hawaii law enforce regarding intoxicants and motor vehicles?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.expected_back: Hawaii prohibits operating a motor vehicle while under the influence of intoxicants.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.front: What have you already agreed to under implied consent simply by driving on Hawaii's public highways?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.expected_back: Under implied consent, anyone who operates a motor vehicle on Hawaii's public highways is deemed to have consented to a test of the amount of alcohol in the blood.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.front: For how many years can your license be revoked if you refuse an officer's alcohol test request?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.expected_back: A police officer who believes a driver is under the influence may request a test, and refusing can bring license revocation for one year, two years or four years depending on the driver's prior alcohol enforcement contacts.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.front: Does refusing an alcohol test block an impaired-driving charge, and how can taking the test help an innocent driver?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.expected_back: A driver who refuses the test may still be charged with driving under the influence, and the test can also prove that a driver is not under the influence.

sec11-card-sec11-R09.front: How does implied consent relate to administrative license revocation?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.expected_back: Implied consent means every driver has already agreed to be tested, while administrative revocation is what follows when the test is failed or refused.

sec11-card-sec11-R10.front: What two opposite outcomes can a blood-alcohol test prove, and why is refusing futile against charges?
sec11-card-sec11-R10.expected_back: A test can convict a driver by showing alcohol, while it can also clear a driver by showing none, and refusing it does not prevent a driving under the influence charge.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.front: Is alcohol a stimulant or a depressant, how does it hurt driving skills, and why might drinkers feel energized?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.expected_back: Alcohol is a depressant, not a stimulant; it slows reflexes, interferes with judgment, reduces alertness and impairs vision, and any feeling of stimulation comes only from lowered inhibitions that cost you caution and self-control.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.front: Does switching among beer, wine, or whiskey change impairment risk?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.expected_back: It makes no difference whether you drink beer, wine, whiskey or another beverage, because the amount of alcohol that reaches your blood is what causes the problem.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.front: How does drinking on an empty stomach compare with drinking after a recent meal?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.expected_back: Alcohol can affect you differently at different times, and a small amount on an empty stomach acts more rapidly than it would after a recent meal.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.front: Why do black coffee, food, or cold showers fail to sober you up, and what actually removes blood alcohol?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.expected_back: Once alcohol is in your blood nothing can lessen its effect; black coffee, food or a cold shower may wake you up but will not sober you up, because only time lets the liver burn the alcohol and the kidneys and lungs eliminate it.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.front: Why does alcohol's true physical effect contradict the lively feeling many drinkers experience?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.expected_back: Alcohol depresses reflexes, judgment, alertness and vision, while the stimulated feeling after drinking is only the loss of inhibition.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.front: How does eating food before drinking differ in effect from eating food, drinking coffee, or showering afterward?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.expected_back: Food eaten before drinking slows how fast alcohol acts, while food, coffee or a cold shower taken afterward does nothing to remove alcohol already in the blood.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.front: Where outdoors in public is consuming or possessing an alcoholic beverage illegal?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.expected_back: Consuming or possessing an alcoholic beverage anywhere on a public highway or a public sidewalk is illegal.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.front: Where inside a motor vehicle is keeping an opened alcoholic beverage container illegal on a public road?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.expected_back: Keeping an opened alcoholic beverage container in the part of a motor vehicle normally occupied by the driver or passengers is prohibited on any public road.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.front: How does Hawaii's public-drinking ban differ from its vehicle open-container ban?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.expected_back: Consuming or possessing alcohol on a public highway or sidewalk is illegal, while keeping an opened container in the passenger area of a vehicle is a separate prohibition on public roads.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.front: What should you ask your doctor before driving on any prescription or non-prescription medicine?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.expected_back: Many drugs interfere with safe driving, including some in medicines your doctor prescribes and some in medicines sold without a prescription, so ask your doctor about any driving-related effects before taking a medicine.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.front: Which two common over-the-counter remedies often contain ingredients that impair driving?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.expected_back: Some over-the-counter allergy remedies and cold pills contain ingredients that can affect your driving ability.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.front: How do stimulant amphetamines and sedative or tranquilizer overdoses affect driving and survival?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.expected_back: Amphetamines, found in stimulants and diet pills and known on the illegal market as pep pills and speed, and overdoses of tranquilizers or sedatives known as downers, greatly impair driving and can by themselves cause death.

sec11-card-sec11-F20.front: Why must you never combine alcohol with prescription, over-the-counter, or other drugs?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.expected_back: Combining alcohol with drugs can produce a far stronger effect than either one alone, so never mix alcohol and drugs.

sec11-card-sec11-F21.front: How do illegal drugs like hallucinogens, heroin, and cocaine affect awareness, and what driving rule applies?
sec11-card-sec11-F21.expected_back: Some of the most dangerous drugs, such as LSD, heroin and cocaine, can be obtained only illegally, they can make users completely unaware of or indifferent to their surroundings, and anyone under their influence must not try to drive.

sec11-card-sec11-F22.front: Why is every drug sold on the illegal market inherently dangerous?
sec11-card-sec11-F22.expected_back: Every drug on the illegal market is dangerous because there is no way to be certain of its strength or purity.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.front: How do pharmacy medicines like cold and allergy pills compare in effect with illegal drugs like heroin or cocaine?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.expected_back: Prescription and over-the-counter medicines such as allergy and cold pills can impair driving, while illegal drugs such as LSD, heroin and cocaine can leave a user unaware of the surroundings altogether.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.front: How do amphetamines contrast with tranquilizers and sedatives, and what danger do overdoses of both share?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.expected_back: Amphetamines are stimulants sold illegally as pep pills and speed, while tranquilizers and sedatives are downers, and an overdose of either can be fatal on its own.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.front: Roughly how many fatal crashes and what share of United States traffic deaths involve alcohol each year?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.expected_back: Alcohol is a factor in more than eighteen thousand fatal motor vehicle crashes every year in the United States, about forty percent of the total, and that is every driver's problem whether or not the driver drinks.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.front: Why does the drinking-driver problem include ordinary social drinkers and even people taking alcohol-containing medicine?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.expected_back: The drinking-driver problem reaches far beyond alcoholics; anyone who drives after taking alcohol, even the alcohol in a medicine, is part of it, because alcohol and other drugs cloud judgment and make people misjudge their own intoxication.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.front: Which three commitments make up your personal share of solving the impaired-driving problem?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.expected_back: A large share of the solution rests with you as a driver: understand what alcohol and other drugs do to you, know your limits and stay within them, and do not drive after taking an intoxicant.

sec12-card-sec12-F25.front: When must safety belts be worn, and in what four ways do they protect everyone in a crash?
sec12-card-sec12-F25.expected_back: Safety belts must be worn at all times when driving or riding, and they protect you by keeping you from being thrown from the car, from striking the windshield or interior, from injuring others by being thrown against them, and from being thrown out of the driver's seat where you control the vehicle.

sec12-card-sec12-F26.front: How deadly is ejection, up to what speed can belts make crashes survivable, and how slow can an unbelted crash kill?
sec12-card-sec12-F26.expected_back: Being thrown from the car makes death five times more likely, lap and shoulder belts make a crash survivable at speeds up to sixty miles per hour, and an unbelted occupant can be killed at speeds as low as twelve miles per hour.

sec12-card-sec12-F28.front: How should your lap belt and shoulder belt fit, and when do modern belts lock?
sec12-card-sec12-F28.expected_back: A lap belt should fit snugly across the hip bones and lower abdomen, the shoulder belt should be just loose enough to fit your fist between the belt and your chest, and belts in late-model vehicles allow body movement and lock only on impact.

sec12-card-sec12-F29.front: Why must small children use dedicated child seats rather than riding in someone's lap or standing on a seat?
sec12-card-sec12-F29.expected_back: Children too small for regular belts need special child seats, no person is strong enough to hold even a small infant in a crash or sudden stop, a child must never ride in someone's lap or stand on a seat, and the five seconds it takes to buckle up can save years of severe handicap.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.front: How does proper tightness for a lap belt differ from proper slack for a shoulder belt?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.expected_back: The lap belt sits snug across the hip bones, while the shoulder belt stays loose enough to admit a fist between belt and chest.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.front: How does the top survivable crash speed with belts compare against the lowest fatal crash speed without belts?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.expected_back: Belts make a crash survivable up to sixty miles per hour, while going unbelted can be fatal at only twelve miles per hour.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.front: What does defensive driving mean, what risky road users do you guard against, and whom must you guard against first?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.expected_back: Defensive driving means identifying dangerous situations and acting against the danger before a crash situation develops, defending against aggressive, careless, inattentive, impulsive, ignorant and intoxicated drivers and pedestrians, and first defending against yourself if you show any of those traits.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.front: Which five habits does a defensive driver practice to prevent crashes?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.memory_hook: Moving eyes, look-ahead, escape, space, speed
sec12-card-sec12-F16.expected_back: To avoid crashes a defensive driver stays alert with eyes moving, looks well ahead to anticipate chain-reaction situations, keeps an alternate plan and a way out, maintains proper following distance, and maintains proper speed for all highway conditions.

sec12-card-sec12-F17.front: Where does almost all safe-driving information come from, where should you focus extra attention, and how does speed affect vision?
sec12-card-sec12-F17.expected_back: Almost all the information needed to drive safely comes from looking and seeing, with constant awareness of conditions near the vehicle and special attention to conditions a considerable distance ahead, and speed reduces your field of vision.

sec12-card-sec12-F18.front: Where should your scanning pattern place attention, and what do post-crash claims of not seeing really mean?
sec12-card-sec12-F18.expected_back: Seeing should occupy your whole attention, using a scanning pattern that keeps most attention ahead with regular glances to the sides, the rear-view mirror and the instrument panel, because crash statements that begin with I did not see usually mean I was not paying attention.

sec12-card-sec12-R08.front: How does defending against other drivers connect with checking your own behavior?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.expected_back: Defensive driving defends against other drivers' aggression, carelessness and intoxication, while a driver who shows those traits must first defend against himself.

sec12-card-sec12-R09.front: How does proper defensive scanning differ from sightseeing, daydreaming, or looking inside the cabin?
sec12-card-sec12-R09.expected_back: Scanning keeps most attention far ahead with regular glances aside, in the mirror and at the panel, while sightseeing, daydreaming and looking inside the vehicle are the distractions it excludes.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.front: How should you handle distracting tasks like eating, grooming, reading, music changes, or tending kids and pets?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.expected_back: Anything that takes your attention from driving can lead to a poor choice, so avoid eating, drinking, phoning, writing, reading, smoking, grooming, changing music, looking at things outside or inside the vehicle, talking to passengers, dealing with children or pets, applying makeup or shaving, and handle such things before you start or pull over safely first.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.front: How loud may your stereo be, and what is Hawaii's rule on headsets or earphones while driving?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.expected_back: Keep the stereo low enough to hear sirens, horns and screeching tires outside the vehicle, and never drive with headsets or earphones covering or inserted in both ears, because they make emergency horns and sirens too hard to hear.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.front: Why does even hands-free phone talk hurt driving, where should calls happen, and how should pets ride?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.expected_back: Talking on a cell phone pulls attention toward the conversation even with hands-free equipment, so avoid the phone or radio while moving, pull over in a safe place to make a call, and keep pets in a carrier rather than in the driver's lap.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.front: Does using hands-free phone gear make calling safe in motion, or what does the Hawaii manual require?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.expected_back: Hands-free equipment still leaves a phone call distracting, while pulling over in a safe place is the manual's only acceptable way to take the call.

sec12-card-sec12-R12.front: How does the rule on vehicle stereos differ from the rule on headsets covering or inserted in both ears?
sec12-card-sec12-R12.expected_back: Keeping the stereo low preserves your hearing of sirens and horns, while headsets over or in both ears are forbidden outright while driving.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.front: Which five personal traits or shortcomings cause bad driving habits?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.expected_back: Bad driving habits are caused by five things, laziness, impatience, inattention, arrogance and ignorance.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.front: Which two critical safety actions fade away when laziness creeps into a driver's routine?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.expected_back: Laziness shows when the head-turn look behind for traffic before changing lanes, leaving the curb or opening a door on the traffic side shrinks to a mirror glance and then to an occasional check, and when the signal before such moves is dropped, a pair of habits that can cause a first crash.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.front: How does impatience erode proper stopping at stop signs and red lights over time?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.expected_back: Impatience shows when pressure from following vehicles and an empty cross street tempt a driver to make only a good try at stopping at a stop sign or red light, even for a right turn, until the stop becomes a mere slowing down.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.front: Which three aggressive moves mark an impatient driver between stops?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.expected_back: The impatient driver speeds from stop to stop, weaves through traffic and tailgates when blocked, disrupting traffic and raising crash risk without realizing it.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.front: How does physical posture and wheel grip change as a once-alert new driver slips into inattention?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.expected_back: Inattention grows as a new driver who sat up straight with a firm grip and full awareness relaxes, leans back, loosens the grip and lets attention wander, and then the vehicle wanders too.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.front: What telltale behaviors show an inattentive driver with passengers or when driving alone?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.expected_back: The inattentive driver drives with one arm out the window, gestures while talking to passengers, pays little attention to traffic, daydreams or gazes off the road when alone, and forfeits safety through that inattention.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.front: How does an arrogant driver differ from a merely impatient one, and how should you respond to one?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.expected_back: Where the impatient driver is merely in a hurry, the arrogant driver is purposely in a hurry, treats the vehicle as an extension of ego, ignores traffic laws and others' right of way, and should never be competed with or imitated, because there is nothing to gain and too much to lose.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.front: What dangerous errors does an ignorant driver commit, and whom do they usually blame?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.expected_back: The ignorant driver does not know sign meanings, markings, right-of-way rules or safe procedures, turns from the wrong lane, drives too slowly from uncertainty, stops at the end of a freeway on-ramp or crosses markings that prohibit crossing, and usually blames other drivers.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.front: What excuse do drivers with stacked bad habits tell themselves after crashing, and what extra bad habits pile on?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.expected_back: A driver with a combination of bad habits who is in a crash is sure it just happened and was unavoidable, and further bad habits include failing to yield, skipping safety belts, drinking before the drive home, backing without checking that the area is clear, and being distracted by passengers, maps or lighting smoking materials.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.front: How do you build automatic good driving habits, and how does that change trips?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.expected_back: Good driving habits form just as easily as bad ones by deliberately repeating the proper action until it becomes automatic, making trips more enjoyable for you and more comfortable for passengers.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.front: How does any habit become automatic, and why do bad driving habits sneak in over time?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.expected_back: A habit forms when you do the same thing so many times that it becomes automatic, and driving habits form because the same physical actions are repeated over and over while your natural tendency to reduce those actions, without thinking, produces bad habits.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.front: What separates an impatient driver's mindset from an arrogant driver's mindset?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.expected_back: The impatient driver is simply in a hurry, while the arrogant driver is purposely in a hurry and competes with the vehicle as an extension of ego.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.front: How do the telltale signs of laziness differ from the telltale signs of inattention?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.expected_back: Laziness shrinks the look-behind and drops the signal, while inattention loosens the grip and lets the eyes and the vehicle wander.

sec12-card-sec12-F30.front: When a car strikes a solid barrier at thirty miles per hour, how fast does an unbelted occupant keep flying forward?
sec12-card-sec12-F30.expected_back: When a car hits a barrier at thirty miles per hour it crushes and slows, but an unbelted person keeps moving forward inside the car at thirty miles per hour.

sec12-card-sec12-F31.front: In a thirty-mile-per-hour barrier crash, what are the exact fractions of a second for the car stopping and the human collision?
sec12-card-sec12-F31.expected_back: The car stops about one tenth of a second after impact, and about one fiftieth of a second later the unbelted person slams into the dashboard and windshield in the human collision, which takes only one hundredth of a second.

sec12-card-sec12-F32.front: Why do buckled occupants avoid the human collision entirely?
sec12-card-sec12-F32.expected_back: A belted occupant moves forward only until the belts restrain the body, keeping head and chest off the interior, and rides down the collision as part of the car's slower, energy-absorbing stop, so for belted people there is no human collision.

sec12-card-sec12-F27.front: What can unbelted passengers do to infants and small children in a crash, and what happens to an unbelted driver?
sec12-card-sec12-F27.expected_back: In a crash, infants and small children can be crushed to death by occupants who are not wearing seat belts, and the first impact often throws an unbelted driver away from the controls.

sec12-card-sec12-R07.front: How much faster is the unbelted human collision than the car's own barrier stop?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.expected_back: The car's collision takes about one tenth of a second, while the unbelted person's human collision takes about one hundredth of a second and begins one fiftieth of a second after the car stops.

sec12-card-sec12-F23.front: What should dash warning lamps do at startup, and what do lit yellow versus lit red lamps mean afterward?
sec12-card-sec12-F23.expected_back: When the ignition is turned on every warning lamp on the instrument panel should light, a lamp that stays dark is not working, and after the computer check the warnings should go out, with a yellow light that stays on being a warning and a red light meaning danger to be checked immediately.

sec12-card-sec12-F24.front: When should the brake lamp turn off, and what does it mean if it lights when pressing the foot brake?
sec12-card-sec12-F24.expected_back: Releasing the parking brake should turn the brake warning lamp off, and a lamp that comes on when the foot brake is pressed means the brake system is defective and the vehicle must not be driven.

sec12-card-sec12-F20.front: Which fluids and parts need checking if unchecked within the past week, along with glass and fuel?
sec12-card-sec12-F20.expected_back: Correct any defect affecting safe operation as soon as possible, check or have checked the coolant, oil, battery water, tire condition and pressure and lamps if they have not been checked within the previous week, keep the windshield and windows clean, and make sure there is enough fuel to complete the trip.

sec12-card-sec12-F21.front: Which controls must you locate and test before pulling out in an unfamiliar vehicle?
sec12-card-sec12-F21.memory_hook: Signals, lights, wipers, brakes, gear, horn
sec12-card-sec12-F21.expected_back: In an unfamiliar vehicle, take a few minutes to locate and try the turn and hazard signals, head lamps and beam selector, wipers and washers, brakes, gear selector and horn, and fix any defect before driving.

sec12-card-sec12-R05.front: After the startup computer check finishes, how does a lit yellow dash light differ in urgency from a red one?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.expected_back: A yellow lamp that stays lit after the computer check is a warning, while a red lamp means danger that must be checked immediately.

sec12-card-sec12-R11.front: How do weekly maintenance checks on your regular car differ from pre-drive checks in an unfamiliar car?
sec12-card-sec12-R11.expected_back: Fluids, tires and lamps unchecked within the past week are checked before a trip, while an unfamiliar vehicle calls for a few minutes locating its signals, lights, wipers, brakes, gear selector and horn.

sec12-card-sec12-F19.front: Under which physical or emotional states should you skip driving, and what alternatives should you use?
sec12-card-sec12-F19.expected_back: Do not drive when ill, injured, emotionally upset or under the influence of intoxicants, follow your physician's advice when taking medication, get help from friends or public transportation for a necessary trip, and call the police in an emergency.

sec12-card-sec12-F22.front: What four planning habits apply before driving to an unfamiliar area?
sec12-card-sec12-F22.expected_back: When driving to an unfamiliar area know the exact destination and check it on a map first, choose the route with traffic, road, weather and light conditions in mind, allow enough time, and postpone or cancel the trip if you doubt you can cope comfortably with the conditions.

sec12-card-sec12-F33.front: How must an adult wear the belt, and how must a baby be secured rather than held in someone's arms?
sec12-card-sec12-F33.expected_back: Wear the lap and shoulder belt low and snug, place a baby in a car safety seat using an infant seat or a convertible seat in the infant or toddler position, and never carry a baby in your arms.

sec12-card-sec12-F34.front: Which household items must never replace a car safety seat, and why does legged baby clothing beat a sack sleeper?
sec12-card-sec12-F34.expected_back: A household carrier, travel bed or cloth carrier must not be used in place of a car safety seat, and clothing with legs lets the harness fit snugly while a papoose bunting or sack sleeper does not.

sec12-card-sec12-F35.front: What are the common infant car-seat installation errors, and how should a blanket be used in cold weather?
sec12-card-sec12-F35.expected_back: Common car seat mistakes are an infant facing forward, a harness not used or not snug, and a seat belt in the wrong place, not tight or not used, and in cold weather the baby is not wrapped in a blanket under the harness but has the straps pulled through holes cut in the blanket, which is folded over after buckling.

sec12-card-sec12-R10.front: Which car-seat positions are proper for a baby, and which infant orientation is explicitly listed as wrong?
sec12-card-sec12-R10.expected_back: A baby rides in a car safety seat using an infant seat or a convertible seat in the infant or toddler position, while placing an infant facing forward is listed under ways not to use a seat.

sec15-card-sec15-F18.front: What happens during a tire blowout, what usually causes it, and how often should you inspect tires?
sec15-card-sec15-F18.expected_back: A tire blowout is the sudden release of air that collapses a tire and can cause loss of control, it most often results from poor tire care, so check pressure and condition every month.

sec15-card-sec15-F19.front: Why keep off the brakes in a blowout, and how do you bring the car safely off the road?
sec15-card-sec15-F19.expected_back: In a blowout do not apply the brakes, which can make the vehicle uncontrollable; grip the wheel firmly and steer to stay in your lane against a pull that may go either way, slow gradually without the brakes until very slow, then brake lightly and pull off into a safe area, since a blown tire can be driven slowly for some distance without damaging the rim.

sec15-card-sec15-F20.front: How do you steer a lost wheel to a stop, what failure often accompanies it, and how does it leave?
sec15-card-sec15-F20.expected_back: Losing a wheel is uncommon but is handled like a blowout, partial or total brake failure is likely when it happens, and once stopped the vehicle cannot be moved and must be towed.

sec15-card-sec15-F21.front: Why is total brake failure rare on modern cars, and what two signs reveal partial failure?
sec15-card-sec15-F21.expected_back: Total brake failure is very unlikely on a modern car because the service brake system almost always keeps partial braking, and a partial failure shows as reduced braking and a warning light on the panel.

sec15-card-sec15-F22.front: What four actions stop a vehicle safely if the service brakes fail completely?
sec15-card-sec15-F22.expected_back: If the brakes fail completely, pump the pedal quickly, shift to a lower gear, look for an escape route such as a side road or flat open area while warning others with lights and horn, and apply the parking brake gradually, never rapidly or with great force, until you stop.

sec15-card-sec15-F23.front: When partial power-steering loss strikes, how must you respond at the wheel?
sec15-card-sec15-F23.expected_back: Complete steering failure almost never happens on a well-maintained vehicle, but a partial loss can occur with power steering, in which case you must apply greater effort to the wheel and never give up on steering.

sec15-card-sec15-F24.front: How should you bring the car to a halt if steering ever fails completely?
sec15-card-sec15-F24.expected_back: If the steering fails completely, slowly reduce speed and use the brakes as needed to avoid striking anything, stopping as smoothly as possible.

sec15-card-sec15-R01.front: Contrast your immediate right-foot action in a tire blowout versus complete brake failure?
sec15-card-sec15-R01.expected_back: In a blowout the brakes stay off until the car is very slow, while in a complete brake failure the first move is to pump the pedal quickly.

sec15-card-sec15-R12.front: How do brake impact and moving the vehicle afterward differ between a lost wheel and a blowout?
sec15-card-sec15-R12.expected_back: A lost wheel is handled like a blowout but usually brings brake failure and a tow, while a blowout alone can be driven slowly to safety without rim damage.

sec15-card-sec15-F09.front: Where on a congested freeway entrance lane should you slow or wait, and why not at the tip?
sec15-card-sec15-F09.expected_back: To enter a freeway follow the signs to the correct entrance, and if the entrance lane is congested slow down or stop near its beginning rather than creeping to the end of the entrance lane and stopping, because merging from a stop at the end of the ramp is very difficult and dangerous.

sec15-card-sec15-F10.front: How do you merge from an open entrance lane when the freeway lane is clear versus occupied?
sec15-card-sec15-F10.expected_back: When the entrance lane is clear, signal your merge, accelerate to match freeway traffic, and if the near lane is clear move into it and hold your speed, but if vehicles are coming, slow slightly and move in behind them.

sec15-card-sec15-F11.front: Which freeway lanes carry through traffic near the limit, and who belongs in the right lane?
sec15-card-sec15-F11.expected_back: On the freeway watch all signs, through traffic uses the left or center lanes at or near the posted limit, the right lane is for vehicles that cannot keep up and should stay open as much as possible for entering and leaving traffic, and a right-lane driver leaves space for entering vehicles.

sec15-card-sec15-F12.front: What freeway habits on lane changes, stopping, slowing, and tailgating prevent multi-car pileups?
sec15-card-sec15-F12.expected_back: Avoid lane changes on the freeway, signal well ahead of any you make, use the mirrors and look back first, never stop unless absolutely unavoidable, never slow unnecessarily, and never follow too closely, because freeway rear-end collisions are common and usually involve several vehicles.

sec15-card-sec15-F13.front: What three directional moves are strictly forbidden on a freeway, and how do you reverse direction?
sec15-card-sec15-F13.expected_back: Never cross a freeway center divider, turn around or back up on a freeway; if you must go the other way, drive to the next exit, leave and re-enter in the opposite direction.

sec15-card-sec15-F14.front: Where do you stop in a freeway emergency, may you walk, and how do you help stranded drivers?
sec15-card-sec15-F14.expected_back: For an emergency stop try to reach the next exit, otherwise drive entirely off the roadway as far from traffic as possible, never stand or walk on the freeway, and do not stop to help other drivers in trouble but report them to the proper authorities.

sec15-card-sec15-F15.front: When do you slow down for a freeway exit, and what must you do if you miss it?
sec15-card-sec15-F15.expected_back: To leave the freeway watch the exit signs, signal, move into the exit lane, keep your speed until you are completely on the exit ramp and then slow smoothly, and if you miss your exit never stop or back up but continue to the next exit.

sec15-card-sec15-R03.front: Pair the lawful fix for missing a freeway exit with needing the opposite freeway direction?
sec15-card-sec15-R03.expected_back: A missed freeway exit means continuing to the next exit, while needing the opposite direction means leaving at the next exit and re-entering, never crossing the divider or turning around.

sec15-card-sec15-R04.front: Compare how you handle a backed-up freeway entrance lane versus a wide-open one?
sec15-card-sec15-R04.expected_back: A congested entrance lane calls for slowing or stopping near its beginning, while a clear entrance lane calls for signaling and accelerating to match freeway speed before merging.

sec15-card-sec15-R10.front: Contrast the role of left and center freeway lanes with the right-hand lane?
sec15-card-sec15-R10.expected_back: Through freeway traffic uses the left and center lanes near the posted limit, while the right lane is for slower vehicles and for entering and leaving traffic.

sec15-card-sec15-F31.front: What driving inputs trigger most skids, and how quickly must you respond when one starts?
sec15-card-sec15-F31.expected_back: Most skids come from sudden changes of direction or speed, with excessive speed for road and traffic conditions the most common cause, so take extra care on wet, slippery or gravel-covered surfaces and correct a skid immediately and smoothly before control is lost.

sec15-card-sec15-F32.front: What should your feet do immediately when a skid or control loss begins?
sec15-card-sec15-F32.expected_back: When a skid or control problem starts, stop or reduce whatever you were doing when it began, avoid the brakes and release them if braking started the skid, and ease off the accelerator, which may end the skid by itself.

sec15-card-sec15-F33.front: Which direction and how firmly do you turn the steering wheel to recover from a rear-wheel skid?
sec15-card-sec15-F33.expected_back: To steer out of a skid, turn the wheel firmly but not sharply in the direction the rear of the vehicle is sliding, right for a skid to the right and left for a skid to the left, straighten as the skid stops, and if overcorrection starts a skid the other way, steer gently into that skid and repeat until you have control.

sec15-card-sec15-R02.front: Contrast steering out of a skid with recovering after wheels drop off the pavement edge?
sec15-card-sec15-R02.expected_back: In a skid you steer in the direction the rear is sliding and release the brakes, while off the pavement edge you keep straight, slow gently and steer back only at a safe speed.

sec15-card-sec15-F03.front: How do you cut low-sun glare, and which lights belong on during dim dawn or dusk?
sec15-card-sec15-F03.expected_back: When driving toward the rising or setting sun use the sun visors and sunglasses and keep the windshield and windows absolutely clean to cut glare, and in the dim period just before sunrise and after sunset, worse under a cloudy sky, turn on the low-beam head lamps so others can see you and watch for unlighted objects and pedestrians.

sec15-card-sec15-F04.front: How do you prepare your eyes and glass before driving after dark?
sec15-card-sec15-F04.expected_back: No one sees as well at night as in daylight, and alternating light and darkness keeps a driver from reaching full night seeing ability, so protect your eyes from bright light for several hours before a night drive and clean the windshield and windows inside and out.

sec15-card-sec15-F05.front: What three rules govern vehicle lamps, safe speed, and high beams at night?
sec15-card-sec15-F05.expected_back: At night make sure every lamp works, reduce speed so you can stop within the distance you can see ahead, and never use high beams when approaching or following other vehicles.

sec15-card-sec15-F06.front: How do you handle glaring oncoming lights, and what do red lane reflectors warn?
sec15-card-sec15-F06.expected_back: If an approaching vehicle's lights are too bright, flash your high beams once and look toward the right edge of the road, using lane markings or reflectors as a guide, and remember that red lane reflectors mean you are going the wrong way in the lane.

sec15-card-sec15-R05.front: Pair your headlamp rule at dawn or dusk with your response to blinding oncoming high beams?
sec15-card-sec15-R05.expected_back: Before sunrise and after sunset you should turn on low-beam headlamps so others can see you, while if an oncoming vehicle's lights are too bright at night you should flash your high beams once and look toward the right edge of the road.

sec15-card-sec15-F25.front: Why must you never jerk the wheel back onto pavement after dropping onto the shoulder?
sec15-card-sec15-F25.expected_back: If your wheels drop off the pavement edge, do not jerk the wheel to force the vehicle back, because gravel, dirt or the pavement lip resists a smooth return; keep driving with the wheels off the pavement, slow down, brake gently, and at a safe speed steer back onto the pavement ready to correct immediately to stay in your lane.

sec15-card-sec15-F26.front: How do you help a passing driver trapped by oncoming traffic once you read their move?
sec15-card-sec15-F26.expected_back: If a vehicle passing you cannot complete the pass because of oncoming traffic, steer as far right as is safe, even onto the shoulder, and then either slow so the passer can pull in ahead or, if the passer seems to be dropping back, accelerate so it can return behind you, after making sure of the other driver's intention.

sec15-card-sec15-F27.front: What warning and steering escape must you use—and never use—when an oncoming car fills your lane?
sec15-card-sec15-F27.expected_back: If an oncoming vehicle is in your lane, flash your lights and sound the horn, quickly slow and steer right out of the lane into any clear area, even off the road while avoiding solid objects and pedestrians, and never swerve into the oncoming lane.

sec15-card-sec15-R06.front: Compare avoiding a wrong-way car in your lane with helping a trapped overtaker beside you?
sec15-card-sec15-R06.expected_back: An oncoming vehicle in your lane is met by flashing, honking and steering right, while an overtaking vehicle in trouble is helped by steering right and adjusting your speed to its driver's intention.

sec15-card-sec15-F28.front: How does a stuck accelerator behave, and right after what driver action does it often stick?
sec15-card-sec15-F28.expected_back: A stuck accelerator keeps the vehicle at speed or accelerating after your foot is lifted, and it often develops right after the pedal has been pushed fully down.

sec15-card-sec15-F29.front: What pedal, ignition-key, and braking sequence stops a car with a stuck accelerator?
sec15-card-sec15-F29.expected_back: For a stuck accelerator slap the pedal hard, quickly pressing and releasing it, turn the ignition only far enough to stop the engine without engaging the steering lock, expecting heavier steering and braking effort, apply the brakes and pull off into a safe area.

sec15-card-sec15-F30.front: What two mechanical events usually kill power steering, and how do you stop safely?
sec15-card-sec15-F30.expected_back: Power steering failure usually comes with engine failure or a lost drive belt, requires extra effort to keep steering control, and calls for reducing speed and driving to a safe area to stop.

sec15-card-sec15-R07.front: Contrast handling a stuck gas pedal with handling lost power-steering assist?
sec15-card-sec15-R07.expected_back: A stuck accelerator is answered by slapping the pedal and switching the engine off short of the steering lock, while power steering failure is answered simply by extra effort, reduced speed and a safe stop.

sec15-card-sec15-F34.front: What three vehicle problems start most car fires, and how should you treat any burning smell?
sec15-card-sec15-F34.expected_back: Vehicle fires usually start with an engine that has overheated, a short in the electrical system, or a leak of fuel or oil, and any burning odor should be investigated at once.

sec15-card-sec15-F35.front: What must you shut off and where must passengers go immediately if vehicle fire is suspected?
sec15-card-sec15-F35.expected_back: If fire occurs or is suspected, drive to a safe area clear of traffic and stop, turn off the ignition and every electrical switch, and get all occupants out, away from the vehicle and off the roadway because poisonous fumes can fill the vehicle quickly.

sec15-card-sec15-F36.front: How do you smother a small vehicle fire, what liquid is forbidden, and how do you treat big fires?
sec15-card-sec15-F36.expected_back: Smother a small fire with an extinguisher, dirt, sand or a blanket, never use water on a gasoline, oil or electrical fire, and do not try to fight a large gasoline or oil fire but seek assistance.

sec15-card-sec15-F37.front: After a breakdown, where should the car and passengers wait depending on nearby safe ground?
sec15-card-sec15-F37.memory_hook: Clear road, safe ground or inside
sec15-card-sec15-F37.expected_back: Most breakdowns are not dangerous in themselves but can leave the vehicle stalled in a hazardous position, so move it to a safe spot if possible, keep occupants away from traffic by moving them to a reachable safe location, and otherwise keep them inside the vehicle.

sec15-card-sec15-F38.front: What gear warns traffic after a breakdown, how do you greet strangers, and what signals distress?
sec15-card-sec15-F38.expected_back: After a breakdown use hazard lights, flares, warning reflectors and a flashlight, which should always be carried, stay locked in the vehicle until sure of a helper's intentions and ask that the police be notified if in doubt, and signal for help by raising the hood and tying a white cloth to the antenna or door handle.

sec15-card-sec15-F39.front: How do walking rules after a breakdown on an ordinary highway differ from a freeway?
sec15-card-sec15-F39.expected_back: If you must leave a broken-down vehicle, lock it and return as soon as practicable, walk facing traffic and well clear of the roadway if you must walk along a highway, and never walk on a freeway but stay with the vehicle until help arrives.

sec15-card-sec15-R08.front: Contrast tackling a small vehicle fire with facing a large fuel fire or reaching for water?
sec15-card-sec15-R08.expected_back: A small vehicle fire is smothered with an extinguisher, dirt, sand or a blanket, while a large gasoline or oil fire is left to the professionals and water is never used on fuel or electrical fires.

sec15-card-sec15-R09.front: How does waiting after a breakdown on a surface road compare with waiting on a freeway?
sec15-card-sec15-R09.expected_back: After a breakdown occupants stay in the vehicle unless a reachable safe spot exists, while on a freeway no one walks at all and everyone waits with the vehicle.

sec15-card-sec15-F16.front: What three vehicle controls enter every emergency, and what is your golden braking and steering rule?
sec15-card-sec15-F16.expected_back: Every driving emergency involves brakes, steering and power, so stay calm, never slam the brakes into a wheel slide because a sliding vehicle cannot be controlled, and steer toward the least dangerous place available.

sec15-card-sec15-F17.front: How do you apply maximum emergency braking, why wear your seatbelt, and when do you stop steering?
sec15-card-sec15-F17.expected_back: In an emergency apply maximum braking without sliding the wheels, releasing and reapplying the brakes if any wheel slides, which antilock brakes do automatically, wear your belt so you stay in position to control the vehicle, and keep trying to control it even after striking something.

sec15-card-sec15-F01.front: Which three road spots freeze first or hide ice even when surrounding pavement looks clear?
sec15-card-sec15-F01.expected_back: In winter conditions a bridge deck or the road beneath it can ice over while the surrounding road stays clear, shaded stretches hold snow and ice longer, and a shiny patch on the road may be ice.

sec15-card-sec15-F02.front: How should you use your brakes and steering on packed snow or ice?
sec15-card-sec15-F02.expected_back: On packed snow or ice use the brakes very cautiously and intermittently, because locked wheels mean loss of control, and steer into a clear area if a collision seems imminent.

sec15-card-sec15-F07.front: What road design features make freeways safe at high speeds?
sec15-card-sec15-F07.expected_back: Freeways are safe high-speed roads because they have no steep hills or sharp curves to limit sight distance, no stop signs, signals or railroad crossings, and entrances and exits only at planned locations, so their driving has its own procedures.

sec15-card-sec15-F08.front: What route details and four vehicle items must you check before entering a freeway?
sec15-card-sec15-F08.expected_back: Plan a freeway trip with a map, knowing exactly where you will enter and leave, and make sure the vehicle has enough gasoline, oil, water and good tires, because service stations are off the freeway and a breakdown on the freeway can create an extremely dangerous situation.

sec15-card-sec15-R11.front: How does manual threshold emergency braking relate to what antilock brakes do?
sec15-card-sec15-R11.expected_back: Emergency braking is maximum pressure released whenever a wheel slides, while antilock brakes perform that release automatically.

sec16-card-sec16-F21.front: What driver error causes over two-thirds of collisions between cars and motorcycles?
sec16-card-sec16-F21.expected_back: Motorcycle riders are friends, relatives and neighbors, motorcycles are fuel and space efficient, but riders are more vulnerable to injury in a crash, and research shows that over two-thirds of car and motorcycle crashes result from a car driver turning in front of the motorcyclist.

sec16-card-sec16-F22.front: How does a motorcycle's narrow profile trick your eyes on distance and speed, and how should you look?
sec16-card-sec16-F22.expected_back: A motorcycle's narrow silhouette and short length can make it seem farther away and slower than it really is, so a car driver should take a second and a third look, because the small size also makes it harder to spot and some riders cut between cars into places where drivers cannot see them.

sec16-card-sec16-F23.front: What two things must you actively confirm about any motorcycle before turning or entering an intersection?
sec16-card-sec16-F23.expected_back: Before starting a turn or entering an intersection, confirm that you have actually seen any motorcycle and judged its speed.

sec16-card-sec16-F27.front: Where do car-and-motorcycle crashes happen most often, and why?
sec16-card-sec16-F27.expected_back: Intersections are the most likely places for car and motorcycle collisions, usually because the car driver does not see the motorcycle and turns into its path.

sec16-card-sec16-F28.front: Why shouldn't you trust a rider's lane shift or flashing turn signal until a turn clearly begins?
sec16-card-sec16-F28.expected_back: A rider moves to one side of the lane to prepare for a turn or to avoid an unseen hazard, so never assume the rider's intention until the maneuver is unmistakably started, and remember that motorcycle turn signals do not cancel automatically and riders sometimes forget to switch them off.

sec16-card-sec16-R10.front: Pair why riders face higher injury risk with the top cause behind over two-thirds of car-bike crashes?
sec16-card-sec16-R10.expected_back: Motorcyclists are more vulnerable to injury than car drivers in a crash, while over two thirds of crashes between cars and motorcycles happen when a car driver turns in front of the motorcyclist.

sec16-card-sec16-R04.front: How do a motorcycle's small size and high agility create two opposite visual traps?
sec16-card-sec16-R04.expected_back: A motorcycle's small size makes it look farther away and slower than it is, while its maneuverability lets it appear suddenly in places a driver cannot see.

sec16-card-sec16-R05.front: Contrast what a rider's lane shift or blinking lamp might mean with what actually proves a turn?
sec16-card-sec16-R05.expected_back: A rider moving to one side of the lane may be preparing a turn or dodging a hazard, while a blinking motorcycle signal may be a forgotten one, so only an unmistakably started maneuver reveals intent.

sec16-card-sec16-F04.front: How does a truck or bus driver's forward view compare with side and immediate rear visibility?
sec16-card-sec16-F04.expected_back: A large vehicle's high driving position gives better forward visibility, but visibility to the sides and rear is severely limited, other traffic is seen only through mirrors, and the area immediately behind the vehicle cannot be seen at all.

sec16-card-sec16-F05.front: What two physical dimensions must large-vehicle drivers account for when turning, shifting lanes, or backing?
sec16-card-sec16-F05.expected_back: Drivers of large vehicles must allow for their greater width and length when turning, changing lanes or backing.

sec16-card-sec16-F06.front: Where should car drivers position themselves near a large truck or bus, and why?
sec16-card-sec16-F06.expected_back: Other drivers should give a large vehicle extra space for its maneuvers, and when near one should stay where its driver can see them and where their own view of traffic is not blocked, because large vehicles need more room to turn.

sec16-card-sec16-F07.front: Why must you leave generous space before merging ahead of a large truck or crossing its path?
sec16-card-sec16-F07.expected_back: Large vehicles need greater stopping distances, so their drivers allow for it and other drivers must allow for it too when changing lanes in front of them or at intersections.

sec16-card-sec16-F08.front: How quickly do large vehicles accelerate and maneuver, and how does that affect passing them?
sec16-card-sec16-F08.expected_back: Large vehicles accelerate very slowly and cannot maneuver as quickly as other vehicles, and they may travel below the posted limit, so use caution when approaching or passing them.

sec16-card-sec16-F09.front: How do large-truck drivers prevent downhill brake fade, and what should car drivers watch for?
sec16-card-sec16-F09.expected_back: Continuous braking to control speed on a downgrade makes brakes ineffective, which is more dangerous for large vehicles, so their drivers shift to a lower gear before a steep descent and other drivers should stay alert for overtaking large vehicles and move out of their way.

sec16-card-sec16-F10.front: What aerodynamic force hits smaller cars approaching or passing fast-moving trucks and buses?
sec16-card-sec16-F10.expected_back: Large fast-moving vehicles create wind gusts strong enough to push a smaller vehicle off its line, so drivers of smaller vehicles should be ready to correct their steering when approaching or passing large vehicles near top speed.

sec16-card-sec16-R01.front: Contrast what a big-rig driver sees ahead with what can be seen along the sides and tail?
sec16-card-sec16-R01.expected_back: A large vehicle's driver sees farther ahead than a car driver, while the sides, the rear and especially the area immediately behind are blind except through mirrors.

sec16-card-sec16-R07.front: Combine the four handling limits of large vehicles that demand extra following and passing space?
sec16-card-sec16-R07.expected_back: Large vehicles need more distance to stop and more room to turn, while they also accelerate slowly and may travel below the limit, so both following and passing need extra margin.

sec16-card-sec16-R08.front: Pair a large truck's steep-downgrade hazard with its high-speed passing hazard for small cars?
sec16-card-sec16-R08.expected_back: A large vehicle's downgrade danger is brake fade, answered by a lower gear, while its slipstream danger is a wind gust that pushes smaller vehicles sideways.

sec16-card-sec16-F24.front: Which portion of a lane do motorcyclists often prefer, and why do they shift across it?
sec16-card-sec16-F24.expected_back: A motorcyclist's position in the lane changes with conditions, often riding in the left portion of the lane to see better and be more visible, but moving to the center or the right side to avoid traffic or be seen.

sec16-card-sec16-F25.front: Why might a motorcyclist swerve abruptly inside their lane over surfaces a car barely feels?
sec16-card-sec16-F25.expected_back: Minor hazards such as potholes or railroad tracks that a car ignores can be major problems for a motorcycle, so the rider shifts position within the lane to gain distance from them, sometimes suddenly, and motorists must be alert for those quick changes.

sec16-card-sec16-F26.front: Why is sharing a traffic lane side-by-side with a motorcycle forbidden?
sec16-card-sec16-F26.expected_back: Respect a motorcycle's space and position, because motorcycles are allowed the full width of a lane to maneuver, and never share a lane with a motorcyclist, since that restricts the rider's ability to avoid hazards.

sec16-card-sec16-F29.front: What is the minimum following gap behind a motorcycle, and why add even more cushion?
sec16-card-sec16-F29.expected_back: Allow at least a two-second following distance behind a motorcycle so the rider has room to maneuver or stop, and increase the gap further because a motorcycle's speed and distance are hard to judge and sudden braking must be avoided.

sec16-card-sec16-F30.front: When do both riders and motorists make more bad choices, raising motorcycle injury risk?
sec16-card-sec16-F30.expected_back: Riders and drivers both make more wrong decisions when stopping distance or the ability to see and react is short, and a rider's injury risk rises when forced to avoid obstacles ahead or when a driver follows too closely.

sec16-card-sec16-F31.front: How should you drive while a motorcyclist is overtaking your car?
sec16-card-sec16-F31.expected_back: Passing rules are similar for motorcycles, so a motorist being overtaken by a motorcycle keeps lane position and speed and lets the rider complete the pass and settle into proper lane position quickly.

sec16-card-sec16-F32.front: How much lane space do you give when passing a motorcycle, and why wait before returning?
sec16-card-sec16-F32.expected_back: When passing a motorcycle give it a full lane, never crowd into its lane, and do not return to the original lane too soon, because that can force the rider to swerve right into traffic or off the road.

sec16-card-sec16-R06.front: Contrast your duty when a motorcycle passes you with your duty when passing a motorcycle?
sec16-card-sec16-R06.expected_back: When a motorcycle passes you, you hold your lane and speed, while when you pass a motorcycle you give it a full lane and do not return early.

sec16-card-sec16-R09.front: Distinguish the baseline time gap behind a motorcycle from the recommended cushion?
sec16-card-sec16-R09.expected_back: Two seconds is the minimum gap behind a motorcycle, while an even larger gap is advised because the rider's speed and distance are hard to judge.

sec16-card-sec16-F14.front: What mirror equipment is required when a towed trailer blocks your inside rearview mirror?
sec16-card-sec16-F14.expected_back: If a trailer is large enough to block the view through the inside rear-view mirror, the towing car must have outside mirrors of proper size on both sides.

sec16-card-sec16-F15.front: Which two weight thresholds require a loaded trailer to carry independent brakes and breakaway protection?
sec16-card-sec16-F15.expected_back: A loaded trailer that weighs more than half the weight of the towing vehicle, or three thousand pounds or more, must have its own brakes and breakaway protection.

sec16-card-sec16-F16.front: What rules govern passengers riding inside utility trailers versus house trailers?
sec16-card-sec16-F16.expected_back: Passengers should not ride in trailers, and riding in a house trailer is prohibited.

sec16-card-sec16-F17.front: Where must trailer safety chains attach, and where must they never attach?
sec16-card-sec16-F17.expected_back: A trailer must have safety chains attached to the frame of the towing vehicle and to the trailer, never to a part of the hitch.

sec16-card-sec16-F18.front: How should a trailer hitch match the load, and which type of hitch should never be trusted?
sec16-card-sec16-F18.expected_back: The towing vehicle needs a hitch proper for the size and type of trailer, large trailers need special hitches, and a bumper hitch should never be relied on for any trailer.

sec16-card-sec16-F19.front: What percentage of trailer weight belongs on the hitch, and what goes wrong above or below it?
sec16-card-sec16-F19.expected_back: A trailer load must be balanced so that about ten to fifteen percent of the trailer's weight rests on the hitch, because too much hitch weight makes steering difficult and too little makes the trailer fishtail, and the trailer must never be overloaded.

sec16-card-sec16-F20.front: What cargo, wheel, fender, tire, and lighting equipment must a road-legal trailer have?
sec16-card-sec16-F20.expected_back: The load must be held securely in place, and the trailer must have properly mounted and lubricated wheels covered by fenders or mud guards, good properly inflated tires, and tail, stop, turn signal and license plate lamps plus side marker lamps and reflectors where required.

sec16-card-sec16-R02.front: Compare which trailers require independent brakes with which trailers require frame-attached safety chains?
sec16-card-sec16-R02.expected_back: A trailer needs its own brakes when it exceeds half the tow vehicle's weight or three thousand pounds, while every trailer regardless of weight needs safety chains fixed to the frames.

sec16-card-sec16-R03.front: Contrast the handling symptom of too much hitch weight against too little hitch weight?
sec16-card-sec16-R03.expected_back: Too much weight on the hitch makes the tow vehicle hard to steer, while too little makes the trailer fishtail, so ten to fifteen percent of the trailer weight is the target.

sec16-card-sec16-R11.front: Pair the equipment rule for vision-blocking trailers with the passenger ban for house trailers?
sec16-card-sec16-R11.expected_back: A large trailer that blocks the inside mirror requires outside mirrors on both sides, while a house trailer may never carry passengers.

sec16-card-sec16-F01.front: What do trucks, tractor-trailers, and buses demand from their own drivers and from surrounding motorists?
sec16-card-sec16-F01.expected_back: Trucks, tractor-semitrailers, truck trailers and buses need special skill, attentiveness and consideration to operate, and for everyone's safety other road users must also understand the limitations of these large vehicles.

sec16-card-sec16-F02.front: What licensing and conduct standard applies to professional drivers of large vehicles?
sec16-card-sec16-F02.expected_back: A driver of a large vehicle must hold a valid license for that vehicle category, and because most such drivers drive for a living they should be the most skilled and experienced drivers on the road, setting the example of safe driving while being exposed to driving hazards far longer than ordinary drivers.

sec16-card-sec16-F03.front: Why must large-vehicle drivers stay constantly mindful of vehicle limits, road users, and cargo?
sec16-card-sec16-F03.expected_back: Because of their size and weight, large vehicles cause great damage and injury in a crash, so their drivers must stay constantly aware of the limits and potential of their vehicles and give proper consideration to other road users, passengers and cargo.

sec16-card-sec16-F11.front: What packaging, labeling, and exterior truck markings must hazmat drivers verify, and why?
sec16-card-sec16-F11.expected_back: Large trucks often carry explosive, flammable, radioactive, poisonous or other dangerous materials, and their drivers must see that the cargo is packaged and labeled correctly and that the truck itself carries markings showing the type of material, so responders can take the right protective action after a crash.

sec16-card-sec16-F12.front: Which four emergency items must most large vehicles carry and their drivers know how to use?
sec16-card-sec16-F12.expected_back: Most large vehicles must carry emergency equipment such as fire extinguishers, flares, emergency reflectors and first aid kits, and their drivers must know what is required and how and when to use it.

sec16-card-sec16-F13.front: How does hitching a trailer—especially a large one—change an ordinary car or pickup?
sec16-card-sec16-F13.expected_back: Many car and small truck drivers tow trailers, and many of the limitations of large vehicles apply to a vehicle towing a trailer, especially a large one.

sec16-card-sec16-R12.front: Contrast when exterior hazmat markings are required with when emergency safety kits are carried?
sec16-card-sec16-R12.expected_back: Hazardous-material trucks must be marked so responders know the cargo, while emergency equipment such as extinguishers and flares is carried on most large vehicles whatever the cargo.

sec16-card-sec16-F33.front: What testing, registration, and insurance standards apply to motorcycles?
sec16-card-sec16-F33.expected_back: Motorcycles need special knowledge and skill, so most states require a separate motorcycle knowledge test and skill test for a motorcycle license, and motorcycles must be registered and insured to the same standards as a car.

sec16-card-sec16-F34.front: How should motorists view and treat motorcycles in everyday traffic?
sec16-card-sec16-F34.expected_back: Motorcycles are full partners in the traffic mix to be treated with respect and courtesy, so watch for the unexpected and give riders their share of the road.

sec17-card-sec17-F15.front: Which lanes must stop for a school bus flashing alternating red lamps, and what fine can apply?
sec17-card-sec17-F15.expected_back: When a school bus is stopped on a highway with its alternating red lamps flashing, every driver in the bus's lane and in all adjacent lanes must stop before reaching the bus and stay stopped until the bus moves on or the red lamps go off, and breaking this law can cost one thousand dollars.

sec17-card-sec17-F16.front: When are oncoming drivers exempt from stopping for a school bus, and what defines that road?
sec17-card-sec17-F16.expected_back: Vehicles traveling in the opposite direction on a divided highway need not stop for a school bus, a divided highway being two roadways separated by a strip of land or other space not meant for vehicle travel.

sec17-card-sec17-F17.front: What roadside clue warns that a school bus is nearby, and why slow down immediately?
sec17-card-sec17-F17.expected_back: Drivers out when school buses make their runs should be alert, because children waiting along the road in the morning mean a bus is in the area and waiting children may dart in front of traffic.

sec17-card-sec17-R01.front: Contrast who must stop for school-bus flashing red lights with the sole oncoming exemption?
sec17-card-sec17-R01.expected_back: Traffic in the school bus's lane and all adjacent lanes must stop for flashing red lamps, while opposite-direction traffic on a divided highway is exempt.

sec17-card-sec17-F05.front: What speed readiness and audible warning does Hawaii law require when pedestrians are on or near the road?
sec17-card-sec17-F05.expected_back: As a driver you must slow and be ready to stop whenever you see people walking on or crossing the road or children near it, and the law requires you to sound the horn as necessary to warn any pedestrian on the roadway.

sec17-card-sec17-F06.front: How do you identify a blind pedestrian, and how do traffic signals affect your duty to stop?
sec17-card-sec17-F06.expected_back: You must stop for any blind person in the roadway, identified by a white cane or a guide dog, regardless of the traffic signal or the traffic situation.

sec17-card-sec17-F07.front: What two driver moves are prohibited around pedestrian safety zones and cars stopped for walkers?
sec17-card-sec17-F07.expected_back: The law prohibits driving through a pedestrian safety zone and prohibits passing a vehicle that has stopped to let a pedestrian cross.

sec17-card-sec17-F08.front: Where must you scan hardest for children and walkers, and whose hand signal requires a stop?
sec17-card-sec17-F08.expected_back: Be especially watchful for children near schools, parks, playgrounds and residential areas, stop on the signal of any school crossing guard, and the law requires watching for pedestrians when turning at intersections and when entering or leaving driveways.

sec17-card-sec17-F09.front: What check and which side of the car should you and passengers use when getting out?
sec17-card-sec17-F09.expected_back: Before you or your passengers get out, look for approaching vehicles, and leave the vehicle on the side away from traffic whenever possible.

sec17-card-sec17-R02.front: Compare your legal duty toward a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog versus other walkers?
sec17-card-sec17-R02.expected_back: A blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog must be given a stop regardless of the signal, while other pedestrians are owed a slowdown, readiness to stop and a horn warning as needed.

sec17-card-sec17-R11.front: Name the two prohibited driver acts around pedestrians alongside the one required warning?
sec17-card-sec17-R11.expected_back: Driving through a pedestrian safety zone and passing a car stopped for a pedestrian are both prohibited by law, while sounding the horn to warn a pedestrian on the roadway is required by law.

sec17-card-sec17-F21.front: What minimum side gap applies when passing a bicycle, and what right-turn crash must you avoid?
sec17-card-sec17-F21.expected_back: When passing a bicyclist keep at least three feet between the bicycle and your vehicle until safely past, remember the rider may be faster than you think, and avoid the common crash of passing and then slowing to turn right across the rider's path.

sec17-card-sec17-F22.front: How must drivers treat bike lanes and overtaking cyclists when preparing to turn right?
sec17-card-sec17-F22.expected_back: Stay out of bike lanes, especially when turning right at an intersection, look for and yield to bicyclists when crossing a bike lane, do not pass a bicyclist if you are about to turn right, and train yourself to check for overtaking bicyclists at every right turn.

sec17-card-sec17-F23.front: Why must you check behind before swinging open a parked car door?
sec17-card-sec17-F23.expected_back: Look before opening your car door, because opening a door unexpectedly so as to endanger moving traffic, including bicyclists, is a traffic violation.

sec17-card-sec17-F20.front: What share of car-bicycle crashes comes from illegal wrong-way riding, and when must drivers watch for it?
