sec17-card-sec17-F20.expected_back: Riding against traffic is illegal, but many inexperienced bicyclists do it and this behavior causes about twenty-five percent of all bicycle and car crashes, so drivers should watch for wrong-way riders especially when turning.

sec17-card-sec17-F18.front: What legal status do bicycles hold in Hawaii, and why must motorists stay extra alert around them?
sec17-card-sec17-F18.expected_back: Bicycles are legally vehicles with all the rights and responsibilities of other vehicles, yet motorists must be extra alert for them because they are harder to see, may ride unpredictably, and show a wide range of riding ability.

sec17-card-sec17-F19.front: Where do bicycles normally ride, when may they move into the lane, and what changes on one-way streets?
sec17-card-sec17-F19.expected_back: Bicyclists must ride as near the right edge of the road as practicable but may move into the lane to prepare a left turn, pass another bicycle or avoid an obstacle at the edge, and they may legally ride along the left edge of a one-way road.

sec17-card-sec17-R03.front: Pair a driver's minimum clearance when passing a cyclist with the legal rule on opening car doors?
sec17-card-sec17-R03.expected_back: A motorist passing a bicyclist should keep at least three feet of clearance until safely past, while opening a vehicle door unexpectedly in a way that creates a hazard for moving traffic or bicyclists is a traffic violation.

sec17-card-sec17-R07.front: Contrast the major bicycle-crash error committed by riders with the classic crash committed by drivers?
sec17-card-sec17-R07.expected_back: Wrong-way riding causes about a quarter of bicycle and car crashes, while passing a bicyclist and then turning right across the rider is the crash named for motorists.

sec17-card-sec17-F10.front: Where must pedestrians cross legally, and why keep watching cars even inside painted lines?
sec17-card-sec17-F10.expected_back: As a pedestrian cross only at crosswalks because jaywalking is illegal, obey all traffic laws and signals as the law requires, and watch for cars at all times because pavement lines and signals do not guarantee your safety.

sec17-card-sec17-F11.front: What should a pedestrian do when arriving at a green signal that has already been lit awhile?
sec17-card-sec17-F11.expected_back: Never start across the street on a green light that has already been showing for some time; wait for the green on the next cycle.

sec17-card-sec17-F12.front: When does Hawaii law forbid a pedestrian from stepping into a street or crosswalk?
sec17-card-sec17-F12.expected_back: The law prohibits entering the street or a crosswalk when vehicles are approaching close by, because they may not be able to stop, and you should look for turning vehicles before crossing and never run alongside or across a street.

sec17-card-sec17-F13.front: Which side do you walk on where no sidewalk exists, and what clothing, sobriety, and child rules apply?
sec17-card-sec17-F13.expected_back: Walk on the left side of the street facing oncoming traffic, wear bright clothing when walking on or beside a road, stay off the road when under the influence of alcohol or drugs, and keep your children from playing in the street.

sec17-card-sec17-F14.front: What soliciting and parking-space behaviors on the traveled roadway are illegal for pedestrians?
sec17-card-sec17-F14.expected_back: Standing or walking on the traveled roadway to solicit anything, or to hold a vehicle or a parking place, is prohibited by law.

sec17-card-sec17-R06.front: Combine where pedestrians must legally cross with how to treat an aging green light?
sec17-card-sec17-R06.expected_back: A pedestrian must cross only within crosswalks rather than jaywalking, while a pedestrian facing a green light that has been showing for some time should wait for the green signal on the next cycle before starting across.

sec17-card-sec17-R09.front: Contrast which side of a road a pedestrian uses with which side a bicyclist rides on?
sec17-card-sec17-R09.expected_back: A pedestrian walks on the left side facing traffic, while a bicyclist rides on the right side with traffic.

sec17-card-sec17-F25.front: Which traffic laws bind bicyclists, and why ride with traffic even for half a block?
sec17-card-sec17-F25.expected_back: Bicyclists must obey all signs, signals and traffic regulations, which is the law and also earns respect for their place on the road, and they should always ride with traffic even for a short distance because motorists are not looking for fast bicycles coming from the wrong direction.

sec17-card-sec17-F26.front: While watching left for a gap to turn right, whom do drivers and cyclists alike forget?
sec17-card-sec17-F26.expected_back: When turning right, motorists and bicyclists alike often concentrate so hard on traffic from the left that they forget to check for pedestrians coming from the right.

sec17-card-sec17-F27.front: List the four situations when a slower bicyclist may legally leave the right edge and take the lane?
sec17-card-sec17-F27.expected_back: A bicyclist slower than normal traffic rides as close to the right edge as practicable, may use the left edge on a one-way road, and may take the travel lane to turn left, avoid hazards, keep pace with traffic, or when the lane is too narrow to share safely with a motor vehicle.

sec17-card-sec17-F28.front: When must cyclists ride single file versus two abreast, and what penalties apply to bike violations?
sec17-card-sec17-F28.expected_back: On the roadway bicyclists must ride single file, although they may ride two abreast on a bike lane or path wide enough not to impede traffic, and a bicyclist who breaks a traffic law faces the same penalties as a driver.

sec17-card-sec17-F29.front: What rules govern right-turn-only lanes, required night bike gear, and carrying extra bike passengers?
sec17-card-sec17-F29.expected_back: Bicyclists must follow lane markings, leaving a right-turn-only lane when going straight, must have a headlight and rear reflector at night with a rear light, pedal reflectors and light clothing recommended, and must not carry passengers unless the bicycle is equipped for them.

sec17-card-sec17-F30.front: Where is sidewalk bicycling banned in Hawaii, and what speed and yield rules apply elsewhere?
sec17-card-sec17-F30.expected_back: Bicycles may not be ridden on sidewalks in business districts, and elsewhere sidewalk riding is allowed only at ten miles per hour or less while always yielding to pedestrians.

sec17-card-sec17-R04.front: Compare which edge a bicycle uses on a standard two-way street versus a one-way street?
sec17-card-sec17-R04.expected_back: Bicycles ride at the right edge of a two-way road, while on a one-way road they may ride along the left edge.

sec17-card-sec17-R05.front: Contrast Hawaii's sidewalk-riding ban in business districts with residential sidewalk rules?
sec17-card-sec17-R05.expected_back: Sidewalk riding is forbidden in business districts, while elsewhere it is allowed at ten miles per hour or less with pedestrians given the right of way.

sec17-card-sec17-R12.front: Distinguish mandatory night bicycle lighting from additional gear the manual recommends?
sec17-card-sec17-R12.expected_back: A night-riding bicyclist must have a headlight and rear reflector, while a rear light, pedal reflectors and light clothing are only recommended.

sec17-card-sec17-F01.front: What share of Hawaii traffic fatalities are pedestrians, and which age groups make up nearly half?
sec17-card-sec17-F01.expected_back: Pedestrians account for twenty percent of Hawaii's traffic deaths, the people killed are mostly non-drivers, and nearly half of them are younger than fifteen or older than sixty-five.

sec17-card-sec17-F02.front: Where do almost 90 percent of fatal pedestrian crashes happen, and what are most victims doing?
sec17-card-sec17-F02.expected_back: Almost ninety percent of fatal pedestrian crashes happen in the roadway, more than half of them while crossing, and only slightly more than ten percent happen off the roadway.

sec17-card-sec17-F03.front: Why does pedestrian survival inside the roadway depend on both walker and driver?
sec17-card-sec17-F03.expected_back: The roadway is the domain of the motor vehicle, and a pedestrian who enters it has no physical protection, so safety depends entirely on the alertness and actions of both pedestrian and driver.

sec17-card-sec17-F04.front: Why are young children and older adults vulnerable to pedestrian crashes for very different reasons?
sec17-card-sec17-F04.memory_hook: Kids misjudge danger, elders move slower
sec17-card-sec17-F04.expected_back: Children are quick and see well but do not understand traffic and underestimate a vehicle's danger and force, while older people are often handicapped by poor vision, slow reaction, inability to move fast and greater vulnerability to injury.

sec17-card-sec17-R08.front: Pair pedestrians' overall share of Hawaii traffic deaths with the age split inside pedestrian fatalities?
sec17-card-sec17-R08.expected_back: Pedestrians make up twenty percent of Hawaii traffic deaths, while almost half of pedestrian deaths are people under fifteen or over sixty-five.

sec17-card-sec17-F31.front: Why wear a bike helmet on short slow rides, and why avoid weaving between parked cars?
sec17-card-sec17-F31.expected_back: Wear a bicycle helmet every ride even where it is not legally required, because serious head injury does not require speed or distance, and be predictable by never swerving in and out of parked cars or traffic.

sec17-card-sec17-F32.front: What look, hand-signal, and parked-car clearance habits protect a bicyclist?
sec17-card-sec17-F32.expected_back: Look behind and make sure it is clear before a left turn or a move into the travel lane, use proper hand signals for turning and stopping, and keep at least three feet from parked cars so a suddenly opened door cannot hit you while watching for cars pulling out.

sec17-card-sec17-F33.front: Why skip headphones on a bicycle, and what pre-ride mechanical check comes before rolling?
sec17-card-sec17-F33.expected_back: Do not wear headphones when riding, because you need to hear traffic and stay alert to potholes, broken pavement and slippery surfaces, and before each ride confirm working brakes, a tight seat and handlebars, and properly inflated tires in good shape.

sec17-card-sec17-F34.front: Why isn't simple eye contact with a driver enough for a cyclist, and what confirms recognition?
sec17-card-sec17-F34.expected_back: Be visible in bright clothing and never assume a driver has seen you even after eye contact; get a response from the driver so you are sure.

sec17-card-sec17-F35.front: Describe the two lawful ways a bicyclist can execute an intersection left turn?
sec17-card-sec17-F35.expected_back: A bicyclist may turn left like a motor vehicle, signaling, moving to the center of the lane when safe and completing the turn, or like a pedestrian by riding to the crosswalk, walking the bicycle across and riding on from there.

sec17-card-sec17-F36.front: Why shouldn't a bicyclist squeeze past cars on the right, and what is safer in stopped traffic?
sec17-card-sec17-F36.expected_back: A bicyclist should not pass vehicles on the right, because drivers may not expect or see a rider there, and when traffic is stopped it is safer and more courteous to take a place in line.

sec17-card-sec17-F24.front: What three everyday benefits does the Hawaii manual give for treating bicyclists with aloha?
sec17-card-sec17-F24.expected_back: Treat bicyclists with aloha, since every bicycle on the road means one fewer car, less pollution and potentially one more open parking space at your destination.

sec17-card-sec17-R10.front: Contrast a cyclist's vehicular left turn with a pedestrian-style left turn?
sec17-card-sec17-R10.expected_back: A bicyclist may turn left from the center of the lane like a car, while the pedestrian-style option is to walk the bicycle across in the crosswalk.

sec02-card-sec02-F19.front: Where can you renew a Hawaii driver's license, and how early before expiration may you do it?
sec02-card-sec02-F19.expected_back: Any driver licensing office in Hawaii can renew your license, and the renewal may be done during the six months before the expiration date.

sec02-card-sec02-F20.front: Does Hawaii give a grace period to keep driving after your driver's license passes its expiration date?
sec02-card-sec02-F20.expected_back: Every Hawaii driver's license is void after its expiration date, and there is no grace period for driving on an expired license.

sec02-card-sec02-F21.front: How long after expiration may you still renew a Hawaii license before having to start over from scratch?
sec02-card-sec02-F21.expected_back: A license may still be renewed within one year after it expires, but if you miss that renewal period you must go through the procedure for an original license.

sec02-card-sec02-F22.front: What screening is required before license renewal, and how often may you renew by mail?
sec02-card-sec02-F22.expected_back: You must pass a vision test before your license is renewed, and you may renew by mail once but must appear before the examiner of drivers at every other renewal.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.front: Contrast the early and late license renewal windows with your legal right to drive once the card expires?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.expected_back: Renewal is allowed during the six months before expiration and during the year after it, but the license itself is void from the moment it expires with no grace period.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.front: Compare how often a vision test is needed at renewal with how often an in-person counter appearance is needed?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.expected_back: A vision test is required at every renewal, while the in-person visit is required only at every other renewal because one mail renewal is allowed in between.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.front: From 11 p.m. through 5 a.m., when may a provisional license holder legally drive?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.expected_back: A provisional license holder may drive between eleven at night and five in the morning only with a licensed parent or guardian, unless the trip is to or from work or to or from a school-authorized activity.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.front: During the eleven-to-five overnight hours, how many riders under eighteen may a provisional driver carry without a parent aboard?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.expected_back: During those late-night hours a provisional driver may not carry more than one person under eighteen unless a parent or guardian is in the vehicle.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.front: What safety-belt or child-restraint rule applies whenever a provisional driver is behind the wheel?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.expected_back: Whenever a provisional driver is at the wheel, every occupant must wear a safety belt or ride in a child restraint.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.front: How long must you hold your provisional license before applying for a full driver's license?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.expected_back: With a provisional license, you must hold that provisional license for six months before applying for a driver's license.

sec02-card-sec02-R10.front: How do work and school exceptions interact with the overnight minor-passenger limit for provisional drivers?
sec02-card-sec02-R10.expected_back: A provisional driver's late-night exceptions are work and school activities, while the late-night passenger limit of one person under eighteen is lifted only when a parent or guardian rides along.

sec02-card-sec02-F23.front: Under what three card conditions can you apply for a duplicate license, and what must accompany the request?
sec02-card-sec02-F23.expected_back: You may apply for a duplicate license whenever your license is lost, stolen or mutilated, and proper identification is required with the application.

sec02-card-sec02-F24.front: How and within how many days must you report a residence move on your license, including extra REAL ID proof?
sec02-card-sec02-F24.expected_back: Within thirty days of changing your residence address you must notify the county examiner of drivers in writing, giving your old and new address, your name and your license number, and a REAL ID license holder must submit two documents proving the new address.

sec02-card-sec02-F25.front: How and within what deadline must you report a legal name change for your driver's license?
sec02-card-sec02-F25.expected_back: A change of name requires you to appear in person at the appropriate examiner of drivers within thirty days with proof of the change.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.front: Both share a thirty-day deadline, so how does reporting a license address change differ from reporting a name change?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.expected_back: An address change is reported in writing within thirty days, while a name change is reported in person within thirty days with proof.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.front: Who must bring you to the performance test, and what paperwork and condition must your test vehicle have?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.expected_back: For the driver performance test you must be brought to the testing station by a licensed driver and supply a vehicle in safe operating condition that has a current registration, a current safety inspection certificate and an insurance identification card, with every safety defect fixed beforehand.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.front: What three things are strictly off-limits during your Hawaii driver performance test?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.expected_back: During the performance test you will not be asked to break any law, no tricks are used, and no passengers are allowed in the vehicle.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.front: How does Hawaii treat autocycles for driving on a Category 3 license versus taking the Category 3 road test?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.expected_back: A category three license lets you drive an autocycle, but you may not use an autocycle to take the category three performance test.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.front: Which cars, trucks, and buses are covered by the Category 3 driving test?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.expected_back: The category three driving test is given for cars, light trucks rated at eighteen thousand pounds or less, and buses designed to carry fifteen or fewer occupants.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.front: Which driving zones and specific vehicle-control maneuvers are graded on the Category 3 road test?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.expected_back: On the category three test you must start the vehicle and drive through a business district, parallel park, signal, turn, start and stop properly, get moving on a slight grade without rolling backward, and show that you know and obey traffic laws, ordinances and safe driving practices.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.front: State both halves of Hawaii's Category 3 rule for operating versus road-testing an autocycle?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.expected_back: An autocycle is legal to drive on a category three license, yet it is not allowed as the vehicle for the category three performance test.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.front: Which two-wheeled or three-wheeled vehicles fall under Hawaii Class 1 versus Class 2?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.expected_back: Hawaii license class one covers mopeds, and class two covers motorcycles and motor scooters.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.front: What weight rating, passenger count, and three-wheeled vehicle type are covered by a Hawaii Class 3 license?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.expected_back: Class three covers any single vehicle with a gross vehicle weight rating of eighteen thousand pounds or less, vehicles designed to carry fifteen or fewer passengers including the driver, and autocycles.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.front: What exact gross vehicle weight rating band requires a Hawaii Class 4 license?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.expected_back: Class four covers any single vehicle with a gross vehicle weight rating from eighteen thousand one to twenty-six thousand pounds.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.front: What combined weight rating and towed-unit weight trigger a Commercial Class A license?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.expected_back: Commercial class A covers a combination of vehicles rated at twenty-six thousand one pounds or more when the towed vehicles are rated at more than ten thousand pounds.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.front: Which heavy single vehicles and trailer limits belong to Commercial Class B?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.expected_back: Commercial class B covers a single vehicle rated at twenty-six thousand one pounds or more, or such a vehicle towing a unit rated at not more than ten thousand pounds.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.front: When does a smaller vehicle outside Class A and B still require a Commercial Class C license?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.expected_back: Commercial class C covers a single vehicle or combination that fits neither class A nor class B but is designed to carry sixteen or more passengers or hauls hazardous materials that require placards.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.front: What specialized cargo or vehicles match commercial endorsement letters H, T, P, N, X, and S?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.expected_back: Commercial endorsement H is for placardable hazardous materials, T for double and triple trailers, P for vehicles built for sixteen or more passengers including the driver, N for tank vehicles, X for tank vehicles carrying placardable hazardous materials, and S for school buses.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.front: Where do the gross vehicle weight cutoffs sit between Class 3, Class 4, and commercial classes?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.expected_back: Class three stops at a gross vehicle weight rating of eighteen thousand pounds, class four runs from eighteen thousand one to twenty-six thousand pounds, and commercial classes begin at twenty-six thousand one pounds.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.front: What ten-thousand-pound trailer rule separates Commercial Class A from Commercial Class B?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.expected_back: Commercial class A requires the towed units to exceed ten thousand pounds, while class B is a heavy single vehicle whose towed unit does not exceed ten thousand pounds.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.front: Distinguish commercial endorsements P, S, and T from one another?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.memory_hook: P passengers, S school, T trailers
sec02-card-sec02-R06.expected_back: Endorsement P covers vehicles built for sixteen or more passengers, while endorsement S covers school buses specifically and endorsement T covers double and triple trailers.

sec02-card-sec02-F38.front: When must you carry your valid driver's license, and what must you do if a police officer asks for it?
sec02-card-sec02-F38.expected_back: Whenever you operate a motor vehicle or a moped you must carry your valid driver's license and present it to a police officer on demand.

sec02-card-sec02-F39.front: What are the two categories of written Hawaii traffic citations, and how is the less serious one treated?
sec02-card-sec02-F39.expected_back: A violation of the Hawaii vehicle law usually brings a written citation of one of two kinds, the less serious traffic infraction, handled as a civil matter with sanctions such as fines and license or registration stoppers, or the serious traffic crime.

sec02-card-sec02-F40.front: What response options settle a civil traffic infraction compared with a traffic crime citation?
sec02-card-sec02-F40.expected_back: A person cited for a traffic infraction may pay, write a statement or appear in person, while a person cited for a traffic crime faces possible jail and must appear in court.

sec02-card-sec02-F31.front: Where does Hawaii check every original or renewal applicant's record, and what blocks issuance?
sec02-card-sec02-F31.expected_back: Information on every applicant for an original or renewed Hawaii license is sent to the National Driver Register, and if that register shows a license suspended or revoked in another state or the District of Columbia, Hawaii will not issue a license.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.front: Why can you settle a traffic infraction by mail or payment while a traffic crime forces a court visit?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.expected_back: A traffic infraction can be settled by paying, writing a statement or appearing, while a traffic crime requires a court appearance because jail is possible.

sec02-card-sec02-F26.front: Do major surgery, amputation, illness, slower reflexes, or vision trouble automatically end your Hawaii driving privilege?
sec02-card-sec02-F26.expected_back: Driver licenses can be issued to people with disabilities or reduced capability to drive safely in every traffic condition, so major surgery, amputation, serious illness, diminished reflexes or vision problems do not automatically end the driving privilege.

sec02-card-sec02-F27.front: What medical input and functional tests help the licensing office tailor a restricted license?
sec02-card-sec02-F27.expected_back: The licensing office may review a medical report from the driver's health care provider and give vision and skills tests of functional ability, after which a license with restrictions can be issued that keeps the driver within the safe limits of that ability.

sec02-card-sec02-F28.front: Under what sole medical finding does Hawaii withdraw a driver's license altogether?
sec02-card-sec02-F28.expected_back: A license is withdrawn only after a finding that the driver cannot drive safely under any condition. Often no restrictions are needed; when needed, one or more conditions appear on the license.

sec02-card-sec02-F29.front: What do Hawaii's lettered license restriction codes B, C, D, F, G, H, and K stand for?
sec02-card-sec02-F29.expected_back: Common license restriction codes include B for corrective lenses that must be worn, C for a mechanical aid, D for a prosthetic aid, F for an outside mirror, G for daylight driving only, H for driving limited to employment and K for intrastate driving only.
pills: G DAY H WORK K STATE

sec02-card-sec02-F30.front: What vehicle equipment or operating limits match Hawaii's numbered restriction codes 2 through 9?
sec02-card-sec02-F30.expected_back: Numbered restriction codes on a Hawaii license mean two for full hand equipment, three for mechanical signals, four for power steering, five for power brakes, six for a steering knob, seven for a cushion, eight for a medical restriction and nine for a three-wheel motorcycle.

sec02-card-sec02-R11.front: Broadly speaking, what kinds of conditions do Hawaii's lettered restriction codes cover versus numbered codes?
sec02-card-sec02-R11.expected_back: Lettered codes can identify required aids and driving limits; numbered codes include equipment requirements, medical restrictions and three-wheel motorcycle operation.

sec02-card-sec02-F36.front: How does the manual define a moped by wheels and horsepower, and which license categories allow riding one?
sec02-card-sec02-F36.expected_back: The manual defines a moped as a device on two or three wheels whose motor is rated at no more than two horsepower, and operating one on public streets requires a driver's license of any category.

sec02-card-sec02-F37.front: How can someone with no driver's license at all earn legal authority to ride a moped?
sec02-card-sec02-F37.expected_back: A person without any driver's license may obtain a category one moped license by following that category's procedure and using the moped for any required performance test.

sec02-card-sec02-F15.front: Which two specialized tests must Category 1 moped and Category 2 motorcycle or scooter applicants pass?
sec02-card-sec02-F15.expected_back: A category one or two applicant must pass a special written examination on rules of the road, highway signs and safe driving for the motorcycle, motor scooter or moped, and must also pass an off-road skills test described in the Motorcycle Operator Manual.

sec02-card-sec02-F18.front: Which three test segments make up the commercial skills exam required for a Category 4 license?
sec02-card-sec02-F18.expected_back: A category four applicant must pass the commercial skills test, made up of a vehicle inspection test, a basic control skills test and a road test, as described in the Hawaii Commercial Driver's License Manual.

sec02-card-sec02-F32.front: Besides marking organ and tissue donor status at licensing, why should you tell your family about that choice?
sec02-card-sec02-F32.expected_back: When applying for or renewing a license you may designate yourself an organ and tissue donor under the Uniform Anatomical Gift Act, and you should tell your family because their permission to use organs or tissues will be requested.

sec02-card-sec02-F33.front: What does the AHCD notation on a Hawaii license tell emergency medical staff?
sec02-card-sec02-F33.expected_back: You may have the AHCD notation placed on your license to show that you have an advance health care directive, which alerts medical personnel to your special instructions if a serious illness or crash leaves you unable to speak for yourself.

sec02-card-sec02-F34.front: Since October 1, 2014, who qualifies to add a veteran notation to the front of a Hawaii license?
sec02-card-sec02-F34.expected_back: Since October first, twenty fourteen, an applicant who served in any United States uniformed service and was discharged under conditions other than dishonorable may have a veteran notation placed on the front of the license.

sec02-card-sec02-F35.front: Which allied Korean conflict veterans gained access to Hawaii's license veteran notation on April 26, 2016?
sec02-card-sec02-F35.expected_back: Since April twenty-sixth, twenty sixteen, the veteran notation is also available to veterans of the Korean conflict, including those who served in the armed forces of the Republic of Korea under United Nations command and are now United States citizens.

sec02-card-sec02-R09.front: Who can ride a moped right away versus who needs to apply specifically for a Category 1 license?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.expected_back: Any category of driver's license permits moped operation, while a category one license is the route for a person who has no license at all.

sec06-card-sec06-F35.front: Who yields when vehicles arrive at an intersection together, and who yields on a left turn?
sec06-card-sec06-F35.expected_back: When vehicles reach an intersection at the same time you yield to the car on the right, and when turning left you yield to all oncoming traffic close enough to be a hazard.

sec06-card-sec06-F36.front: What yielding and stopping duties apply at protected routes and when pulling out of an alley, driveway, or farmyard?
sec06-card-sec06-F36.expected_back: You yield to all traffic on the protected route, stopping first where a stop is required, and you must stop and yield when entering any public street or road from an alley, driveway or farmyard.

sec06-card-sec06-F37.front: To whom must you yield right after a traffic signal turns green before moving forward?
sec06-card-sec06-F37.expected_back: When a light turns green you yield to pedestrians and to vehicles still caught in the intersection before you proceed.

sec06-card-sec06-F29.front: How are funeral processions and convoys marked, what intersection priority do they hold, and what must you never do?
sec06-card-sec06-F29.expected_back: Funeral processions and convoys have the right of way at intersections, their vehicles usually use headlamps for identification while the first and last vehicles usually carry distinctive markings, and you should not drive between vehicles in a funeral procession.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.front: How does yielding on simultaneous intersection arrival differ from yielding during a left turn?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.expected_back: When vehicles approach an intersection at the same time, yield to the car on the right, while a driver turning left must yield to oncoming traffic that is close enough to pose a hazard.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.front: How does pulling out of an alley, driveway, or farmyard differ from entering a protected route off a side road?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.expected_back: Entering from an alley, driveway or farmyard requires a full stop and yield, while entering a protected route from a side road requires yielding to the protected traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-R12.front: Where do funeral processions and convoys hold right-of-way compared with emergency vehicles?
sec06-card-sec06-R12.expected_back: Funeral processions and convoys hold the right of way at intersections, while emergency vehicles take the right of way everywhere by requiring you to clear a path and stop.

sec06-card-sec06-F31.front: May you pass on the right shoulder, and how much clear road ahead is needed to pass near a hill or curve?
sec06-card-sec06-F31.expected_back: You must not pass on the right shoulder of the highway, and you must not pass when approaching a hill or curve without seven hundred to one thousand feet of clear distance ahead.

sec06-card-sec06-F32.front: Before what two events must a pass finish, and what is unlawful when another car passes you?
sec06-card-sec06-F32.expected_back: You must not pass when the maneuver cannot be completed without interfering with the safety of an oncoming vehicle and before a yellow line appears in your lane, and when you are being passed it is unlawful to increase your speed.

sec06-card-sec06-F33.front: Which left-side sign announces a solid yellow no-passing line, and what passing rule applies around a flashing school bus?
sec06-card-sec06-F33.expected_back: You must not pass when a solid yellow line is in your lane, which is announced by a yellow no passing zone pennant on the left side of the road ahead, nor when a school bus on the same roadway has its flashing lights operating.

sec06-card-sec06-F34.front: Within what distance of intersections, rail tracks, narrow bridges, viaducts, or tunnels is passing banned, and what does a zone-end sign mean?
sec06-card-sec06-F34.expected_back: You must not pass within one hundred feet of or while crossing any intersection or railroad crossing, nor within one hundred feet of a posted narrow bridge, viaduct or tunnel, and the end of a no passing zone only means visibility has improved, not that passing is safe.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.front: In what four highway situations are you forbidden from driving on the left half of the roadway?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.expected_back: The left half of the roadway is forbidden on a road with four or more lanes of moving traffic unless signs say otherwise, near the top of a hill or on a curve, within one hundred feet of or inside an intersection or railroad crossing, and within one hundred feet of a bridge or tunnel when oncoming vehicles cannot be seen.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.front: How does the no-passing buffer at intersections, tracks, and narrow bridges compare with the sight distance for hills or curves?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.expected_back: An intersection or railroad crossing bars passing during the crossing and for one hundred feet on approach. The same approach distance applies to a posted narrow bridge, viaduct or tunnel. At a hill or curve, passing needs seven hundred to one thousand feet of clear road ahead.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.front: For which three maneuvers must you always signal—even with zero traffic visible—and how far ahead must signaling start?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.expected_back: You must signal every time you slow down, turn or change lanes, even when no other vehicle is in sight, and signals must be given for at least one hundred feet, about five car lengths, before the maneuver, with a longer signal advisable at higher speeds.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.front: When are hand signals mandatory, and does turning on a blinker ever grant automatic right-of-way?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.expected_back: Hand signals must be used when the vehicle's turn signals are not working, and signaling never gives you the right to make the move until you have checked that it can be completed without interfering with other traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.front: Why must your spare foot stay clear of the brake pedal unless slowing down?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.expected_back: Keep your foot off the brake pedal whenever you are not actually braking, because a lit stop lamp sends following drivers a false stop signal.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.front: At least how far from the nearest rail must you stop when signals, gates, flaggers, horns within fifteen hundred feet, or visible trains warn?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.expected_back: You must stop at least fifteen feet from the nearest rail of a railroad crossing when an electric or mechanical signal warns of a train, when a gate is lowered or a flagman signals, when a train within one thousand five hundred feet sounds an audible warning, or when an approaching train is visible and close enough to be a hazard.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.front: How does the minimum turn-signal advance distance compare with the minimum stopping distance at railroad tracks?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.expected_back: A turn or lane-change signal must begin at least one hundred feet ahead, while a railroad stop must be at least fifteen feet from the nearest rail.

sec06-card-sec06-R13.front: How do hand signals for broken blinkers contrast with resting your foot on the brake pedal?
sec06-card-sec06-R13.expected_back: Hand signals replace turn signals only when the vehicle's signals are not working, while resting a foot on the brake pedal creates a false stop signal and must be avoided.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.front: What is the major cause of most crashes, and what does Hawaii's basic speed law forbid?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.expected_back: Excessive speed for conditions is the major cause of most crashes, and the basic speed law forbids driving faster than is reasonable and prudent for the area, the road and traffic, pedestrians, weather and light.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.front: What three speed-limit and traffic-flow rules govern maximums, posted minimums, and holding up cars behind you?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.expected_back: You must not exceed the posted maximum speed limit, must not drive below a posted minimum speed limit, and must not drive so slowly that you hold back other traffic, pulling off the road or changing route if you cannot keep up.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.front: Which lane belongs to slower drivers on multilane roads, and what speed contests are banned on public streets?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.expected_back: If you drive more slowly than traffic on a multilane road, stay in the right-hand lane so others can pass on your left, and never take part in any race, speed contest or speed exhibition on a public street or highway.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.front: In which four community or school settings do lower speed limits apply?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.expected_back: Lower speed limits apply near schools and playgrounds, at school crossing signs while children are present, and on residential and business streets.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.front: How does violating a posted minimum speed limit differ from holding back traffic?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.expected_back: Driving below a posted minimum limit is a violation, while driving so slowly that you hold back traffic is a violation even where no minimum is posted.

sec06-card-sec06-F27.front: How must you respond—without slamming brakes in panic—when you hear a siren or spot red or blue emergency lights?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.expected_back: When you hear an emergency vehicle's siren, bell or horn or see its flashing red or blue lamps you must give it a clear path and stop, without panicking or jamming on the brakes, by reducing speed, locating the vehicle and its direction, and moving out of its path.

sec06-card-sec06-F28.front: What should you do if an emergency rig is right behind you in heavy traffic, or stopped ahead with lights flashing?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.expected_back: When an emergency vehicle is right behind you in heavy traffic, continue slowly until you can clear its way, and when you come upon a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, slow or stop as the situation demands and, if it is safe, keep an empty lane between your vehicle and it.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.front: What four steps must you complete before walking away from an unattended vehicle?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.expected_back: Before leaving a vehicle unattended, shut off the engine, lock the ignition and take the key, set the parking brake, and turn the wheels toward the curb if the vehicle is on a grade.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.front: Exceeding how many occupants in the front seat can count as prohibited driver interference?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.expected_back: Driving with more than three persons in the front seat may constitute interference with the driver, which is prohibited.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.front: How does your duty for an approaching emergency vehicle differ from passing a stopped one with flashing lights?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.expected_back: For an approaching emergency vehicle you pull out of its path and stop, while for a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights you slow or stop and leave an empty lane beside it when safe.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.front: What five hazard or access spots are off-limits for parking?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.expected_back: Parking is prohibited anywhere your vehicle is hazardous to other traffic, where it will be towed, on a sidewalk, in front of or so close to a driveway that it interferes with its use, and within or so close to an intersection that it interferes with traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.front: Where else is parking banned around water supply, pedestrian crossings, posted curbs, and highway structures?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.expected_back: Parking is also prohibited in front of or so close to a fire hydrant that it could interfere with the hydrant's use, on or so close to a crosswalk that it blocks drivers' view of pedestrians, where official signs or markings prohibit standing or parking, and on a bridge, elevated structure or inside a tunnel.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.front: Does sitting inside the car excuse double parking, and what is the maximum legal distance from the curb?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.expected_back: Double parking, stopping on the roadway side of another car at the edge of the road, is prohibited whether or not you stay in the vehicle, and so is parking more than twelve inches from the curb.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.front: How much clear street width must remain beside your parked car, and what zones or roadside chores are banned?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.expected_back: You may not park in a passenger or freight loading zone, anywhere that leaves less than ten feet of street width for free movement of traffic, or on a public road to repair a vehicle except in an emergency, wash it, or display it for sale.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.front: When may a vehicle overhang a marked stall, and what is the continuous street-parking time limit?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.expected_back: A vehicle may not be parked so that it sticks out of a marked space unless it is larger than the space, and no vehicle may stay parked on a public street or highway continuously for more than twenty-four hours.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.front: When may you use an accessible parking stall, and why must the striped access aisle stay open?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.expected_back: A space marked with the international symbol of accessibility may be used only when you display the placard or plate issued to the disabled person being transported, and the access aisle beside such a space must stay clear for wheelchair lifts, ramps and other mobility devices.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.front: May you stop briefly in a tow-away zone during posted hours, and whom do you contact if towed?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.expected_back: In a tow-away zone you must not park or stop even momentarily during the hours on the official sign, except when blocked by traffic, and a vehicle left there is towed by the police, whom you contact for recovery information.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.front: How does the twelve-inch parking rule differ from the ten-foot parking rule?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.expected_back: Parking must be within twelve inches of the curb, while a street must keep at least ten feet of width free for traffic beside a parked vehicle.

sec06-card-sec06-R10.front: How does ordinary twenty-four-hour street parking contrast with posted tow-away hours?
sec06-card-sec06-R10.expected_back: A vehicle may stay parked on a public street for up to twenty-four hours continuously, while in a tow-away zone even a momentary stop during the posted hours is prohibited.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.front: What three authorities must you obey whenever driving on a Hawaii street or highway?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.expected_back: You must obey every traffic law while driving on a street or highway, obey all lawful orders and directions of a police officer, and operate your vehicle as traffic signs, signals and pavement markings indicate.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.front: Which half of the road do you drive on, how much narrow road gets shared, and which lane fits slower traffic?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.expected_back: Drive on the right half of the roadway, pass oncoming vehicles on the right, give opposite-direction traffic at least half of the main traveled roadway on narrow roads, and when moving slower than other traffic you should use the extreme right lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.front: In what three situations may you legally use the left half of the roadway?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.expected_back: You may use the left half of the roadway when overtaking a vehicle going your way on a road with two or three lanes of moving traffic and no oncoming traffic, when an obstruction blocks your side and oncoming vehicles are not using the left half, or when driving on a one-way street.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.front: Under what three road or turn conditions is passing another vehicle on the right permitted?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.expected_back: Passing on the right is permitted when the vehicle ahead is about to turn left without driving off the pavement or main traveled roadway, on a paved road with two or more marked lanes in each direction, or on a one-way street with two or more marked lanes.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.front: In which direction must you travel on a designated one-way roadway?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.expected_back: On a one-way roadway you must drive only in the direction the posted signs indicate.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.front: What three rules govern driving on a roadway divided into marked traffic lanes?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.expected_back: On a road marked with traffic lanes you must drive entirely within one lane, change lanes only after checking that the change is safe, and use the lane the signs or pavement markings assign.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.front: How should you set your following distance, and what extra spacing rule applies when towing another vehicle?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.expected_back: Your following distance must stay reasonable and prudent for the speed, the traffic, the road and the weather, and a vehicle that is towing another must leave enough room ahead for an overtaking vehicle to move into safely.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.front: How does using the left half of the road on a two- or three-lane road differ from a four-plus-lane road?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.expected_back: You may use the left half of a two or three lane road to pass when no traffic is coming, while on a road with four or more lanes the left half is off limits unless signs direct otherwise.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.front: When passing legally on the right, what surface boundary separates a legal pass from an illegal one?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.expected_back: You may pass on the right if the vehicle ahead is preparing a left turn, if a paved road has at least two marked lanes for each direction, or if a one-way street has at least two marked lanes. Stay on the pavement or main traveled roadway; the right shoulder is never a passing lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F30.front: Which vehicles must carry an eighteen-inch reflective triangle on the back, and how should you react on spotting one?
sec06-card-sec06-F30.expected_back: A highly reflective eighteen-inch triangular slow-moving vehicle emblem must be displayed on the rear of vehicles designed to travel at twenty-five miles per hour or less, and when you see it you should reduce speed and approach cautiously.

sec06-card-sec06-R11.front: How does the eighteen-inch reflective rear triangle differ from the yellow left-side pennant?
sec06-card-sec06-R11.expected_back: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is an eighteen-inch reflective triangle for vehicles built for twenty-five miles per hour or less, while the no passing zone pennant is a yellow sign on the left side of the road.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.front: Which vehicle owners must carry motor vehicle insurance to register or drive in Hawaii?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.expected_back: Every owner of a car, bus or truck must carry motor vehicle insurance in order to register or operate the vehicle in Hawaii.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.front: How much medical and rehabilitative coverage per person do Hawaii's basic mandatory benefits include?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.expected_back: The basic mandatory benefits include up to ten thousand dollars per person for medical and rehabilitative expenses.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.front: What are Hawaii's mandatory bodily-injury and property-damage liability minimums, and is your own car's damage included?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.expected_back: Mandatory liability coverage is twenty thousand dollars per person with an aggregate of forty thousand dollars per accident for bodily injury, plus ten thousand dollars per accident for property damage, and damage to your own car is not covered without additional coverage.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.front: How do Hawaii's mandatory bodily-injury liability limits compare with its property-damage limit?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.expected_back: Liability coverage pays twenty thousand dollars per person and forty thousand dollars per accident for bodily injury, while property damage coverage is ten thousand dollars per accident.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.front: How does the ten-thousand-dollar medical benefit differ in scope from the ten-thousand-dollar property-damage limit?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.expected_back: The ten-thousand-dollar medical and rehabilitative benefit is a per-person amount, while the ten-thousand-dollar property damage liability is a per-accident amount.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.front: Who must carry vehicle insurance in Hawaii, and what fine or jail term can a violation bring?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.expected_back: Insurance is required of every owner of a car, bus or truck to register or operate it, while a violation of the insurance law can bring a fine up to five thousand dollars or thirty days in jail.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.front: Which crashes must be reported to police immediately by the fastest communication method?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.expected_back: A traffic crash that causes any personal injury, a death, or property damage of three thousand dollars or more must be reported to the police immediately by the quickest means of communication.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.front: What three immediate steps must you take if you are involved in a crash?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.expected_back: If you are in a crash, stop immediately, move your vehicle off the traveled part of the road if possible, and never leave the scene without identifying yourself and rendering assistance.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.front: What details and document must you provide after a crash, and to whom?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.expected_back: At a crash a driver must give name, address and vehicle registration information, and on request show a driver's license, to anyone injured and to the driver, occupant or attendant of any vehicle or other property that was damaged.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.front: What must you do if you hit an unattended parked vehicle or damage roadside property?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.expected_back: If you strike an unattended vehicle you must stop and find the owner or leave a written notice with your name, address and the circumstances, and if you damage other property along the highway you must notify its owner.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.front: How do your identification duties differ between hitting an occupied vehicle and hitting an unattended vehicle?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.expected_back: When you hit an attended vehicle you exchange name, address, registration and license on request, while when you hit an unattended vehicle you find the owner or leave a written notice.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.front: Which two groups of drivers fall under Hawaii's motor vehicle safety responsibility law?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.expected_back: The motor vehicle safety responsibility law affects every driver involved in a crash that causes death, injury or property damage over three thousand dollars, and every person convicted in court of certain vehicle offenses.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.front: Whom must you notify after a safety-responsibility crash, and which numbered insurance form must you file?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.expected_back: After such a crash you must report it to the police department and your insurance company and file evidence of insurance on form SR twenty-one.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.front: How long must you maintain financial-responsibility proof after certain court convictions, and which numbered form is filed?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.expected_back: After conviction of certain vehicle offenses you must file and maintain proof of financial responsibility for three years from the conviction date and file evidence of insurance on form SR twenty-two.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.front: What penalty hits a driver who fails to comply with Hawaii's safety responsibility law?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.expected_back: The penalty for failing to comply with the safety responsibility law is suspension of the driver's license.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.front: How does safety-responsibility form twenty-one differ from form twenty-two in trigger and duration?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.expected_back: Form SR twenty-one is filed as evidence of insurance after a crash, while form SR twenty-two is filed after a conviction and proof must be maintained for three years.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.front: Which two separate events bring a driver under the motor vehicle safety responsibility law?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.expected_back: The safety responsibility law reaches drivers through crashes with death, injury or damage over three thousand dollars, and separately through court convictions for certain vehicle offenses.

sec10-card-sec10-R10.front: What extra document can you lose under the insurance law beyond the license suspension under the safety responsibility law?
sec10-card-sec10-R10.expected_back: Non-compliance with the safety responsibility law costs the driver's license by suspension, while non-compliance with the insurance law can also cost the vehicle's registration certificate.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.front: When can someone sue over property damage versus bodily injury after a Hawaii crash?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.expected_back: You can sue or be sued for property damage at any time, but for bodily injury only when medical bills exceed five thousand dollars, when the injury causes loss of use of a body part or function or permanent and serious disfigurement, or when the injury results in death.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.front: How does the dollar threshold for reporting a crash to police differ from the medical threshold for a bodily-injury lawsuit?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.expected_back: A crash must be reported to police at three thousand dollars or more of property damage, while medical bills exceeding five thousand dollars permit a bodily-injury lawsuit.

sec10-card-sec10-R09.front: Why is suing for vehicle or property damage easier than suing for bodily injury in Hawaii?
sec10-card-sec10-R09.expected_back: Property damage can be sued over at any time, while bodily injury can be sued over only above the medical threshold, for loss of a body function or serious permanent disfigurement, or for death.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.front: How should you summon help and handle injured people at a crash scene, and why avoid moving them?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.expected_back: Help the injured by calling the nearest police agency and asking for an ambulance if needed, then act promptly but carefully without moving injured people unnecessarily, because unskilled handling can turn minor injuries into serious ones.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.front: Which three basic steps protect an injured person while waiting for trained medical help?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.expected_back: Keep an injured person warm until skilled help arrives, try to stop severe bleeding with direct pressure, and protect the victim from oncoming traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.front: How should you protect a crash scene from approaching cars, and which two emergency items belong in your vehicle?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.expected_back: Have someone warn approaching cars to prevent further damage, and keep a flashlight and flares in your vehicle for such emergencies.

sec10-card-sec10-R08.front: How does caring for injured victims differ from handling oncoming traffic at a crash scene?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.expected_back: The injured are kept warm and still and their bleeding is pressed directly, while passing traffic is warned by another person using flares or a flashlight.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.front: Which four penalties—alone or combined—can apply to each separate violation of Hawaii's motor vehicle insurance law?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.expected_back: Each violation of the motor vehicle insurance law is a separate offense punishable by a fine of up to five thousand dollars or thirty days in jail, suspension of the driver's license, forfeiture of the vehicle registration certificate, or any combination of these.

sec14-card-sec14-F28.front: What weather condition causes most Hawaii driving problems, alongside isolated high-road fog and wind gusts?
sec14-card-sec14-F28.expected_back: Hawaii's weather problems for drivers come mainly from rain, with isolated fog on high-elevation roads and occasional gusty winds, and rain both reduces visibility and changes the road surface.

sec14-card-sec14-F29.front: Why are the first few drops of rain most slippery, and how much following distance is needed?
sec14-card-sec14-F29.expected_back: The first few drops of rain are a danger signal, because the road is most slippery before the oil dropped by passing cars has washed away and oil on water can feel like ice, so slow down, add caution and keep at least double your usual following distance.

sec14-card-sec14-F30.front: What happens to good highway tires up to 35 mph in standing rain versus faster speeds?
sec14-card-sec14-F30.expected_back: Prolonged or heavy rain leaves a layer of water on the road, and at speeds up to thirty-five miles per hour tires with good highway tread wipe the surface like a windshield wiper, but at higher speeds the water cannot be cleared and the tires ride up on it like a surfboard, which is called hydroplaning.

sec14-card-sec14-F31.front: At what speed can partial hydroplaning begin, and when can tires lose all pavement contact?
sec14-card-sec14-F31.expected_back: Partial hydroplaning may begin at thirty-five miles per hour, it grows with speed and with the amount of water, and at fifty-five miles per hour in heavy rain the tires may lose all contact with the pavement, leaving you unable to brake, accelerate or steer.

sec14-card-sec14-F32.front: What three tire and speed habits keep your car from hydroplaning in heavy rain?
sec14-card-sec14-F32.expected_back: To prevent hydroplaning keep good tread depth, because worn or bald tires hydroplane at lower speeds, keep tires at proper pressure, because under-inflated tires hydroplane at lower speeds, and reduce speed, because hydroplaning happens most at higher speeds.

sec14-card-sec14-F33.front: How may soaked brakes behave after deep puddles, and how do you restore normal grip?
sec14-card-sec14-F33.expected_back: After deep water or prolonged heavy rain the brakes may be wet and pull to one side or not hold at all, so reduce speed and apply gentle pedal pressure until they work properly again.

sec14-card-sec14-R01.front: Pair the speed where partial hydroplaning begins with the speed where total contact can vanish?
sec14-card-sec14-R01.expected_back: Partial hydroplaning can begin at thirty-five miles per hour, while complete loss of tire contact can come at fifty-five miles per hour in heavy rain.

sec14-card-sec14-R07.front: How does the road hazard from the first raindrops differ from prolonged heavy rain?
sec14-card-sec14-R07.expected_back: The first drops of rain make the road most slippery because of road oil, while prolonged rain creates the water layer that causes hydroplaning.

sec14-card-sec14-R08.front: Contrast how you handle wet brakes after water with a road under fast water over a foot deep?
sec14-card-sec14-R08.expected_back: Wet brakes are dried by gentle pedal pressure at reduced speed, while a flooded road with fast water over one foot deep is never driven through at all.

sec14-card-sec14-F20.front: Does a turn signal grant right-of-way, and for what minimum distance must it flash before moving?
sec14-card-sec14-F20.expected_back: A turn signal shows your intent but gives you no right to make the move, you alone are responsible for making it safely, and traffic regulations require the signal for at least one hundred feet before every turn or lane change and long enough for others to see and understand it.

sec14-card-sec14-F21.front: When you need to slow down for an upcoming turn or lane shift, which comes first?
sec14-card-sec14-F21.expected_back: If you must slow before a turn or lane change, begin signaling before you slow so other drivers are alerted that you may reduce speed.

sec14-card-sec14-F24.front: What three core rules govern every use of your turn signals?
sec14-card-sec14-F24.expected_back: The three rules of turn signals are to signal every time you intend to turn or change lanes, to begin well in advance so others can see and understand, and to remember that the signal shows intent only and grants no right to move.

sec14-card-sec14-F22.front: Name the common turn-signal mistakes drivers make at red lights, right turns, and quiet streets?
sec14-card-sec14-F22.expected_back: Common signaling errors are waiting at a red light without signaling the intended turn, signaling too briefly or only after the move has begun, not signaling a right turn, not signaling in a lane that requires a turn, and not signaling because no one seems to be watching.

sec14-card-sec14-F23.front: According to the Hawaii manual, what attitudes or state of mind does poor signaling reveal?
sec14-card-sec14-F23.expected_back: Failing to signal properly is a frequent driver error that shows ignorance, arrogance or uncertainty and a lack of courtesy, and it may mean the driver has no idea what to do next.

sec14-card-sec14-R09.front: Combine the timing rule for signaling before braking with Hawaii's mandatory signal distance?
sec14-card-sec14-R09.expected_back: Signaling must begin before you slow for a turn, while the signal itself must run for at least one hundred feet before the turn or lane change.

sec14-card-sec14-F05.front: Where should you always choose to park, and which blind roadway spots must you avoid?
sec14-card-sec14-F05.expected_back: Always park where the vehicle is clear of traffic and readily visible to approaching drivers, avoiding hidden spots such as just beyond a curve or the crest of a hill.

sec14-card-sec14-F06.front: What brake, gear, and curb-wheel steps secure a car parked on a hill?
sec14-card-sec14-F06.expected_back: When parking on a hill, always set the hand brake, shift to park if the vehicle has it or otherwise into reverse or low gear, and turn the front wheels toward the curb so that all four wheels would have to climb the curb before the vehicle could roll free.

sec14-card-sec14-F07.front: Which direction does the Hawaii manual tell you to turn front wheels whether parked uphill or downhill?
sec14-card-sec14-F07.expected_back: Whether you park uphill or downhill, the manual directs you to turn the wheels to the right so that a vehicle that rolls free rolls away from traffic.

sec14-card-sec14-F11.front: Unless markings show otherwise, how much gap must parallel-parked bumpers keep from neighboring cars?
sec14-card-sec14-F11.expected_back: When parallel parked, your front and rear bumpers should be no closer than two feet to the other vehicles unless the street is marked otherwise.

sec14-card-sec14-F12.front: Unless angle parking is marked, which way must your car face and how close to the curb?
sec14-card-sec14-F12.expected_back: Unless angle parking is clearly designated, you park parallel to the curb facing the direction of traffic, with the curbside wheels no more than twelve inches from the curb or the whole vehicle inside the marked stall.

sec14-card-sec14-R05.front: How do the manual's two hill-parking statements explain turning wheels toward the curb and right?
sec14-card-sec14-R05.expected_back: On a hill the front wheels go toward the curb so the car cannot roll free, while the manual also directs turning them to the right uphill or downhill so a loose car rolls away from traffic.

sec14-card-sec14-F18.front: What do four-way hazard flashers mean, may you drive with them on, and is there a hand signal?
sec14-card-sec14-F18.expected_back: The four-way hazard flashers tell other drivers that your vehicle is stopped in a hazardous spot on the roadway; they must never be used while moving, they show as every turn indicator flashing, and no hand signal exists for them.

sec14-card-sec14-F19.front: How are electric stop lamps triggered, how can you verify them at night, and what backs them up?
sec14-card-sec14-F19.expected_back: Electric stop lamps operate automatically when the service brake is used, at night their glow should be visible behind the vehicle when you press the pedal, and a hand signal may be used to show braking or slowing.

sec14-card-sec14-F16.front: Why must every driver still know hand signals, and what is their lone advantage?
sec14-card-sec14-F16.expected_back: Hand signals remain an accepted way to show intentions and knowing them is required in case the electric signals fail, their only advantage being that they are seldom subject to failure.

sec14-card-sec14-F17.front: What five practical drawbacks make hand signals weaker than electric turn indicators?
sec14-card-sec14-F17.expected_back: Hand signals are hard to tell from other arm motions, hard to see in darkness and bad weather, not readily visible to drivers on the right, require an open window, and leave only one hand on the wheel.

sec14-card-sec14-F13.front: Since what model year has every vehicle carried electric turn, stop, and four-way hazard signals?
sec14-card-sec14-F13.expected_back: Electric stop signals have been standard for more than fifty years, most vehicles built since the early nineteen fifties have electric turn signals, and since nineteen sixty-eight every vehicle has had electric turn, stop and four-way hazard signals.

sec14-card-sec14-F14.front: What visibility and control advantages do electric turn signals hold over arm signals?
sec14-card-sec14-F14.expected_back: Electric signals can be operated instantly from a closed vehicle, are visible in darkness and bad weather and from all angles except the immediate sides, are seldom misinterpreted, and leave both hands free for control.

sec14-card-sec14-F15.front: What are the two electric-signal failures, and what causes a blinker to stay on after lane shifts?
sec14-card-sec14-F15.expected_back: The disadvantages of electric signals are failure to cancel and failure to function, and a failure to cancel usually comes from a turn or lane change too small to trip the self-cancelling mechanism combined with the driver not watching the panel indicator, whose abnormal behavior is the clue to a signal problem.

sec14-card-sec14-R03.front: Contrast when you use four-way hazard flashers versus directional turn signals at intersections?
sec14-card-sec14-R03.expected_back: Hazard flashers indicate a vehicle in a hazardous roadway position and must not be used while moving. Signal every intended turn or lane change, including an intended turn while stopped at an intersection.

sec14-card-sec14-R06.front: Trade off the main weaknesses of electric signals against the main weaknesses of hand signals?
sec14-card-sec14-R06.expected_back: Electric signals can fail to cancel or fail to work, while hand signals rarely fail but are hard to see at night, from the right side and through a closed window.

sec14-card-sec14-F34.front: What three steps apply when heavy rain cuts visibility despite wipers, including if sight stays poor?
sec14-card-sec14-F34.expected_back: When heavy rain cuts visibility even with the wipers running, reduce speed and turn on the low-beam head lamps so others can see you, and if you still cannot see clearly, pull onto the shoulder or another clear area and stop until the rain lets up.

sec14-card-sec14-F35.front: Why avoid flooded roadways, and what depth of swiftly moving water must never be crossed?
sec14-card-sec14-F35.expected_back: Avoid driving through flooded areas because you may be stranded, and never drive through swiftly moving water more than one foot deep, which will sweep the vehicle off the road.

sec14-card-sec14-F36.front: Where does fog appear on Hawaii roads, and why are isolated fog patches extra dangerous?
sec14-card-sec14-F36.expected_back: Fog in Hawaii almost never occurs at low elevations but can meet the road at higher elevations where low clouds touch the ground, and patches of fog are especially hazardous because they appear suddenly.

sec14-card-sec14-F37.front: Which beams do you use in fog, and below what sight distance must you pull off and stop?
sec14-card-sec14-F37.expected_back: In fog, sharply reduce speed and use low beams, never high beams, whose reflection reduces your own vision and the approaching driver's, be ready for an emergency stop, and if you cannot see at least two car lengths, about forty feet, pull completely off the pavement, stop and turn on the hazard signals.

sec14-card-sec14-F38.front: What does Hawaii's manual advise unseasoned island drivers facing winter snow and ice elsewhere?
sec14-card-sec14-F38.expected_back: Winter driving elsewhere brings hazards unknown in Hawaii, and unless experienced you should avoid it, otherwise fit snow tread tires, start slowly and test the brakes gently once moving, keep the windows clear of snow, ice and frost, keep a safe distance and watch for vehicles in trouble, drive slower and stay on the clear dry parts of the road.

sec14-card-sec14-R02.front: Which headlight setting governs both fog and heavy rain, and what goes wrong with high beams?
sec14-card-sec14-R02.expected_back: Low beams are the rule in both fog and heavy rain, while high beams in fog reflect back and blind both you and the oncoming driver.

sec14-card-sec14-R12.front: Compare the pull-off threshold in fog with the pull-off threshold in blinding rain?
sec14-card-sec14-R12.expected_back: In fog you stop when you cannot see two car lengths, about forty feet, while in heavy rain you stop whenever you cannot see clearly even with the wipers on.

sec14-card-sec14-F08.front: How do you pull into a designated angle parking stall?
sec14-card-sec14-F08.expected_back: For angle parking, keep safe clearance and drive forward into the space with equal room on each side between the lines.

sec14-card-sec14-F09.front: What side gap and steering angle start a parallel park alongside the front car?
sec14-card-sec14-F09.expected_back: Parallel parking begins by signaling and stopping even with the front car about eighteen inches from it with the rear bumpers even, then backing slowly with the wheel turned sharply right until the car is at about a forty-five degree angle to the street, then quickly straightening the front wheels and backing slowly.

sec14-card-sec14-F10.front: When do you cut the wheel hard left during parallel parking, and how do you finish?
sec14-card-sec14-F10.expected_back: When your front bumper is even with the other car's rear bumper, turn the wheel sharply and rapidly all the way left and back slowly toward the car behind without touching it, then turn sharply right, pull forward slowly and center the car in the space.

sec14-card-sec14-R04.front: Name the starting side gap, final bumper gap, and final curb distance in parallel parking?
sec14-card-sec14-R04.expected_back: Parallel parking starts eighteen inches from the front car and ends with bumpers at least two feet from the neighbors, while the curbside wheels must finish within twelve inches of the curb.

sec14-card-sec14-F25.front: How do large trucks and buses trade off protection, visibility, and agility against small vehicles?
sec14-card-sec14-F25.expected_back: You share the road with trucks, buses, cars, motorcycles, bicycles and pedestrians, and larger vehicles protect their occupants more and are easier to see but harder to operate, while small vehicles protect less and are less visible but more agile.

sec14-card-sec14-F26.front: What two visibility habits keep you safe around motorcycles/bicycles versus trucks/buses?
sec14-card-sec14-F26.expected_back: Recognize the capabilities and limits of other vehicles and your own, look carefully for smaller vehicles such as motorcycles and bicycles, and make sure the drivers of trucks and buses can see you.

sec14-card-sec14-F27.front: How much lane width is a motorcyclist legally entitled to occupy?
sec14-card-sec14-F27.expected_back: Give motorcyclists, bicyclists and pedestrians plenty of room and look for them with extra care when turning or changing lanes, and a motorcyclist is entitled to the entire width of the traffic lane.

sec14-card-sec14-R11.front: Summarize the visibility, handling, and protection contrast between large and small road users?
sec14-card-sec14-R11.expected_back: Larger vehicles are easier to see but harder to operate, while smaller vehicles are more agile but less visible and less protective.

sec14-card-sec14-F01.front: Above roughly what speed will most automatic transmissions refuse a manual downshift?
sec14-card-sec14-F01.expected_back: Most automatic transmissions downshift when the selector is moved to the next lower position, but above about sixty miles per hour they will not, so the vehicle must first slow before an automatic transmission can downshift.

sec14-card-sec14-F02.front: Why does the manual discourage routine downshifting as your main way to slow down?
sec14-card-sec14-F02.expected_back: Routine downshifting to slow down is not recommended because it decelerates the vehicle sharply without lighting the stop lamps to warn following drivers, so downshifting to reduce speed should only supplement the brakes.

sec14-card-sec14-F03.front: How do passenger automatics downshift for highway passing, and what does manual downshift abuse cause?
sec14-card-sec14-F03.expected_back: At normal highway speeds every passenger car automatic transmission downshifts by itself when the accelerator is fully depressed, downshifting at higher speeds may actually reduce the vehicle's ability to accelerate, and abusing the technique stresses the engine and transmission and can lead to costly repairs.

sec14-card-sec14-F04.front: When is downshifting a proper emergency move, and what surface demands extra caution?
sec14-card-sec14-F04.expected_back: Downshifting is a proper emergency procedure for slowing a vehicle after partial or complete brake failure, but it needs extra care on a slippery surface because the unequal forces it creates can cause control problems.

sec14-card-sec14-R10.front: Contrast the two situations where downshifting is proper with why routine slowing by gear is bad?
sec14-card-sec14-R10.expected_back: Downshifting is proper as an emergency measure after brake failure and before a steep downgrade, while downshifting as a routine way to slow is discouraged because following drivers get no stop-lamp warning.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.front: What is the youngest age at which you can qualify for a Hawaii instruction permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.expected_back: You must be at least fifteen and a half years old to be eligible for an instruction permit.

sec01-card-sec01-F35.front: What minimum age and preliminary screenings launch Hawaii's graduated licensing program for an instruction permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F35.expected_back: Under the graduated licensing program the minimum age to acquire an instruction permit is fifteen and a half years, and the applicant must pass the preliminary examinations, a vision screening test and a rules of the road test.

sec01-card-sec01-F38.front: How many days must you hold an instruction permit, and what minimum age applies before seeking a provisional license?
sec01-card-sec01-F38.expected_back: You must hold a valid instruction permit for one hundred eighty days before you may apply for a provisional license, and the minimum age for a provisional license is sixteen years.

sec01-card-sec01-F27.front: What is the minimum age for a Hawaii Class 3 license, and what extra requirement applies under age eighteen?
sec01-card-sec01-F27.expected_back: To get a class three driver's license you must be at least seventeen years old, and an applicant under eighteen must first complete the graduated licensing program.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.front: How long must a driver under eighteen hold a provisional license before qualifying for Class 3?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.expected_back: A driver under eighteen must hold a provisional license for at least six months before becoming eligible for a class three driver's license.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.front: Contrast the starting age for an instruction permit with the age and permit-holding rule for a provisional license?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.expected_back: An instruction permit can be issued at fifteen and a half, while a provisional license requires age sixteen and one hundred eighty permit days.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.front: How do the age and prerequisites for a provisional license compare with those for a Class 3 license?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.expected_back: A provisional license comes at sixteen after the permit period, while a class three license requires age seventeen and completion of the graduated program for anyone under eighteen.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.front: How is the instruction-permit holding period measured compared with the provisional-license holding period?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.expected_back: The permit-holding requirement is one hundred eighty days, while the provisional-holding requirement before class three is six months.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.front: Who must supervise an instruction permit driver, where must that person sit, and which vehicle is exempt from the seat rule?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.expected_back: An instruction permit lets you drive only while supervised by a driver who is at least twenty-one years old and licensed for that type of vehicle, and in every vehicle except a motorcycle that supervising driver must sit in the right front seat.

sec01-card-sec01-F36.front: How does the required companion for a permit holder change from 11 p.m. through 5 a.m.?
sec01-card-sec01-F36.expected_back: A permit holder may drive on any highway only when accompanied by a licensed driver who is at least twenty-one years old, and between eleven at night and five in the morning that accompanying driver must be the permit holder's parent or guardian.

sec01-card-sec01-F37.front: What restraint rule applies to every person riding with an instruction permit driver?
