sec09-card-sec09-F11.teaching_text: Overtaking past a rectangular Do Not Pass posting puts you head-on into blind hills, curves, or intersections.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.question_text: What shape, colors, and roadside placement distinguish a No Passing Zone sign?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.teaching_text: Mounting the pennant on the left shoulder keeps the zone start visible even behind a tall truck.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.question_text: What does a rectangular black-and-white Pass With Care sign announce?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.teaching_text: Even after the restriction ends, Pass With Care reminds you to verify clear oncoming sightlines before pulling out.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.question_text: How does the role of a rectangular Do Not Pass sign differ from the left-side pennant?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.teaching_text: Both work as a pair so drivers on two-lane highways never miss the exact line where passing becomes illegal.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.question_text: How do Do Not Pass and No Passing Zone signs differ in shape, color, placement, and job?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.teaching_text: Pairing rectangular regulatory bans with yellow-and-black left-side pennants is a classic Hawaii knowledge-test comparison.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.question_text: What limits can rectangular black-and-white speed signs set, and how must you drive within them?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.teaching_text: Speed limits can vary by vehicle type, hour, or weather, and crawling below a posted minimum breaks the law too.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.question_text: What should you do at a Reduced Speed Ahead sign, and where does the lower limit take legal effect?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.teaching_text: Easing off the gas early avoids abrupt braking right at the upcoming lower speed-limit post.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.question_text: What do black-and-white lane use control signs show, and what rule applies to your lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.teaching_text: Going straight from a mandatory turn lane or turning against lane arrows collides with adjacent turning lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.question_text: What is the purpose of black-and-white alignment signs along a roadway?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.teaching_text: Alignment rectangles steer traffic cleanly past medians, dividers, and channelized islands without hesitation.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.question_text: What visual symbols identify exclusion signs, and what do they restrict?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.teaching_text: A red ring with a diagonal slash delivers an instant universal no for turns, trucks, bikes, or entry.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.question_text: What colors and shape mark worded regulatory signs that govern parking, weights, and vehicle types?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.teaching_text: Checking white curb and roadside rectangles saves you from tow zones, weight violations, and restricted-lane tickets.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.question_text: How does a Reduced Speed Ahead sign differ legally from the speed limit sign that follows it?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.teaching_text: Test questions check whether you know the advance sign prompts smooth deceleration before the enforceable post.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.question_text: How do exclusion signs communicate restrictions differently from other worded regulatory signs?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.teaching_text: Symbol-based red circles stop bad maneuvers at highway speed, while worded white plaques spell out detailed rules.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.question_text: What do roadway warning signs alert you to, and how should you respond?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.teaching_text: Spotting a warning sign early gives you time to cover the brake and scan before the hazard appears.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.question_text: What do most warning signs look like, and which common road hazards do Hawaii's examples include?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.teaching_text: Divided highway starts and ends, steep hills, wet-road skids, pedestrian crossings, and narrowing lanes all share yellow diamonds.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.question_text: Which two meanings can the five-sided school warning carry, and what upcoming intersection control has its own warning?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.teaching_text: Slowing early for both school pentagons and hidden traffic signals prevents panic stops around blind bends.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.question_text: What two groups do construction traffic-control devices protect, and what is their basic color?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.teaching_text: Bright orange separates temporary construction setups from ordinary road conditions so crews and walkers stay safe.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.question_text: Which seven traffic-control devices and personnel are most commonly used in work zones?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.teaching_text: Expecting drums, tubes, arrow boards, and live flagpersons together keeps you alert through shifting lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.question_text: What do construction and maintenance signs warn about, and which shapes do they use?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.teaching_text: Orange diamonds flag unusual hazards ahead while orange rectangles post specific work-zone instructions or closures.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.question_text: Which five channelizing devices guide traffic through work zones, and what is added to them at night?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.teaching_text: Flashing or steady-burning lights mounted on drums, panels, and tubes keep narrow temporary lanes visible after dark.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.question_text: How do diagonal stripes on a barricade or vertical panel tell you which side to pass on?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.teaching_text: Follow the downward slant of the stripes just like water running downhill toward the open travel lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.question_text: What two messages do large flashing or sequencing arrow panels give drivers day and night?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.teaching_text: Merging early when you spot a giant illuminated arrow prevents getting pinned at the closed-lane taper.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.question_text: What clothing do work-zone flagpersons wear, and what tools do they use to direct traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.teaching_text: A flagperson's stop-and-slow paddle or red flag carries full authority to halt traffic for crew and equipment moves.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.question_text: What is the exact directional difference between barricade stripes sloping down right versus down left?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.teaching_text: Misreading diagonal stripes at night can steer a car onto closed pavement behind the barricade.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.question_text: How does a flashing arrow panel's job differ from a flagperson's job in a work zone?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.teaching_text: Arrow boards shift traffic out of closed lanes continuously, whereas flagpersons actively stop, slow, and release queues.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.question_text: Which four kinds of travel information are covered by guide and information signs?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.teaching_text: Spotting route shields, mileage boards, park signs, and service panels early prevents sudden exit-ramp swerves.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.question_text: How do green, blue, and brown guide signs differ in purpose from yellow warning signs?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.teaching_text: Keeping navigation colors separate from hazard yellow helps you prioritize immediate road risks over route reading.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.question_text: What happens to your license, what temporary permit is issued, and what right do you have if you test at point zero eight or higher or refuse testing?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.teaching_text: Administrative revocation pulls your plastic license immediately before any criminal court trial even begins.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.question_text: What blood alcohol limit applies to drivers under age twenty-one under Hawaii's zero tolerance rule?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.teaching_text: Even a fraction of one drink can push an underage driver to point zero two and cost driving privileges.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.question_text: At what blood alcohol percentages is a Hawaii driver considered impaired versus under the influence?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.teaching_text: Staying below point zero eight will not save you when blood alcohol above point zero five already establishes impairment.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.question_text: How does Hawaii distinguish between being impaired and being under the influence by blood alcohol level?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.teaching_text: Test questions target the exact band above point zero five and below point zero eight to catch careless readers.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.question_text: How does the adult administrative revocation level compare with the underage zero tolerance level?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.teaching_text: Underage drivers face revocation at one-fourth of the adult point zero eight blood alcohol threshold.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.question_text: What revocation rule do a failed test and a refused test share, and what extra penalty hits a refusal?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.teaching_text: Refusing testing triggers one, two, or four years of revocation depending on your prior alcohol enforcement record.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.question_text: What core prohibition does Hawaii law enforce regarding intoxicants and motor vehicles?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.teaching_text: Notice the law covers all intoxicants—alcohol and impairing drugs alike—whenever you operate a vehicle.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.question_text: What have you already agreed to under implied consent simply by driving on Hawaii's public highways?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.teaching_text: Using public roads carries an automatic legal agreement to submit to alcohol testing when lawfully requested.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.question_text: For how many years can your license be revoked if you refuse an officer's alcohol test request?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.teaching_text: Prior alcohol enforcement contacts escalate a test refusal all the way up to a four-year license loss.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.question_text: Does refusing an alcohol test block an impaired-driving charge, and how can taking the test help an innocent driver?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.teaching_text: Officers can still prosecute impairment using driving and field evidence, whereas a clean test exonerates a sober driver.

sec11-card-sec11-R09.question_text: How does implied consent relate to administrative license revocation?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.teaching_text: Implied consent sets the advance testing agreement on public roads, and administrative revocation enforces failed or refused tests.

sec11-card-sec11-R10.question_text: What two opposite outcomes can a blood-alcohol test prove, and why is refusing futile against charges?
sec11-card-sec11-R10.teaching_text: Saying no adds stiff refusal revocations without stopping prosecutors from filing an impaired-driving case anyway.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.question_text: Is alcohol a stimulant or a depressant, how does it hurt driving skills, and why might drinkers feel energized?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.teaching_text: Lowered caution fools impaired people into feeling sharp right while their vision, judgment, and reaction speed plummet.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.question_text: Does switching among beer, wine, or whiskey change impairment risk?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.teaching_text: Standard servings of beer, wine, and liquor deliver pure alcohol to your bloodstream with identical impairing power.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.question_text: How does drinking on an empty stomach compare with drinking after a recent meal?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.teaching_text: Without food slowing absorption, even a small drink hits the bloodstream and brain noticeably faster.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.question_text: Why do black coffee, food, or cold showers fail to sober you up, and what actually removes blood alcohol?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.teaching_text: Caffeine or cold water only creates a wide-awake drunk while your liver, kidneys, and lungs work slowly.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.question_text: Why does alcohol's true physical effect contradict the lively feeling many drinkers experience?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.teaching_text: Feeling bold comes from losing self-control, even as reflexes, alertness, judgment, and eyesight slow down.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.question_text: How does eating food before drinking differ in effect from eating food, drinking coffee, or showering afterward?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.teaching_text: Once alcohol enters your bloodstream, nothing swallowed or splashed on your face speeds up liver elimination.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.question_text: Where outdoors in public is consuming or possessing an alcoholic beverage illegal?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.teaching_text: Hawaii bans both drinking and holding alcohol anywhere along public streets and public sidewalks.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.question_text: Where inside a motor vehicle is keeping an opened alcoholic beverage container illegal on a public road?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.teaching_text: Even if the driver stays completely sober, an unsealed bottle in the passenger cabin violates open-container law.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.question_text: How does Hawaii's public-drinking ban differ from its vehicle open-container ban?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.teaching_text: One statute covers highways and sidewalks outdoors while a separate rule bars opened containers inside occupied vehicle cabins.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.question_text: What should you ask your doctor before driving on any prescription or non-prescription medicine?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.teaching_text: Everyday prescriptions and pharmacy remedies can trigger drowsiness, blurred vision, or slowed reaction behind the wheel.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.question_text: Which two common over-the-counter remedies often contain ingredients that impair driving?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.teaching_text: Antihistamines and decongestants can make you drowsy or dizzy enough to drift out of your lane.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.question_text: How do stimulant amphetamines and sedative or tranquilizer overdoses affect driving and survival?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.teaching_text: Pep pills mask exhaustion until sudden collapse, while tranquilizer and sedative downers slow breathing and reflexes fatally.

sec11-card-sec11-F20.question_text: Why must you never combine alcohol with prescription, over-the-counter, or other drugs?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.teaching_text: One drink paired with one pill can hit your nervous system much harder than the sum of each alone.

sec11-card-sec11-F21.question_text: How do illegal drugs like hallucinogens, heroin, and cocaine affect awareness, and what driving rule applies?
sec11-card-sec11-F21.teaching_text: Users can become completely oblivious or indifferent to oncoming traffic, pedestrians, and red lights.

sec11-card-sec11-F22.question_text: Why is every drug sold on the illegal market inherently dangerous?
sec11-card-sec11-F22.teaching_text: Unregulated street doses carry unpredictable potency and hidden contaminants that can incapacitate a person instantly.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.question_text: How do pharmacy medicines like cold and allergy pills compare in effect with illegal drugs like heroin or cocaine?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.teaching_text: Both make driving unsafe, ranging from slowed pharmacy-pill reflexes to total detachment from reality.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.question_text: How do amphetamines contrast with tranquilizers and sedatives, and what danger do overdoses of both share?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.teaching_text: Opposite drug classes push the body in opposite directions yet share the same fatal overdose risk.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.question_text: Roughly how many fatal crashes and what share of United States traffic deaths involve alcohol each year?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.teaching_text: Even drivers who never touch a drop share public roads nightly with impaired motorists.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.question_text: Why does the drinking-driver problem include ordinary social drinkers and even people taking alcohol-containing medicine?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.teaching_text: Intoxicants dull the exact brain centers needed to recognize your own impairment before grabbing the keys.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.question_text: Which three commitments make up your personal share of solving the impaired-driving problem?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.teaching_text: Planning a sober ride before the first drink or dose removes impaired judgment from the equation.

sec12-card-sec12-F25.question_text: When must safety belts be worn, and in what four ways do they protect everyone in a crash?
sec12-card-sec12-F25.teaching_text: Staying strapped in your seat lets you steer and brake through a first glancing hit instead of becoming a projectile.

sec12-card-sec12-F26.question_text: How deadly is ejection, up to what speed can belts make crashes survivable, and how slow can an unbelted crash kill?
sec12-card-sec12-F26.teaching_text: Even a parking-lot speed of twelve miles per hour can kill an unbuckled rider thrown into glass and steel.

sec12-card-sec12-F28.question_text: How should your lap belt and shoulder belt fit, and when do modern belts lock?
sec12-card-sec12-F28.teaching_text: Wearing the lap strap low on strong hip bones instead of soft stomach tissue prevents severe internal crash injuries.

sec12-card-sec12-F29.question_text: Why must small children use dedicated child seats rather than riding in someone's lap or standing on a seat?
sec12-card-sec12-F29.teaching_text: Crash forces multiply a baby's weight far beyond human grip strength, and five seconds buckling prevents lifelong injury.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.question_text: How does proper tightness for a lap belt differ from proper slack for a shoulder belt?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.teaching_text: Test questions check that the lap strap hugs hip bones tightly while the chest strap admits just one fist.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.question_text: How does the top survivable crash speed with belts compare against the lowest fatal crash speed without belts?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.teaching_text: Skipping belts for short slow neighborhood errands ignores that fatal impacts start at just twelve miles per hour.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.question_text: What does defensive driving mean, what risky road users do you guard against, and whom must you guard against first?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.teaching_text: Catching your own impatience, carelessness, or temper comes before reacting to aggressive or impaired strangers.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.question_text: Which five habits does a defensive driver practice to prevent crashes?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.teaching_text: Keeping an escape path, wide following gap, right speed, and far-ahead scan stops chain-reaction pileups before they start.
sec12-card-sec12-F16.must_match_memory_hook: Moving eyes, look-ahead, escape, space, speed

visual_sync.text_span: Moving eyes, look-ahead, escape, space, speed

sec12-card-sec12-F17.question_text: Where does almost all safe-driving information come from, where should you focus extra attention, and how does speed affect vision?
sec12-card-sec12-F17.teaching_text: Faster speeds shrink peripheral awareness into tunnel vision, making far-ahead scanning even more essential.

sec12-card-sec12-F18.question_text: Where should your scanning pattern place attention, and what do post-crash claims of not seeing really mean?
sec12-card-sec12-F18.teaching_text: Drivers who say they never saw the other car were almost always daydreaming or looking away instead of scanning.

sec12-card-sec12-R08.question_text: How does defending against other drivers connect with checking your own behavior?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.teaching_text: You cannot out-drive careless or aggressive strangers if you bring the exact same risky traits into the driver's seat.

sec12-card-sec12-R09.question_text: How does proper defensive scanning differ from sightseeing, daydreaming, or looking inside the cabin?
sec12-card-sec12-R09.teaching_text: Purposeful glances across road, mirrors, and gauges gather safety cues, while sightseeing locks eyes off traffic.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.question_text: How should you handle distracting tasks like eating, grooming, reading, music changes, or tending kids and pets?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.teaching_text: Taking eyes or hands off driving for food, makeup, maps, or passengers invites split-second lane drift and rear-end hits.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.question_text: How loud may your stereo be, and what is Hawaii's rule on headsets or earphones while driving?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.teaching_text: Covering or plugging both ears masks emergency sirens, warning horns, and skidding tires until impact.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.question_text: Why does even hands-free phone talk hurt driving, where should calls happen, and how should pets ride?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.teaching_text: Phone conversations hijack mental focus even with both hands on the wheel, and loose lap pets block steering.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.question_text: Does using hands-free phone gear make calling safe in motion, or what does the Hawaii manual require?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.teaching_text: Exams specifically test that mental conversation overload persists on speakerphone, leaving pulling over as the safe choice.

sec12-card-sec12-R12.question_text: How does the rule on vehicle stereos differ from the rule on headsets covering or inserted in both ears?
sec12-card-sec12-R12.teaching_text: Moderate cabin speakers still let outside sirens penetrate, whereas dual earbuds seal off urgent warning sounds.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.question_text: Which five personal traits or shortcomings cause bad driving habits?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.teaching_text: Every dangerous shortcut behind the wheel traces back to one or more of those five human root causes.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.question_text: Which two critical safety actions fade away when laziness creeps into a driver's routine?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.teaching_text: Replacing a real head-turn blind-spot check with a lazy mirror glance—and skipping blinkers—sets up sideswipes and dooring.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.question_text: How does impatience erode proper stopping at stop signs and red lights over time?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.teaching_text: Feeling rushed by cars behind you turns crisp stops into rolling slowdowns that miss crossing bikes and cars.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.question_text: Which three aggressive moves mark an impatient driver between stops?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.teaching_text: Jackrabbit sprints, constant lane weaving, and bumper-riding rattle surrounding traffic while saving almost zero trip time.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.question_text: How does physical posture and wheel grip change as a once-alert new driver slips into inattention?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.teaching_text: Where your posture and eyes drift, your front tires follow right across lane lines.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.question_text: What telltale behaviors show an inattentive driver with passengers or when driving alone?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.teaching_text: Hanging an arm out the window, gesturing during stories, or gazing off-road trades away your reaction cushion.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.question_text: How does an arrogant driver differ from a merely impatient one, and how should you respond to one?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.teaching_text: Racing or blocking an ego-driven rule-breaker offers nothing to gain and everything to lose.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.question_text: What dangerous errors does an ignorant driver commit, and whom do they usually blame?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.teaching_text: Halting abruptly on a highway entrance ramp or turning from an improper lane blindsides surrounding lawful drivers.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.question_text: What excuse do drivers with stacked bad habits tell themselves after crashing, and what extra bad habits pile on?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.teaching_text: Skipping belts, blind backing, non-yielding, drinking, and cabin distractions build crashes that were completely preventable.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.question_text: How do you build automatic good driving habits, and how does that change trips?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.teaching_text: Practicing full stops, signals, and head checks every single drive wires smooth, stress-free muscle memory.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.question_text: How does any habit become automatic, and why do bad driving habits sneak in over time?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.teaching_text: Trimming small physical steps without noticing turns crisp beginner technique into sloppy crash-prone habits.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.question_text: What separates an impatient driver's mindset from an arrogant driver's mindset?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.teaching_text: Impatience simply rushes carelessly through traffic, whereas arrogance purposefully bullies right-of-way just to feed ego.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.question_text: How do the telltale signs of laziness differ from the telltale signs of inattention?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.teaching_text: Lazy drivers skip head-turns and signals on moves, while inattentive drivers loosen grip and drift mid-lane.

sec12-card-sec12-F30.question_text: When a car strikes a solid barrier at thirty miles per hour, how fast does an unbelted occupant keep flying forward?
sec12-card-sec12-F30.teaching_text: Crushing metal slows the vehicle frame, while inertia hurls unbuckled riders forward at full pre-crash speed.

sec12-card-sec12-F31.question_text: In a thirty-mile-per-hour barrier crash, what are the exact fractions of a second for the car stopping and the human collision?
sec12-card-sec12-F31.teaching_text: No human arms can brace against a dashboard impact that starts one-fiftieth of a second after the bumper halts.

sec12-card-sec12-F32.question_text: Why do buckled occupants avoid the human collision entirely?
sec12-card-sec12-F32.teaching_text: Sharing the vehicle's slower energy-absorbing crumple keeps head and chest off hard glass and steering columns.

sec12-card-sec12-F27.question_text: What can unbelted passengers do to infants and small children in a crash, and what happens to an unbelted driver?
sec12-card-sec12-F27.teaching_text: An unbuckled adult becomes a heavy projectile inside the cabin while an unbuckled driver gets thrown off the pedals.

sec12-card-sec12-R07.question_text: How much faster is the unbelted human collision than the car's own barrier stop?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.teaching_text: Stopping ten times more abruptly against a hard dashboard multiplies peak impact force on the human body.

sec12-card-sec12-F23.question_text: What should dash warning lamps do at startup, and what do lit yellow versus lit red lamps mean afterward?
sec12-card-sec12-F23.teaching_text: A bulb that stays dark at key-on is burned out, while a red light staying lit afterward demands immediate stopping and checking.

sec12-card-sec12-F24.question_text: When should the brake lamp turn off, and what does it mean if it lights when pressing the foot brake?
sec12-card-sec12-F24.teaching_text: Driving with a brake warning lamp triggered under pedal pressure risks total stopping failure in traffic.

sec12-card-sec12-F20.question_text: Which fluids and parts need checking if unchecked within the past week, along with glass and fuel?
sec12-card-sec12-F20.teaching_text: Weekly under-hood, tire, lamp, clean-glass, and fuel checks stop preventable roadside breakdowns.

sec12-card-sec12-F21.question_text: Which controls must you locate and test before pulling out in an unfamiliar vehicle?
sec12-card-sec12-F21.teaching_text: Fumbling for beam switches or defrosters during a sudden tropical downpour steals eyes right off the highway.
sec12-card-sec12-F21.must_match_memory_hook: Signals, lights, wipers, brakes, gear, horn

visual_sync.text_span: Signals, lights, wipers, brakes, gear, horn

sec12-card-sec12-R05.question_text: After the startup computer check finishes, how does a lit yellow dash light differ in urgency from a red one?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.teaching_text: Ignoring a glowing red oil, temperature, or brake lamp can ruin an engine or cause a crash.

sec12-card-sec12-R11.question_text: How do weekly maintenance checks on your regular car differ from pre-drive checks in an unfamiliar car?
sec12-card-sec12-R11.teaching_text: Even a freshly serviced rental car is risky until your hands know every switch, stalk, and pedal.

sec12-card-sec12-F19.question_text: Under which physical or emotional states should you skip driving, and what alternatives should you use?
sec12-card-sec12-F19.teaching_text: Illness, injury, strong emotion, or medication clouds focus just when riding with friends, transit, or emergency help is safer.

sec12-card-sec12-F22.question_text: What four planning habits apply before driving to an unfamiliar area?
sec12-card-sec12-F22.teaching_text: Checking maps, weather, lighting, and travel time beforehand beats panicking at unfamiliar exits in bad weather.

sec12-card-sec12-F33.question_text: How must an adult wear the belt, and how must a baby be secured rather than held in someone's arms?
sec12-card-sec12-F33.teaching_text: An infant seat or convertible seat in infant or toddler position protects fragile necks where human arms fail.

sec12-card-sec12-F34.question_text: Which household items must never replace a car safety seat, and why does legged baby clothing beat a sack sleeper?
sec12-card-sec12-F34.teaching_text: Crotch harness straps need separate pant legs to cinch snugly, and household carriers shatter in real crashes.

sec12-card-sec12-F35.question_text: What are the common infant car-seat installation errors, and how should a blanket be used in cold weather?
sec12-card-sec12-F35.teaching_text: Wrapping thick blankets underneath harness straps creates deadly slack, so buckle snug first or slot straps through.

sec12-card-sec12-R10.question_text: Which car-seat positions are proper for a baby, and which infant orientation is explicitly listed as wrong?
sec12-card-sec12-R10.teaching_text: Facing an infant forward exposes a baby's heavy head and fragile spine to catastrophic crash whip.

sec15-card-sec15-F18.question_text: What happens during a tire blowout, what usually causes it, and how often should you inspect tires?
sec15-card-sec15-F18.teaching_text: Neglected underinflation and tread damage cause most sudden tire collapses, making monthly pressure checks vital.

sec15-card-sec15-F19.question_text: Why keep off the brakes in a blowout, and how do you bring the car safely off the road?
sec15-card-sec15-F19.teaching_text: Braking on a collapsed tire yanks the car violently sideways, whereas coasting down slowly spares control and rims.

sec15-card-sec15-F20.question_text: How do you steer a lost wheel to a stop, what failure often accompanies it, and how does it leave?
sec15-card-sec15-F20.teaching_text: Sheared hubs often sever brake lines too, and once halted a three-wheeled car must be towed.

sec15-card-sec15-F21.question_text: Why is total brake failure rare on modern cars, and what two signs reveal partial failure?
sec15-card-sec15-F21.teaching_text: Modern service brakes retain partial stopping power while lighting a dash warning lamp when half fails.

sec15-card-sec15-F22.question_text: What four actions stop a vehicle safely if the service brakes fail completely?
sec15-card-sec15-F22.teaching_text: Pumping builds residual pressure while lower gears and smooth parking-brake tension slow you without locking rear wheels.

sec15-card-sec15-F23.question_text: When partial power-steering loss strikes, how must you respond at the wheel?
sec15-card-sec15-F23.teaching_text: Mechanical linkage still turns the front tires even when hydraulic or electric assist drops out.

sec15-card-sec15-F24.question_text: How should you bring the car to a halt if steering ever fails completely?
sec15-card-sec15-F24.teaching_text: Smooth braking brings the car down without violent weight transfer that could spin an unsteered chassis.

sec15-card-sec15-R01.question_text: Contrast your immediate right-foot action in a tire blowout versus complete brake failure?
sec15-card-sec15-R01.teaching_text: Touching brakes destabilizes a blown tire immediately, whereas rapid pumping tries to revive lost hydraulic pressure.

sec15-card-sec15-R12.question_text: How do brake impact and moving the vehicle afterward differ between a lost wheel and a blowout?
sec15-card-sec15-R12.teaching_text: A flat tire can roll slowly off traffic without rim ruin, whereas a missing wheel grounds the hub.

sec15-card-sec15-F09.question_text: Where on a congested freeway entrance lane should you slow or wait, and why not at the tip?
sec15-card-sec15-F09.teaching_text: Stopping at the very end of an on-ramp steals the runway needed to match highway speed.

sec15-card-sec15-F10.question_text: How do you merge from an open entrance lane when the freeway lane is clear versus occupied?
sec15-card-sec15-F10.teaching_text: Matching mainline pace early lets you glide straight in or ease smoothly behind passing cars.

sec15-card-sec15-F11.question_text: Which freeway lanes carry through traffic near the limit, and who belongs in the right lane?
sec15-card-sec15-F11.teaching_text: Keeping through cars center or left frees the right lane for slower climbers and ramp merges.

sec15-card-sec15-F12.question_text: What freeway habits on lane changes, stopping, slowing, and tailgating prevent multi-car pileups?
sec15-card-sec15-F12.teaching_text: High speeds turn one sudden stop or tailgate tap into a chain-reaction multi-vehicle crash.

sec15-card-sec15-F13.question_text: What three directional moves are strictly forbidden on a freeway, and how do you reverse direction?
sec15-card-sec15-F13.teaching_text: Use the next interchange to turn around instead of backing up or cutting across medians.

sec15-card-sec15-F14.question_text: Where do you stop in a freeway emergency, may you walk, and how do you help stranded drivers?
sec15-card-sec15-F14.teaching_text: Standing on shoulders or stopping twice doubles freeway crash targets; keep driving and alert authorities.

sec15-card-sec15-F15.question_text: When do you slow down for a freeway exit, and what must you do if you miss it?
sec15-card-sec15-F15.teaching_text: Decelerating only after entering the off-ramp keeps mainline traffic moving at full speed behind you.

sec15-card-sec15-R03.question_text: Pair the lawful fix for missing a freeway exit with needing the opposite freeway direction?
sec15-card-sec15-R03.teaching_text: Every legal freeway correction moves forward to the next ramp rather than reversing or crossing dividers.

sec15-card-sec15-R04.question_text: Compare how you handle a backed-up freeway entrance lane versus a wide-open one?
sec15-card-sec15-R04.teaching_text: Waiting near the ramp throat preserves acceleration room once a gap opens ahead.

sec15-card-sec15-R10.question_text: Contrast the role of left and center freeway lanes with the right-hand lane?
sec15-card-sec15-R10.teaching_text: Separating steady limit-speed cruisers from slower vehicles and ramp traffic smooths every interchange.

sec15-card-sec15-F31.question_text: What driving inputs trigger most skids, and how quickly must you respond when one starts?
sec15-card-sec15-F31.teaching_text: Abrupt steering or braking at speeds too fast for wet or gravel roads breaks tire grip.

sec15-card-sec15-F32.question_text: What should your feet do immediately when a skid or control loss begins?
sec15-card-sec15-F32.teaching_text: Stopping whatever pedal input broke traction often lets rolling tires regain grip on their own.

sec15-card-sec15-F33.question_text: Which direction and how firmly do you turn the steering wheel to recover from a rear-wheel skid?
sec15-card-sec15-F33.teaching_text: Turning smoothly toward the sliding tail realigns front and rear tracks without whipping into a counter-skid.

sec15-card-sec15-R02.question_text: Contrast steering out of a skid with recovering after wheels drop off the pavement edge?
sec15-card-sec15-R02.teaching_text: Skids need immediate steering toward the slide, whereas shoulder drop-offs require slowing straight before easing back.

sec15-card-sec15-F03.question_text: How do you cut low-sun glare, and which lights belong on during dim dawn or dusk?
sec15-card-sec15-F03.teaching_text: Streaked windshields scatter blinding sunbeams, while twilight shadows hide dark cars unless low beams shine.

sec15-card-sec15-F04.question_text: How do you prepare your eyes and glass before driving after dark?
sec15-card-sec15-F04.teaching_text: Hours of bright glare delay full night adaptation, and interior film halos oncoming headlights.

sec15-card-sec15-F05.question_text: What three rules govern vehicle lamps, safe speed, and high beams at night?
sec15-card-sec15-F05.teaching_text: Outrunning your headlamp reach means spotting dark hazards only after stopping distance has vanished.

sec15-card-sec15-F06.question_text: How do you handle glaring oncoming lights, and what do red lane reflectors warn?
sec15-card-sec15-F06.teaching_text: Tracking the right edge saves night vision, and glowing red pavement markers warn of wrong-way entry.

sec15-card-sec15-R05.question_text: Pair your headlamp rule at dawn or dusk with your response to blinding oncoming high beams?
sec15-card-sec15-R05.teaching_text: Low beams help others spot you at dusk, while one quick flash and right-edge gaze beat glare.

sec15-card-sec15-F25.question_text: Why must you never jerk the wheel back onto pavement after dropping onto the shoulder?
sec15-card-sec15-F25.teaching_text: Fighting the asphalt lip at speed slingshots your car sideways across oncoming lanes.

sec15-card-sec15-F26.question_text: How do you help a passing driver trapped by oncoming traffic once you read their move?
sec15-card-sec15-F26.teaching_text: Moving right onto the shoulder and either braking or accelerating opens whichever gap the passer picks.

sec15-card-sec15-F27.question_text: What warning and steering escape must you use—and never use—when an oncoming car fills your lane?
sec15-card-sec15-F27.teaching_text: Swerving left meets the other driver if they recover back into their own lane at the last instant.

sec15-card-sec15-R06.question_text: Compare avoiding a wrong-way car in your lane with helping a trapped overtaker beside you?
sec15-card-sec15-R06.teaching_text: Rightward escape opens survival space in both crises while speed adjustment clears the trapped passer.

sec15-card-sec15-F28.question_text: How does a stuck accelerator behave, and right after what driver action does it often stick?
sec15-card-sec15-F28.teaching_text: Linkage or floor-mat snags most often catch right after the gas pedal has been pressed flat.

sec15-card-sec15-F29.question_text: What pedal, ignition-key, and braking sequence stops a car with a stuck accelerator?
sec15-card-sec15-F29.teaching_text: Turning the key just far enough to kill spark stops power without locking the steering column.

sec15-card-sec15-F30.question_text: What two mechanical events usually kill power steering, and how do you stop safely?
sec15-card-sec15-F30.teaching_text: Engine stalls or snapped drive belts cut assist instantly, requiring firm arm strength to pull off.

sec15-card-sec15-R07.question_text: Contrast handling a stuck gas pedal with handling lost power-steering assist?
sec15-card-sec15-R07.teaching_text: Runaway throttle demands cutting engine power unlocked, whereas heavy steering simply needs slower muscled pull-off.

sec15-card-sec15-F34.question_text: What three vehicle problems start most car fires, and how should you treat any burning smell?
sec15-card-sec15-F34.teaching_text: Investigating acrid smoke or hot oil smells immediately catches under-hood fires before flames erupt.

sec15-card-sec15-F35.question_text: What must you shut off and where must passengers go immediately if vehicle fire is suspected?
sec15-card-sec15-F35.teaching_text: Cutting ignition and electrical switches starves fuel pumps and sparks while evacuating beats toxic cabin smoke.

sec15-card-sec15-F36.question_text: How do you smother a small vehicle fire, what liquid is forbidden, and how do you treat big fires?
sec15-card-sec15-F36.teaching_text: Water spreads burning gasoline and conducts electrical current; use extinguishers, dirt, or sand on small flames only.

sec15-card-sec15-F37.question_text: After a breakdown, where should the car and passengers wait depending on nearby safe ground?
sec15-card-sec15-F37.teaching_text: Passengers leave the car only when a safe off-road refuge is reachable; otherwise seatbelts inside beat shoulders.
sec15-card-sec15-F37.must_match_memory_hook: Clear road, safe ground or inside

visual_sync.text_span: Clear road, safe ground or inside

sec15-card-sec15-F38.question_text: What gear warns traffic after a breakdown, how do you greet strangers, and what signals distress?
sec15-card-sec15-F38.teaching_text: Staying locked inside while asking strangers to call police protects occupants as raised hoods signal help.

sec15-card-sec15-F39.question_text: How do walking rules after a breakdown on an ordinary highway differ from a freeway?
sec15-card-sec15-F39.teaching_text: Rural highway walkers stay far off pavement facing cars, whereas freeways forbid walking altogether.

sec15-card-sec15-R08.question_text: Contrast tackling a small vehicle fire with facing a large fuel fire or reaching for water?
sec15-card-sec15-R08.teaching_text: Dirt or chemical extinguishers tame tiny flare-ups, whereas roaring fuel fires demand distance and firefighters.

sec15-card-sec15-R09.question_text: How does waiting after a breakdown on a surface road compare with waiting on a freeway?
sec15-card-sec15-R09.teaching_text: High-speed freeway lanes and ramps make walking anywhere near the roadway fatal.

sec15-card-sec15-F16.question_text: What three vehicle controls enter every emergency, and what is your golden braking and steering rule?
sec15-card-sec15-F16.teaching_text: Panic brake-locking kills steering right when aiming toward open ground or bushes could save everyone.

sec15-card-sec15-F17.question_text: How do you apply maximum emergency braking, why wear your seatbelt, and when do you stop steering?
sec15-card-sec15-F17.teaching_text: Seatbelts hold you behind the wheel during violent swerves, and steering continues even past initial impact.

sec15-card-sec15-F01.question_text: Which three road spots freeze first or hide ice even when surrounding pavement looks clear?
sec15-card-sec15-F01.teaching_text: Cold air chills bridge decks from above and below while tree shade preserves slick glare ice.

sec15-card-sec15-F02.question_text: How should you use your brakes and steering on packed snow or ice?
sec15-card-sec15-F02.teaching_text: Light on-and-off pressure prevents wheel lockup, and open snowbanks beat sliding into solid traffic.

sec15-card-sec15-F07.question_text: What road design features make freeways safe at high speeds?
sec15-card-sec15-F07.teaching_text: Eliminating sharp curves, steep hills, traffic lights, rail crossings, and random driveways removes cross-traffic surprises.

sec15-card-sec15-F08.question_text: What route details and four vehicle items must you check before entering a freeway?
sec15-card-sec15-F08.teaching_text: Freeways carry no gas stations on the shoulder, making preventable fuel or coolant stalls needlessly perilous.

sec15-card-sec15-R11.question_text: How does manual threshold emergency braking relate to what antilock brakes do?
sec15-card-sec15-R11.teaching_text: Both techniques keep tires right at rolling grip by releasing pressure the instant a wheel locks.

sec16-card-sec16-F21.question_text: What driver error causes over two-thirds of collisions between cars and motorcycles?
sec16-card-sec16-F21.teaching_text: Exposed riders suffer severe crash trauma whenever a car turns left across an oncoming bike's lane.

sec16-card-sec16-F22.question_text: How does a motorcycle's narrow profile trick your eyes on distance and speed, and how should you look?
sec16-card-sec16-F22.teaching_text: Slim headlights mimic distant cars, and nimble riders slip into blind gaps unless you scan thrice.

sec16-card-sec16-F23.question_text: What two things must you actively confirm about any motorcycle before turning or entering an intersection?
sec16-card-sec16-F23.teaching_text: Glancing past a single headlamp without gauging closing speed triggers classic intersection turn-in crashes.

sec16-card-sec16-F27.question_text: Where do car-and-motorcycle crashes happen most often, and why?
sec16-card-sec16-F27.teaching_text: Busy cross-traffic clutter hides narrow bikes right when turning motorists commit across opposing lanes.

sec16-card-sec16-F28.question_text: Why shouldn't you trust a rider's lane shift or flashing turn signal until a turn clearly begins?
sec16-card-sec16-F28.teaching_text: Riders weave inside lanes around debris, and motorcycle turn signals often lack automatic self-canceling switches.

sec16-card-sec16-R10.question_text: Pair why riders face higher injury risk with the top cause behind over two-thirds of car-bike crashes?
sec16-card-sec16-R10.teaching_text: Zero steel cage plus turning motorists misjudging approach speed makes intersection lefts doubly dangerous.

sec16-card-sec16-R04.question_text: How do a motorcycle's small size and high agility create two opposite visual traps?
sec16-card-sec16-R04.teaching_text: Narrow width fools depth perception forward while quick handling lets bikes surface abruptly beside you.

sec16-card-sec16-R05.question_text: Contrast what a rider's lane shift or blinking lamp might mean with what actually proves a turn?
sec16-card-sec16-R05.teaching_text: Forgotten blinkers and pothole dodges look like turn setups until the bike genuinely leans into the corner.

sec16-card-sec16-F04.question_text: How does a truck or bus driver's forward view compare with side and immediate rear visibility?
sec16-card-sec16-F04.teaching_text: Tall seats overlook traffic ahead, yet sides rely strictly on mirrors and the tail stays completely invisible.

sec16-card-sec16-F05.question_text: What two physical dimensions must large-vehicle drivers account for when turning, shifting lanes, or backing?
sec16-card-sec16-F05.teaching_text: Long trailers track wide across corners and need far larger side gaps than passenger sedans.

sec16-card-sec16-F06.question_text: Where should car drivers position themselves near a large truck or bus, and why?
sec16-card-sec16-F06.teaching_text: Staying where the rig's driver sees you keeps your car clear of wide turns and blocked forward views.

sec16-card-sec16-F07.question_text: Why must you leave generous space before merging ahead of a large truck or crossing its path?
sec16-card-sec16-F07.teaching_text: Loaded trucks require far more pavement to halt than cars, turning tight cut-ins into rear-end crushes.

sec16-card-sec16-F08.question_text: How quickly do large vehicles accelerate and maneuver, and how does that affect passing them?
sec16-card-sec16-F08.teaching_text: Heavy rigs build speed sluggishly and often climb below posted limits, requiring patient sightline checks.

sec16-card-sec16-F09.question_text: How do large-truck drivers prevent downhill brake fade, and what should car drivers watch for?
sec16-card-sec16-F09.teaching_text: Continuous braking cooks heavy truck drums fast, so clear the lane immediately if a rig overtakes downhill.

sec16-card-sec16-F10.question_text: What aerodynamic force hits smaller cars approaching or passing fast-moving trucks and buses?
sec16-card-sec16-F10.teaching_text: Bow waves and trailer turbulence shove light cars toward shoulders unless hands stay ready to countersteer.

sec16-card-sec16-R01.question_text: Contrast what a big-rig driver sees ahead with what can be seen along the sides and tail?
sec16-card-sec16-R01.teaching_text: Tailgating right behind trailer doors hides your car completely from every cab window and mirror.

sec16-card-sec16-R07.question_text: Combine the four handling limits of large vehicles that demand extra following and passing space?
sec16-card-sec16-R07.teaching_text: Long braking, wide cornering, slow acceleration, and below-limit climbs require generous buffers front and back.

sec16-card-sec16-R08.question_text: Pair a large truck's steep-downgrade hazard with its high-speed passing hazard for small cars?
sec16-card-sec16-R08.teaching_text: Gravity threatens truck brakes on hills while displaced highway air buffets compact cars alongside.

sec16-card-sec16-F24.question_text: Which portion of a lane do motorcyclists often prefer, and why do they shift across it?
sec16-card-sec16-F24.teaching_text: Riding left opens sightlines and mirror visibility, while shifting center or right dodges traffic hazards.

sec16-card-sec16-F25.question_text: Why might a motorcyclist swerve abruptly inside their lane over surfaces a car barely feels?
sec16-card-sec16-F25.teaching_text: Potholes and angled rail tracks that four tires straddle easily can deflect a motorcycle's front wheel.

sec16-card-sec16-F26.question_text: Why is sharing a traffic lane side-by-side with a motorcycle forbidden?
sec16-card-sec16-F26.teaching_text: Squeezing alongside a rider steals the lateral escape space needed to dodge road debris or wind.

sec16-card-sec16-F29.question_text: What is the minimum following gap behind a motorcycle, and why add even more cushion?
sec16-card-sec16-F29.teaching_text: Judging a narrow bike's deceleration is tricky, and any rear-end tap throws an unprotected rider.

sec16-card-sec16-F30.question_text: When do both riders and motorists make more bad choices, raising motorcycle injury risk?
sec16-card-sec16-F30.teaching_text: Tailgating and short sightlines force rushed panic maneuvers around sudden road obstacles ahead.

sec16-card-sec16-F31.question_text: How should you drive while a motorcyclist is overtaking your car?
sec16-card-sec16-F31.teaching_text: Predictable speed and centered lane tracking let the passing rider clear your blind zone briskly.

sec16-card-sec16-F32.question_text: How much lane space do you give when passing a motorcycle, and why wait before returning?
sec16-card-sec16-F32.teaching_text: Cutting back in early crowds the front tire and forces the rider toward traffic or shoulders.

sec16-card-sec16-R06.question_text: Contrast your duty when a motorcycle passes you with your duty when passing a motorcycle?
sec16-card-sec16-R06.teaching_text: Holding steady helps an overtaking rider finish fast, while using a full lane protects an overtaken rider.

sec16-card-sec16-R09.question_text: Distinguish the baseline time gap behind a motorcycle from the recommended cushion?
sec16-card-sec16-R09.teaching_text: Expanding beyond two seconds offsets how hard single-taillight braking is to read.

sec16-card-sec16-F14.question_text: What mirror equipment is required when a towed trailer blocks your inside rearview mirror?
sec16-card-sec16-F14.teaching_text: Dual side mirrors restore rear lane sightlines hidden behind a wide box or boat hull.

sec16-card-sec16-F15.question_text: Which two weight thresholds require a loaded trailer to carry independent brakes and breakaway protection?
sec16-card-sec16-F15.teaching_text: Heavy unbraked trailers overpower car rotors and run wild if a coupling ever separates.

sec16-card-sec16-F16.question_text: What rules govern passengers riding inside utility trailers versus house trailers?
sec16-card-sec16-F16.teaching_text: Unbelted riders inside towed boxes have zero crash protection, and house-trailer occupancy breaks Hawaii law.

sec16-card-sec16-F17.question_text: Where must trailer safety chains attach, and where must they never attach?
sec16-card-sec16-F17.teaching_text: Chains hooked onto a detachable hitch drop right onto the road if the hitch assembly snaps off.

sec16-card-sec16-F18.question_text: How should a trailer hitch match the load, and which type of hitch should never be trusted?
sec16-card-sec16-F18.teaching_text: Decorative car bumpers twist or tear loose under tongue loads and highway bounce.

sec16-card-sec16-F19.question_text: What percentage of trailer weight belongs on the hitch, and what goes wrong above or below it?
sec16-card-sec16-F19.teaching_text: Excess tongue weight unloads front steering tires, whereas tail-heavy trailers whip into violent fishtails.

sec16-card-sec16-F20.question_text: What cargo, wheel, fender, tire, and lighting equipment must a road-legal trailer have?
sec16-card-sec16-F20.teaching_text: Fenders tame road spray while working tail, stop, turn, and plate lights alert trailing traffic.

sec16-card-sec16-R02.question_text: Compare which trailers require independent brakes with which trailers require frame-attached safety chains?
sec16-card-sec16-R02.teaching_text: Brakes kick in past half tow weight or 3,000 pounds, while every single trailer needs frame chains.

sec16-card-sec16-R03.question_text: Contrast the handling symptom of too much hitch weight against too little hitch weight?
sec16-card-sec16-R03.teaching_text: Keeping ten to fifteen percent on the ball preserves both crisp front steering and straight trailer tracking.

sec16-card-sec16-R11.question_text: Pair the equipment rule for vision-blocking trailers with the passenger ban for house trailers?
sec16-card-sec16-R11.teaching_text: Safe towing requires seeing down both flanks while keeping every passenger belted inside the tow car.

sec16-card-sec16-F01.question_text: What do trucks, tractor-trailers, and buses demand from their own drivers and from surrounding motorists?
sec16-card-sec16-F01.teaching_text: Safe highways depend on commercial skill inside the cab plus everyday motorists respecting big-rig physics.

sec16-card-sec16-F02.question_text: What licensing and conduct standard applies to professional drivers of large vehicles?
sec16-card-sec16-F02.teaching_text: Full-time commercial drivers spend far more hours exposed to traffic hazards and must model safe habits.

sec16-card-sec16-F03.question_text: Why must large-vehicle drivers stay constantly mindful of vehicle limits, road users, and cargo?
sec16-card-sec16-F03.teaching_text: Multi-ton momentum turns minor miscalculations into devastating damage for smaller cars and passengers.

sec16-card-sec16-F11.question_text: What packaging, labeling, and exterior truck markings must hazmat drivers verify, and why?
sec16-card-sec16-F11.teaching_text: Clear exterior placards tell firefighters immediately whether cargo is explosive, flammable, toxic, or radioactive.

sec16-card-sec16-F12.question_text: Which four emergency items must most large vehicles carry and their drivers know how to use?
sec16-card-sec16-F12.teaching_text: Trained crews deploy roadside warning triangles and extinguishers fast to contain highway emergencies.

sec16-card-sec16-F13.question_text: How does hitching a trailer—especially a large one—change an ordinary car or pickup?
sec16-card-sec16-F13.teaching_text: Added length and weight slow acceleration, stretch braking distances, and widen turn arcs just like trucks.

sec16-card-sec16-R12.question_text: Contrast when exterior hazmat markings are required with when emergency safety kits are carried?
sec16-card-sec16-R12.teaching_text: Hazard signs depend on dangerous freight inside, whereas flares and extinguishers ride aboard most big rigs.

sec16-card-sec16-F33.question_text: What testing, registration, and insurance standards apply to motorcycles?
sec16-card-sec16-F33.teaching_text: Two-wheel balance demands dedicated knowledge and skill tests alongside full motor-vehicle registration and coverage.

sec16-card-sec16-F34.question_text: How should motorists view and treat motorcycles in everyday traffic?
sec16-card-sec16-F34.teaching_text: Expecting quick rider adjustments and sharing road space courteously keeps vulnerable neighbors alive.

sec17-card-sec17-F15.question_text: Which lanes must stop for a school bus flashing alternating red lamps, and what fine can apply?
sec17-card-sec17-F15.teaching_text: Passing flashing red bus lights risks children crossing multiple lanes and triggers a steep thousand-dollar penalty.

sec17-card-sec17-F16.question_text: When are oncoming drivers exempt from stopping for a school bus, and what defines that road?
sec17-card-sec17-F16.teaching_text: An unpaved strip or physical median separating two roadways shields oncoming lanes from crossing students.

sec17-card-sec17-F17.question_text: What roadside clue warns that a school bus is nearby, and why slow down immediately?
sec17-card-sec17-F17.teaching_text: Excited children gathered along morning curbs often chase dropped items or rush across lanes toward buses.

sec17-card-sec17-R01.question_text: Contrast who must stop for school-bus flashing red lights with the sole oncoming exemption?
sec17-card-sec17-R01.teaching_text: Undivided multi-lane roads stop every lane both ways, whereas physical medians exempt opposing traffic.

sec17-card-sec17-F05.question_text: What speed readiness and audible warning does Hawaii law require when pedestrians are on or near the road?
sec17-card-sec17-F05.teaching_text: Easing off the gas while tapping a timely horn alerts distracted walkers before paths cross.

sec17-card-sec17-F06.question_text: How do you identify a blind pedestrian, and how do traffic signals affect your duty to stop?
sec17-card-sec17-F06.teaching_text: Hawaii law mandates a complete stop for white canes or guide dogs regardless of green lights.

sec17-card-sec17-F07.question_text: What two driver moves are prohibited around pedestrian safety zones and cars stopped for walkers?
sec17-card-sec17-F07.teaching_text: Overtaking a car halted at a crosswalk strikes the hidden pedestrian stepping out across its hood.

sec17-card-sec17-F08.question_text: Where must you scan hardest for children and walkers, and whose hand signal requires a stop?
sec17-card-sec17-F08.teaching_text: Crossing guards hold legal stop authority, and intersection turns or driveway crossings cross active sidewalks.

sec17-card-sec17-F09.question_text: What check and which side of the car should you and passengers use when getting out?
sec17-card-sec17-F09.teaching_text: Stepping onto the sidewalk side keeps passengers and open doors clear of passing fenders and bikes.

sec17-card-sec17-R02.question_text: Compare your legal duty toward a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog versus other walkers?
sec17-card-sec17-R02.teaching_text: Visually impaired walkers get unconditional full stops regardless of lights, while others get caution and horn warnings.

sec17-card-sec17-R11.question_text: Name the two prohibited driver acts around pedestrians alongside the one required warning?
sec17-card-sec17-R11.teaching_text: Staying out of safety zones, holding behind stopped cars, and sounding needed horn warnings saves walkers.

sec17-card-sec17-F21.question_text: What minimum side gap applies when passing a bicycle, and what right-turn crash must you avoid?
sec17-card-sec17-F21.teaching_text: Bicycles roll faster than drivers guess, so overtaking and immediately cutting right hooks straight across them.

sec17-card-sec17-F22.question_text: How must drivers treat bike lanes and overtaking cyclists when preparing to turn right?
sec17-card-sec17-F22.teaching_text: Driving inside bike lanes or passing a rider right before turning right sets up an intersection collision.

sec17-card-sec17-F23.question_text: Why must you check behind before swinging open a parked car door?
sec17-card-sec17-F23.teaching_text: Throwing a door into an approaching cyclist's path causes severe crashes and is a citable offense.

sec17-card-sec17-F20.question_text: What share of car-bicycle crashes comes from illegal wrong-way riding, and when must drivers watch for it?
sec17-card-sec17-F20.teaching_text: Turning motorists scan left for cars and easily miss a wrong-way cyclist rolling off the right.

sec17-card-sec17-F18.question_text: What legal status do bicycles hold in Hawaii, and why must motorists stay extra alert around them?
sec17-card-sec17-F18.teaching_text: Riders hold full vehicle rights and duties yet vary widely in skill and visibility.

sec17-card-sec17-F19.question_text: Where do bicycles normally ride, when may they move into the lane, and what changes on one-way streets?
sec17-card-sec17-F19.teaching_text: Left turns, passing slower bikes, edge debris, and one-way left curbs all justify leaving the right edge.

sec17-card-sec17-R03.question_text: Pair a driver's minimum clearance when passing a cyclist with the legal rule on opening car doors?
sec17-card-sec17-R03.teaching_text: Both rules protect cyclists inside the narrow corridor between moving fenders and curb-parked doors.

sec17-card-sec17-R07.question_text: Contrast the major bicycle-crash error committed by riders with the classic crash committed by drivers?
sec17-card-sec17-R07.teaching_text: Eliminating salmon-riding against traffic and pass-then-turn right hooks prevents huge shares of bike collisions.

sec17-card-sec17-F10.question_text: Where must pedestrians cross legally, and why keep watching cars even inside painted lines?
sec17-card-sec17-F10.teaching_text: Jaywalking breaks Hawaii law, and white stripes or walk signals cannot physically stop a distracted driver.

sec17-card-sec17-F11.question_text: What should a pedestrian do when arriving at a green signal that has already been lit awhile?
sec17-card-sec17-F11.teaching_text: Stepping off late in a green phase risks getting stranded mid-street when cross traffic gets green.

sec17-card-sec17-F12.question_text: When does Hawaii law forbid a pedestrian from stepping into a street or crosswalk?
sec17-card-sec17-F12.teaching_text: Heavy vehicles cannot halt on a dime, and running across streets or ignoring turners invites tragedy.

sec17-card-sec17-F13.question_text: Which side do you walk on where no sidewalk exists, and what clothing, sobriety, and child rules apply?
sec17-card-sec17-F13.teaching_text: Facing oncoming headlights in bright clothes while sober lets you see and dodge drifting cars.

sec17-card-sec17-F14.question_text: What soliciting and parking-space behaviors on the traveled roadway are illegal for pedestrians?
sec17-card-sec17-F14.teaching_text: Standing in live asphalt to flag rides, panhandle, or reserve parking stalls puts bodies in traffic.

sec17-card-sec17-R06.question_text: Combine where pedestrians must legally cross with how to treat an aging green light?
sec17-card-sec17-R06.teaching_text: Crossing at marked corners on a newly turned green gives full walking time across every lane.

sec17-card-sec17-R09.question_text: Contrast which side of a road a pedestrian uses with which side a bicyclist rides on?
sec17-card-sec17-R09.teaching_text: Foot travelers step aside facing traffic on the left, while wheeled vehicles flow right with cars.

sec17-card-sec17-F25.question_text: Which traffic laws bind bicyclists, and why ride with traffic even for half a block?
sec17-card-sec17-F25.teaching_text: Drivers pulling from driveways scan left and never expect fast bikes coming wrong-way off the right.

sec17-card-sec17-F26.question_text: While watching left for a gap to turn right, whom do drivers and cyclists alike forget?
sec17-card-sec17-F26.teaching_text: Staring left for oncoming cars blinds right-turners to pedestrians stepping off the right-hand curb.

sec17-card-sec17-F27.question_text: List the four situations when a slower bicyclist may legally leave the right edge and take the lane?
sec17-card-sec17-F27.teaching_text: Centering in a lane too narrow to share stops cars from squeezing past with unsafe inches.

sec17-card-sec17-F28.question_text: When must cyclists ride single file versus two abreast, and what penalties apply to bike violations?
sec17-card-sec17-F28.teaching_text: Roadways require single file while wide unobstructed bike paths allow pairs, and traffic tickets match drivers.

sec17-card-sec17-F29.question_text: What rules govern right-turn-only lanes, required night bike gear, and carrying extra bike passengers?
sec17-card-sec17-F29.teaching_text: Straight-bound bikes leave turn-only pockets, carry front lights plus rear reflectors, and skip unequipped passengers.

sec17-card-sec17-F30.question_text: Where is sidewalk bicycling banned in Hawaii, and what speed and yield rules apply elsewhere?
sec17-card-sec17-F30.teaching_text: Storefront doors make business sidewalks unsafe, and permitted sidewalks cap bikes at 10 mph behind walkers.

sec17-card-sec17-R04.question_text: Compare which edge a bicycle uses on a standard two-way street versus a one-way street?
sec17-card-sec17-R04.teaching_text: One-way streets eliminate opposing traffic on the left curb, making left-edge riding useful for left turns.

sec17-card-sec17-R05.question_text: Contrast Hawaii's sidewalk-riding ban in business districts with residential sidewalk rules?
sec17-card-sec17-R05.teaching_text: Pedestrians always own sidewalks, and staying at or below ten miles per hour prevents surprise collisions.

sec17-card-sec17-R12.question_text: Distinguish mandatory night bicycle lighting from additional gear the manual recommends?
sec17-card-sec17-R12.teaching_text: Hawaii law mandates a front white lamp and rear reflector, while active rear lights boost visibility further.

sec17-card-sec17-F01.question_text: What share of Hawaii traffic fatalities are pedestrians, and which age groups make up nearly half?
sec17-card-sec17-F01.teaching_text: Nearly half of pedestrians killed on island roads are non-drivers under fifteen or over sixty-five.

sec17-card-sec17-F02.question_text: Where do almost 90 percent of fatal pedestrian crashes happen, and what are most victims doing?
sec17-card-sec17-F02.teaching_text: Stepping across live vehicle lanes accounts for over half of fatal pedestrian impacts statewide.

sec17-card-sec17-F03.question_text: Why does pedestrian survival inside the roadway depend on both walker and driver?
sec17-card-sec17-F03.teaching_text: Human bodies carry zero crash protection inside a space built for multi-ton motor vehicles.

sec17-card-sec17-F04.question_text: Why are young children and older adults vulnerable to pedestrian crashes for very different reasons?
sec17-card-sec17-F04.teaching_text: Children dart impulsively without grasping vehicle force, whereas seniors face slower vision, reflexes, and fragile bones.
sec17-card-sec17-F04.must_match_memory_hook: Kids misjudge danger, elders move slower

visual_sync.text_span: Kids misjudge danger, elders move slower

sec17-card-sec17-R08.question_text: Pair pedestrians' overall share of Hawaii traffic deaths with the age split inside pedestrian fatalities?
sec17-card-sec17-R08.teaching_text: Knowing that one in five road deaths is a walker sharpens alertness near schools and senior centers.

sec17-card-sec17-F31.question_text: Why wear a bike helmet on short slow rides, and why avoid weaving between parked cars?
sec17-card-sec17-F31.teaching_text: Low-speed curb falls fracture skulls easily, and weaving in and out of parked cars ambushes overtaking drivers.

sec17-card-sec17-F32.question_text: What look, hand-signal, and parked-car clearance habits protect a bicyclist?
sec17-card-sec17-F32.teaching_text: Staying three feet outside parked cars clears swinging doors while shoulder checks spot overtaking traffic.

sec17-card-sec17-F33.question_text: Why skip headphones on a bicycle, and what pre-ride mechanical check comes before rolling?
sec17-card-sec17-F33.teaching_text: Open ears catch approaching engines early while firm brakes, tight bars, and full tires prevent spills.

sec17-card-sec17-F34.question_text: Why isn't simple eye contact with a driver enough for a cyclist, and what confirms recognition?
sec17-card-sec17-F34.teaching_text: Drivers can stare straight through a narrow cyclist without registering them until they wave or nod back.

sec17-card-sec17-F35.question_text: Describe the two lawful ways a bicyclist can execute an intersection left turn?
sec17-card-sec17-F35.teaching_text: Experienced riders merge to the center lane, while busy intersections allow dismounting to walk the crosswalk.

sec17-card-sec17-F36.question_text: Why shouldn't a bicyclist squeeze past cars on the right, and what is safer in stopped traffic?
sec17-card-sec17-F36.teaching_text: Drivers rarely check right curb cracks for bikes, making waiting in line safer and more courteous.

sec17-card-sec17-F24.question_text: What three everyday benefits does the Hawaii manual give for treating bicyclists with aloha?
sec17-card-sec17-F24.teaching_text: Every person pedaling takes a car off island roads, cuts exhaust, and leaves another open stall.

sec17-card-sec17-R10.question_text: Contrast a cyclist's vehicular left turn with a pedestrian-style left turn?
sec17-card-sec17-R10.teaching_text: Picking between lane-positioning and walking the crosswalk lets riders match intersection speed and comfort.

sec02-card-sec02-F19.question_text: Where can you renew a Hawaii driver's license, and how early before expiration may you do it?
sec02-card-sec02-F19.teaching_text: Renewing up to half a year ahead prevents last-week appointment crunches before your birthday.

sec02-card-sec02-F20.question_text: Does Hawaii give a grace period to keep driving after your driver's license passes its expiration date?
sec02-card-sec02-F20.teaching_text: Even though you can still renew an expired card for a year, driving on it a single day past expiration is illegal.

sec02-card-sec02-F21.question_text: How long after expiration may you still renew a Hawaii license before having to start over from scratch?
sec02-card-sec02-F21.teaching_text: Letting an expired card sit past twelve months wipes out simple renewal and forces full original-license testing.

sec02-card-sec02-F22.question_text: What screening is required before license renewal, and how often may you renew by mail?
sec02-card-sec02-F22.teaching_text: Alternating one mail cycle with an examiner visit ensures eyesight and driver records stay verified regularly.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.question_text: Contrast the early and late license renewal windows with your legal right to drive once the card expires?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.teaching_text: Test makers love trapping people who confuse the one-year renewal window with a one-year grace period to drive.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.question_text: Compare how often a vision test is needed at renewal with how often an in-person counter appearance is needed?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.teaching_text: Mail renewal skips only the counter line once between visits, never the eyesight standard.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.question_text: From 11 p.m. through 5 a.m., when may a provisional license holder legally drive?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.teaching_text: Late-night solo exemptions cover only direct job or school-authorized trips, never casual food runs.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.question_text: During the eleven-to-five overnight hours, how many riders under eighteen may a provisional driver carry without a parent aboard?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.teaching_text: Only a parent or guardian riding inside lifts the strict single-minor cap during high-risk overnight hours.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.question_text: What safety-belt or child-restraint rule applies whenever a provisional driver is behind the wheel?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.teaching_text: Full cabin restraint compliance is a strict condition of keeping a provisional license.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.question_text: How long must you hold your provisional license before applying for a full driver's license?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.teaching_text: Cleanly completing six months of restricted driving proves readiness for full Class 3 privileges.

sec02-card-sec02-R10.question_text: How do work and school exceptions interact with the overnight minor-passenger limit for provisional drivers?
sec02-card-sec02-R10.teaching_text: Driving home from a night job excuses being out late, yet only a parent aboard lets you carry multiple minors.

sec02-card-sec02-F23.question_text: Under what three card conditions can you apply for a duplicate license, and what must accompany the request?
sec02-card-sec02-F23.teaching_text: Bringing proper identification stops identity thieves from requesting a replacement card under your name.

sec02-card-sec02-F24.question_text: How and within how many days must you report a residence move on your license, including extra REAL ID proof?
sec02-card-sec02-F24.teaching_text: Missing the thirty-day written notice leaves renewal and court mail going to an old house, while REAL ID needs two address proofs.

sec02-card-sec02-F25.question_text: How and within what deadline must you report a legal name change for your driver's license?
sec02-card-sec02-F25.teaching_text: Name updates alter your core legal identity and signature, requiring face-to-face verification of official proof.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.question_text: Both share a thirty-day deadline, so how does reporting a license address change differ from reporting a name change?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.teaching_text: DMV questions love testing that mail works for moves whereas a name change always requires walking into the office.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.question_text: Who must bring you to the performance test, and what paperwork and condition must your test vehicle have?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.teaching_text: Showing up solo on a permit or with an expired safety sticker or dead brake bulb cancels your road test before it starts.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.question_text: What three things are strictly off-limits during your Hawaii driver performance test?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.teaching_text: Examiners test straightforward legal driving with only you and the scorer inside the cabin.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.question_text: How does Hawaii treat autocycles for driving on a Category 3 license versus taking the Category 3 road test?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.teaching_text: Three-wheeled autocycles handle differently from standard cars, so examiners require a regular Category 3 vehicle on test day.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.question_text: Which cars, trucks, and buses are covered by the Category 3 driving test?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.teaching_text: Staying at or under eighteen thousand pounds and fifteen occupants separates standard non-commercial vehicles from heavier tiers.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.question_text: Which driving zones and specific vehicle-control maneuvers are graded on the Category 3 road test?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.teaching_text: Rolling backward when starting on an incline or skipping signals downtown costs crucial performance points.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.question_text: State both halves of Hawaii's Category 3 rule for operating versus road-testing an autocycle?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.teaching_text: Remembering that you earn Category 3 in a car first before hopping into an autocycle beats a classic trick question.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.question_text: Which two-wheeled or three-wheeled vehicles fall under Hawaii Class 1 versus Class 2?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.teaching_text: Motor scooters group with motorcycles under Class 2, leaving low-power mopeds in Class 1.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.question_text: What weight rating, passenger count, and three-wheeled vehicle type are covered by a Hawaii Class 3 license?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.teaching_text: Note that the fifteen-person ceiling counts the driver too, not fifteen passengers plus one driver.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.question_text: What exact gross vehicle weight rating band requires a Hawaii Class 4 license?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.teaching_text: Medium-duty single trucks bridge the gap between everyday Class 3 pickups and full commercial CDL territory.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.question_text: What combined weight rating and towed-unit weight trigger a Commercial Class A license?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.teaching_text: Pulling towed units over ten thousand pounds inside a heavy combination demands top-tier articulated rig training.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.question_text: Which heavy single vehicles and trailer limits belong to Commercial Class B?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.teaching_text: Keeping any towed unit at ten thousand pounds or less keeps a heavy straight truck or bus inside Class B.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.question_text: When does a smaller vehicle outside Class A and B still require a Commercial Class C license?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.teaching_text: High passenger counts or dangerous placarded cargo trigger commercial standards even below heavy truck weights.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.question_text: What specialized cargo or vehicles match commercial endorsement letters H, T, P, N, X, and S?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.teaching_text: Notice X combines tank and placarded hazmat together while S adds dedicated checks beyond P for school buses.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.question_text: Where do the gross vehicle weight cutoffs sit between Class 3, Class 4, and commercial classes?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.teaching_text: One single pound above eighteen thousand or twenty-six thousand bumps a truck into the next license tier.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.question_text: What ten-thousand-pound trailer rule separates Commercial Class A from Commercial Class B?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.teaching_text: Focusing on whether the towed unit crosses ten thousand pounds solves every Class A versus Class B question instantly.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.question_text: Distinguish commercial endorsements P, S, and T from one another?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.teaching_text: Pairing P for sixteen-plus riders, S for school buses, and T for double or triple trailers avoids letter mix-ups.
sec02-card-sec02-R06.must_match_memory_hook: P passengers, S school, T trailers

visual_sync.text_span: P passengers, S school, T trailers

sec02-card-sec02-F38.question_text: When must you carry your valid driver's license, and what must you do if a police officer asks for it?
sec02-card-sec02-F38.teaching_text: Leaving your wallet at home counts as driving without a card on mopeds and cars alike.

sec02-card-sec02-F39.question_text: What are the two categories of written Hawaii traffic citations, and how is the less serious one treated?
sec02-card-sec02-F39.teaching_text: Civil infractions carry fines and license or registration stoppers, whereas serious traffic crimes trigger criminal prosecution.

sec02-card-sec02-F40.question_text: What response options settle a civil traffic infraction compared with a traffic crime citation?
sec02-card-sec02-F40.teaching_text: Potential jail time on a traffic crime eliminates mail-in payment and makes a personal court date mandatory.

sec02-card-sec02-F31.question_text: Where does Hawaii check every original or renewal applicant's record, and what blocks issuance?
sec02-card-sec02-F31.teaching_text: An active suspension or revocation in any state or Washington, D.C. stops Hawaii from issuing or renewing your card.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.question_text: Why can you settle a traffic infraction by mail or payment while a traffic crime forces a court visit?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.teaching_text: Civil infractions carry monetary or administrative penalties, whereas potential jail requires appearing before a judge.

sec02-card-sec02-F26.question_text: Do major surgery, amputation, illness, slower reflexes, or vision trouble automatically end your Hawaii driving privilege?
sec02-card-sec02-F26.teaching_text: Tailored restrictions allow drivers with reduced physical capability to keep operating safely within appropriate traffic limits.

sec02-card-sec02-F27.question_text: What medical input and functional tests help the licensing office tailor a restricted license?
sec02-card-sec02-F27.teaching_text: Matching actual road skills and doctor evaluations keeps restrictions practical rather than overly broad.

sec02-card-sec02-F28.question_text: Under what sole medical finding does Hawaii withdraw a driver's license altogether?
sec02-card-sec02-F28.teaching_text: Licenses stay active, with or without printed conditions, unless no safe driving situation remains possible.
